articles.title: Russian warship sinks off Libya as suspected Ukrainian strikes take war beyond Black Sea
articles.summary:
A Russian warship capsized and sank Sunday after suspected Ukrainian sea drones struck a naval base in eastern Libya, triggering an explosion and fire, according to Libyan officials.

Hours later, a second drone attack also hit a commercial ship off the coast of Benghazi, Reuters reported.

The first ship, the Russian navy corvette Merkury, was docked at Benghazi Naval Base when two explosive-laden sea drones struck the vessel, according to Libyan military officials who spoke to The Associated Press.

UKRAINE POUNDS BLACK SEA FLEET’S ‘LAST MAJOR STRONGHOLD’ WHILE PUTIN FLEXES NAVAL POWER IN PACIFIC

At least four other drones were intercepted and destroyed, the officials said.

Satellite images showed most of the warship capsized and submerged, with only its bow remaining above water. Smoke could be seen rising from the ship's superstructure, and debris was scattered along the pier.

Ten people, including Russian and Libyan nationals, suffered minor injuries in the attack and were receiving treatment in Benghazi, medical sources told Reuters.

The warship had stopped at the port to refuel and resupply while returning to Russia under a maritime cooperation agreement with Libya's eastern-based government, officials said in a statement.

Libyan military officials said an initial investigation indicated that Ukrainian sea drones had been launched from a base in western Libya, according to The AP.

UKRAINE STRIKES DEEP INTO RUSSIA’S ARCTIC GAS HEARTLAND AS TRUMP PUSHES PUTIN TOWARD PEACE

Hours after the warship was struck, a Maltese-flagged commercial ship was also hit by a sea drone off Benghazi, two Libyan military sources told Reuters.

Libyan naval forces rescued the commercial ship's crew, while health officials reported that some crew members sustained minor injuries and were in stable condition.

Libyan naval and air forces also intercepted more than 20 drone boats off Benghazi on Sunday evening, the military sources told Reuters.

The attacks prompted Libya's eastern-based government to seek an international investigation.

Prime Minister Osama Hamad said his government had submitted a formal request to the United Nations General Assembly and Security Council to investigate the attacks, including suspicions that the drones were launched from western Libya.

RUSSIA DEPLOYS NORTH KOREAN MISSILE UNIT TO UKRAINE; MOSCOW-PYONGYANG AXIS DEEPENS: REPORT

Hamad also called for an investigation into the possible presence of Ukrainian military experts in Libya and requested an explanation from Kyiv about their activities.

The eastern government insisted that Libya was not a party to the war between Russia and Ukraine and condemned attempts to use its territory to settle foreign conflicts.

"The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts," the government said.

Benghazi is controlled by forces loyal to Gen. Khalifa Haftar, whose self-styled Libyan National Army dominates eastern and southern Libya and maintains close ties with Russia.

Libya has been divided since the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled longtime dictator Moammar Gadhafi.

UKRAINE UNLEASHES MORE THAN 400 DRONES NEAR MOSCOW IN ONE OF WAR'S BIGGEST ATTACKS

A U. N. recognized government operates from Tripoli, while a rival administration controls much of the east.

The suspected attacks also come as Ukraine has expanded its campaign against Russian naval assets beyond the Black Sea. In December 2025, Ukraine said it struck a Russian-linked oil tanker with aerial drones in the Mediterranean Sea.

In March 2026, Russia accused Ukraine of attacking a Russian liquefied natural gas tanker with naval drones launched from the Libyan coast.

Libyan officials previously told the AP that Ukrainian drone specialists had been operating from military facilities in western Libya, including an air base in Misrata and sites in Tripoli and Zawiya.

Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Ukrainian forces have used explosive-laden sea drones and missiles to strike Russian warships and naval installations, primarily in the Black Sea.

articles.title: Trump says Iran unleashed missile, drone surge after midterms
articles.summary:
President Donald Trump said Sunday that Iran has launched more missiles and drones over the past week than at any point in more than a year, adding that U. S. forces shot them down without any damage and as tensions escalate following the U.S. midterm elections.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump also tied the surge in Iranian attacks to the Nov. 3 midterm elections, when Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress amid voter frustration over the war with Iran and rising fuel costs.

"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

TRUMP RESPONDS AFTER VANCE BLAMES IRAN WAR FOR MIDTERM LOSSES, VP SAYS HIS JOB IS TO SUPPORT PRESIDENT

"One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran, which has killed 81,000 protestors as of today, will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred. "

Trump also said that Iran launched "more drones and missiles over the past week than at any time for over a year," though he said U.S. defenses neutralized the threat.

"Don't worry, they've all been knocked down, and done no damage," Trump said.

"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won't let that happen!" he added.

The remarks also came days after the Senate rejected a war powers resolution in a 48-51 vote on Nov. 19, leaving Trump's military authority intact.

TRUMP WARNS OF NEW STRIKES AGAINST IRAN AFTER NEW YEAR, CALLS NEGOTIATORS ‘PROFESSIONAL TAP DANCERS’

Speaking to Fox News earlier Sunday, Trump said he is inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the new year if diplomatic talks fail to produce a deal, warning that Iranian vessels testing the U.S. naval blockade would end up "at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy."

In his social media post Sunday, Trump accused both Democrats and Iran of trying to keep fuel prices high ahead of the midterm elections and separately questioned the integrity of the vote without providing evidence.

"Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," Trump wrote, adding that it was too bad voters "didn't understand this before they pulled the trigger."

"The whole Election was very 'strange,'" he said. "In the end, America will win! "

articles.title: Trump dares Iran to breach US port blockade as Tehran reportedly readies 14 oil tankers
articles.summary:
Reports that Iran plans to send more than a dozen tankers through the U.S. blockade of its ports raised fears of a wider conflict Sunday, as a maritime security expert warned of a risky confrontation and President Donald Trump dared Tehran to test American forces deployed across the Gulf.

"I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy," Trump told Fox News chief foreign correspondent Trey Yingst when asked whether Iran would attempt to breach the blockade, first imposed in April.

The warning came as reports indicated Iran was preparing a convoy of tankers to breach the blockade from Kharg Island, a critical oil export hub.

TRUMP DETAILS SWEEPING 'ALL OR NOTHING' BLOCKADE OF STRAIT OF HORMUZ AFTER FAILED IRAN TALKS

Maritime security experts warned the vessels could face U.S. naval forces right across the Indian Ocean, while the Institute for the Study of War cautioned that an attempted breakout could perhaps trigger a wider war.

The reported operation would involve tankers sailing from Kharg Island, which handles most of Iran's crude oil exports, toward the Gulf of Oman and with crews reportedly assigned to the vessels and Iranian flags raised ahead of a possible attempt to breach the blockade.

Charlie Brown, a senior adviser to United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI) and maritime sanctions enforcement expert, dismissed the reported operation as "propaganda" and said the plan was unlikely to succeed if ever attempted.

"This supposed plan by the Iranians to suddenly deploy 14 vessels to try to breach the blockade in a convoy — it's farcical," Brown told Fox News Digital on Sunday.

"The blockade is enforced not merely as a line that is crossed, but the ability of the United States Navy to enforce this blockade extends across the entire Indian Ocean and beyond."

BLOCKADE 101: AMERICAN SEA POWER ON DISPLAY AS TRUMP CORNERS IRAN AND WARNS OFF CHINA

"If ships try to get out of the area that is managed by the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet, the U.S. Navy's 7th Fleet is the next area command that has responsibility over the Indian Ocean," he said.

"And they have ships and aircraft that are there right now, and they'll just take up the mission."

The potential confrontation comes amid rising maritime tensions. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported Sunday that a tanker was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman but did not identify the vessel or connect it to the reported Iranian convoy.

"UKMTO has received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman," the agency said in an advisory.

"Vessels are advised to consider the latest maritime security information and maintain awareness of the evolving operational environment."

The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) also warned Iran could attempt to break the blockade within days as mounting economic pressure leaves Tehran with few options.

"Iran's deteriorating economic situation is increasingly dire, which is forcing Iranian officials to reckon with the necessity of breaking the US blockade," the institute said in an update.

The assessment followed a Nov. 20 report by Hamshahri, a Tehran municipality-affiliated outlet, claiming Iran had positioned 14 tankers at Kharg Island to breach the blockade.

TRUMP BLOCKADE SQUEEZING IRAN SO HARD REGIME MAY BE DUMPING OIL INTO GULF, EXPERTS SAY

"Attempting to run the blockade would expose Iran to significant risk that ranges from the destruction of a tanker fleet at minimum to possibly resuming a larger-scale conflict with the United States, or both," the institute said.

"Iran's willingness to accept these risks demonstrates the degree to which the regime views the current economic situation as both dire and unsustainable."

Brown, however, questioned whether Tehran would send the tankers, suggesting the reported operation was an attempt to project defiance rather than a viable strategy.

"This supposed run of the blockade by several Iranian ships that's discussed is most likely propaganda — another one of a series of similar propaganda statements that don't turn out to be true and are easily debunked," he said.

Brown also disputed reports that the tankers were loaded and preparing to depart, citing satellite monitoring of Kharg Island.

"We carefully watched Kharg Island loading by satellite imagery, and there's really no indication that there's been any significant loading there in quite some time."

Brown said coordinating a 14-vessel convoy would also pose major logistical challenges, requiring lead and trailing ships, coordinated communications and procedures for responding to U.S. military orders.

Civilian crews could face significant danger if they refused orders to stop, he warned.

TRUMP WARNS OF NEW STRIKES AGAINST IRAN AFTER NEW YEAR, CALLS NEGOTIATORS ‘PROFESSIONAL TAP DANCERS’

"They would obviously be going into an area of great risk, and they would have to decide whether to comply with the instructions to stop or face action," Brown said.

In a Nov. 18 advisory, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) warned that ships receiving Iranian cargo through ship-to-ship transfers could face interception or seizure, extending the blockade beyond vessels departing Iranian ports, Reuters reported.

Brown said U.S. forces would likely contact the tankers by radio from Navy ships or aircraft and order them to stop. Refusal could trigger an escalated military response.

He said the Navy could transfer responsibility between regional commands, making it difficult for Iranian tankers to escape by sailing farther into the Indian Ocean.

"There's an administrative boundary, a geographic boundary between the 5th Fleet and the 7th Fleet, between CENTCOM and INDOPACOM," Brown said.

"But the U.S. Navy is a global Navy, and they're able to handle these transfers of responsibility when a target or ship of interest crosses that boundary."

Brown said U.S. forces have the ships, aircraft and procedures to intercept multiple vessels at once, while the open waters of the Indian Ocean offer more room to maneuver than the narrow Strait of Hormuz.

"It's a mission of the United States, not merely a mission in CENTCOM," Brown said. "So they have the forces in place."

"So if they do try to make an attempt with multiple ships, I'm quite confident all or most — probably all — would be interdicted," he added.

articles.title: Tehran threatens to 'break legs' as 'Trump corridor' prepares to launch on Iran's border
articles.summary:
Armenia is set to launch a U.S.-backed transportation and energy project along Iran's northern border Monday, despite warnings from a senior Iranian official that Tehran would "break their legs" if President Donald Trump and his allies crossed the Islamic Republic's "red line."

Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan confirmed that the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project would launch Monday, advancing the plan to connect mainland Azerbaijan with its Nakhchivan exclave through southern Armenia and establish energy links with Turkey and Azerbaijan, Turkish media reported, citing Interfax.

The project, a centerpiece of a U.S.-brokered peace initiative between Armenia and Azerbaijan, would also expand American economic involvement in the South Caucasus, where Iran has warned against any development it believes could threaten its security or regional influence.

TRUMP'S FIRST IRAN WAR ESCALATION POST-MIDTERM LOSSES SEEKS TO CHOKE OFF TEHRAN’S TRADE

The corridor has also gained strategic significance amid the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, as Tehran seeks to secure its northern trade routes and limit the U.S. security presence near its borders while Washington maintains its naval blockade and Task Force Iron Gate focuses on Iran's borders.

Speaking at the DigiTec 2026 technology conference in Yerevan, Pashinyan said the new TRIPP initiative, also known as the "Trump Corridor," would strengthen Armenia's regional energy connections, according to Interfax.

"Tomorrow we will officially announce the launch of the TRIPP program, and energy and electricity transit will be an important component of it," Pashinyan said during a public discussion on artificial intelligence.

"We will now connect our network to the electricity grids of Türkiye and Azerbaijan," he added.

The announcement followed a warning from Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior foreign policy adviser to Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who accused Armenia of disregarding Tehran's security concerns over the proposed route.

"I told the Armenian ambassador the final word, clearly, that if Trump and his allies want to cross this Iranian red line, we will break their legs," Velayati wrote in a Nov. 5 article published by the Iranian newspaper Ettelaat, according to Iran's Tasnim News Agency.

TRUMP RETALIATES AFTER IRAN ATTACK AS EXPERT WARNS REGIME IS GROWING MORE DANGEROUS

Velayati also warned that Iran would defend its security interests in the South Caucasus regardless of Russia's involvement, pointing to Tehran's longstanding opposition to the proposed route.

The roughly 26-mile corridor would run through Armenia's southern Syunik province, near the Iranian border, connecting mainland Azerbaijan to Nakhchivan and providing an onward link to Turkey, a NATO member.

The route would include railways, roads, electricity transmission lines and fiber-optic cables, creating trade connections between Central Asia and Europe.

Iran has long opposed proposals for what Azerbaijan calls the "Zangezur Corridor," particularly arrangements that Tehran fears could weaken Armenia's control over the territory, disrupt Iran's access to Armenia or expand the presence of outside powers near its borders.

In August 2025, Velayati had already warned that the corridor could become a "graveyard" for what he called Trump's mercenaries, according to Al Jazeera.

"Such a corridor will turn into a graveyard of the mercenaries of Donald Trump, not a route owned by the U.S. president," Velayati said, according to the outlet.

Velayati also argued that Iran would act to protect the South Caucasus regardless of Moscow's position, while expressing his belief that Russia opposed the corridor on strategic grounds.

NO RETREAT AT HORMUZ — IRAN MUST NOT CONTROL THE WORLD’S ENERGY LIFELINE

During a December 2025 meeting with Armenia's ambassador to Tehran, Grigor Hakobyan, Velayati again raised concerns about the proposed route, according to Iran International.

The project emerged from a U.S.-brokered diplomatic initiative aimed at ending decades of conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan over Nagorno-Karabakh, an internationally recognized part of Azerbaijan that was controlled for years by ethnic Armenian separatists before Azerbaijani forces retook the territory in 2023.

Trump had hosted Pashinyan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev at the White House in 2025, where the two leaders signed a joint declaration intended to advance peace, normalize relations and reopen regional transportation links.

The declaration established the basis for the TRIPP initiative, giving Washington a central role in developing infrastructure.

Under the implementation framework announced by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan in January, the TRIPP Development Company would oversee development of the infrastructure.

TRUMP MEETS KEY IRAN WAR MEDIATOR AS UAE REVEALS MAJOR OIL EXPORT SURGE DESPITE CONFLICT

The framework calls for a U.S.-controlled entity to hold a 74% ownership stake in the company, with Armenia retaining 26%.

The company would receive development rights for an initial 49-year period, with an option for a further 50-year extension. Under the proposed extension, Armenia's ownership stake would increase to 49%.

Armenian authorities would retain jurisdiction over the territory, including responsibility for customs, immigration, law enforcement and border security.

The framework also provides for private operators to help facilitate trade and transit, while final customs and security decisions would remain with Armenian authorities.

On Oct. 28, Armenia's parliament ratified the agreement by a vote of 63-32. Armenian President Vahagn Khachaturyan signed the ratification law Nov. 12.

The United States, Armenia and Azerbaijan also announced the launch of trilateral technical planning groups in November to advance the initiative.

articles.title: Common sleep habit linked to 50% higher death risk in heart patients, recent study finds
articles.summary:
Adults with heart disease who sleep nine or more hours per night could be at a higher risk of death from both heart-related and non-heart-related causes than those who sleep seven to eight hours, according to a recent study.

The cohort study in the journal PLOS One, titled "Sleep duration and cause-specific mortality among US adults with heart disease," analyzed data from 3,287 adults with heart disease from the 2004 National Health Survey linked to the National Death Index running until Dec. 31, 2019.

In the National Health Survey, participants answered whether they had heart disease based on if they had ever been told they had coronary heart disease, a heart attack or a heart condition or disease, according to the study.

MORE NAPS, HIGHER RISK? RESEARCH LINKS DAYTIME SLEEP TO HEALTH WARNINGS IN AGING ADULTS

"Sleep affects blood pressure, blood sugar regulation, inflammation, and appetite hormones, and all of these influence cardiovascular risk," Erin Palinksi-Wade, a New Jersey-based registered dietitian and Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist (CDCES), told Fox News Digital.

The study authors adjusted for health factors and lifestyle behaviors such as body mass index (BMI), alcohol consumption, smoking, physical activity, diabetes, hypertension and more.

Sleep per 24 hours was categorized into durations of six hours or less, seven to eight hours and nine or more hours.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Over approximately 15 years of follow-up, 49.4% of participants died.

Out of all participants, 16.7% died from heart-related causes and 32.6% died from non-heart-related causes.

After adjusting for all lifestyle factors, researchers found that sleeping nine or more hours was linked to a higher mortality risk, compared with sleeping seven to eight hours.

There was a 51% increased risk of all causes of death, a 53% increased risk of heart-related causes of death and a 50% increased risk of non-heart-related mortality.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Sleep duration of six hours or less was significantly associated with non-heart-related death only in the least-adjusted model, and the connection weakened with further adjustment.

"Because the study is observational, it shows an association, not cause and effect. Long sleep may be a symptom of underlying problems like more advanced heart disease, depression, sleep apnea, or medication side effects, and the study couldn't fully account for those," Palinski-Wade said.

The authors noted that their findings do not invalidate the negative cardiovascular effects of getting too little sleep.

"I'm not aware of a convincing biological mechanism by which extra hours of sleep damage the heart," Antony Chu, MD, a cardiologist and clinical assistant professor at Brown University’s Warren Alpert School of Medicine, told Fox News Digital.

"What I see clinically is that patients sleep longer because something is pulling on their reserve: worsening heart failure, untreated obstructive or central sleep apnea, depression, sedating medications, anemia or frailty," Chu said.

Sleeping too much or too little are both potential red flags, Palinski-Wade noted, so it’s important for people to pay attention to how rested they feel rather than only focusing on the number of hours they slept.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Because the study only tested people with pre-existing heart conditions, it should not be used to suggest that prolonged sleep leads to heart disease in the general population, she added.

articles.title: FDA clears tiny surgical robot to remove bladder tumors
articles.summary:
If a doctor finds a tumor in your bladder, you want to know what you're dealing with. Is it cancer? Has it reached the bladder muscle? The tissue removed during surgery helps answer those questions. Now, a tiny surgical robot could give doctors a clearer view of what's happening inside the bladder.

The FDA has authorized the Virtuoso Endoscopy System, developed by Nashville-based Virtuoso Surgical. It uses two needle-sized robotic arms to remove bladder lesions through the urethra, without cutting through the skin. The technology allows surgeons to remove many tumors in one piece, potentially giving pathologists better tissue samples to examine. This new approach to robotic bladder tumor removal could help doctors make more informed treatment decisions.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

WOULD YOU TRUST A TINY DENTAL ROBOT?

The Virtuoso Endoscopy System uses a narrow medical instrument called a rigid endoscope, which enters the bladder through the urethra. At the tip are two miniature robotic arms made from a flexible metal alloy called nitinol. A surgeon controls both arms from a console. One arm lifts and holds the tumor while the other carefully separates it from the tissue underneath. This gives the surgeon two-handed control inside a very small space.

The technique is called en bloc resection, which means removing a tumor in one piece. Surgeons can already perform this procedure using conventional instruments, but it can be technically demanding. Virtuoso designed its system to make that approach easier to perform. The robot also relies entirely on the surgeon's movements. Unlike some autonomous surgical robots being tested in research settings, Virtuoso does not make surgical decisions or operate independently.

Bladder cancer affects thousands of Americans every year. The American Cancer Society estimates that approximately 84,530 people in the United States will receive a bladder cancer diagnosis in 2026. One of the most common procedures for evaluating and removing bladder tumors is called transurethral resection of bladder tumor, or TURBT. During conventional TURBT, surgeons often remove tumors in smaller fragments. While effective for many patients, that approach can disrupt the tissue's original structure. As a result, pathologists may have a harder time determining how deeply cancer has grown. That's particularly important when it comes to the bladder's muscle layer, called the detrusor muscle. Doctors need to know whether cancer has reached this muscle because that can change the recommended treatment.

Removing a lesion intact may preserve more of the information pathologists need. It can also allow them to examine the tissue around the tumor more clearly. Dr. Duke Herrell, a urologic surgeon and CEO of Virtuoso Surgical, explained the potential benefit in the company's FDA announcement. "Removing a tumor intact can provide a better tissue specimen, which supports clearer diagnosis and staging," Herrell said. For patients, a more complete tissue sample could help their medical team determine the next steps with greater confidence.

Virtuoso has already tested the system in human patients, and the early clinical findings are encouraging. In the first 20 patients enrolled in the company-sponsored VIABLE study at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, 94% of removed lesions contained detrusor muscle. That exceeded the study's predefined performance goal of 60%. Researchers also reported that surgical margins could be evaluated in 93% of malignant lesions. Surgical margins are the edges of the removed tissue. Examining them can help doctors assess whether cancer cells extend to the edge of the sample. However, being able to evaluate a margin does not necessarily mean it is free of cancer. The company reported no adverse events during the operations.

There are important limitations to these findings. The study involved a small number of patients at one medical center. The previously published first phase of the same VIABLE study involved six patients and recorded two postoperative adverse events. One patient experienced temporary urinary retention, while another developed a chest infection later linked to a separate esophageal tumor. The company also compared its results with previously published research on conventional bladder tumor removal.

However, the Virtuoso study did not directly compare the robot against traditional instruments in a randomized trial. Researchers still need larger studies to determine whether the system improves long-term outcomes or reduces the need for additional procedures.

BRAIN TUMOR FOUND DURING PREVENTIVE SCAN PUTS FULL-BODY MRIS BACK IN THE SPOTLIGHT

The FDA granted De Novo authorization for the Virtuoso Endoscopy System on Oct. 30, 2026. The company publicly announced the decision on Nov. 10. The authorization establishes a new FDA classification for robotic surgical instruments that operate through an endoscope inside the body. Specifically, the system is authorized to remove bladder lesions in adult patients and obtain tissue samples, including bladder muscle, to assist in diagnosing bladder cancer.

The decision follows the FDA's September 2025 Breakthrough Device Designation for the system. That earlier designation recognized the technology's potential and allowed the company to receive additional regulatory guidance during development. However, the new authorization does not establish that the robot improves survival rates or prevents cancer from returning. The system must also be operated by trained surgeons in an operating room.

Virtuoso Surgical plans a limited U.S. launch in 2027, starting with leading urology centers. The company has not announced which hospitals will receive the system first. That means patients may have to wait before the technology becomes available at their local hospital. Questions also remain about pricing and insurance coverage.

Virtuoso is exploring other potential applications for its miniature robotic instruments, including procedures involving the lungs. However, those uses remain experimental and have not received FDA authorization. For now, the company's focus is bladder surgery, where better tissue samples could help doctors evaluate cancer more accurately.

If you or someone you love is facing bladder cancer, this technology could eventually provide another surgical option. Its miniature robotic arms may help doctors obtain more complete tissue samples during the initial procedure. However, availability will be limited at first, and the early results still need confirmation in larger studies. The robot's FDA authorization also does not guarantee better results for every patient.

If you're discussing bladder tumor surgery with a urologist, ask whether en bloc resection might be appropriate for your situation. You should also ask how the surgeon plans to obtain enough tissue to determine whether cancer has reached the bladder muscle. Those answers can help you understand your options before surgery.

When you're facing a possible cancer diagnosis, getting accurate answers as early as possible can make a real difference. That's what I like about this technology. Virtuoso's tiny robotic arms could help surgeons collect better tissue samples without taking control away from the medical professional performing the operation. It's also encouraging to see the FDA authorize a system designed for such a specific surgical challenge. Still, 20 patients represent a very small study, and I want to see how this robot performs in larger trials before getting too excited about its potential. If the results hold up, this could become a valuable addition to the tools doctors use to diagnose bladder cancer.

Would you trust a surgeon using this new robotic system to remove a tumor, or would you prefer a conventional procedure until there's more evidence of its benefits? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro claims judge ordered passports seized just 7 minutes after Brazil election loss
articles.summary:
Brazilian Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro accused his country's political and judicial establishment of engineering his presidential election defeat, telling Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview that he fled to the United States amid what he described as a campaign of political persecution — and insisting he lost not to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, but to "the system."

Following a razor-thin election, in which incumbent Lula da Silva won 51.8% to 48.2%, the Brazilian Supreme Court immediately canceled Bolsonaro's passports, prompting the senator and his family to flee the country in dramatic fashion, crossing the border into Argentina and flying into Miami, where President Donald Trump granted them political asylum.

Bolsonaro said that he fled for the sake of Brazil, to continue the fight against Alexandre de Moraes and the Brazilian Supreme Court, and alleging both election interference and political persecution.

SEN FLAVIO BOLSONARO FLEES BRAZIL FOR US AFTER ELECTION LOSS, WILL BE ISSUED VISAS: STATE DEPARTMENT

"I did not leave Brazil to run away. I left for Brazil's sake, and these accusations are completely unfounded. This is a case that began with ‘fake news,’ a false media report, and it's a case that was artificially manufactured against me.

"This is the modus operandi, particularly of Alexandre de Moraes in Brazil, when he wants to persecute someone. So, he invented this case against me to leave a kind of sword hanging over my head, something he can use whenever he wants. He wakes up in a bad mood and decides to persecute someone, someone against whom he has artificially manufactured a case," he claimed.

"And look, just a few days before the election, he opens this investigation to try to damage my reputation. It's a way for him to interfere in the election to benefit my opponent. And what struck me most was that just seven minutes after the official election results were announced, he took action to seize my passports, to confiscate my passports and prohibit me from leaving the country."

Bolsonaro added,"Seven minutes. I emphasize that: just seven minutes after the election ended."

He acknowledged he lacks evidence of fraud in the election, but alleged that the electoral system is flawed because it is impossible to demand a recount.

"Look, I don't have proof because I'm prohibited from investigating. The elections in Venezuela were also recognized in the past. And everyone knows those elections were fraudulent," he said.

"In the most recent elections in Venezuela, it was possible to prove that fraud occurred because they adopted a system that we had been asking Brazil to implement for the 2026 elections."

BOLSONARO WINS FIRST ROUND OF BRAZILIAN PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION, AS TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATES CONTINUE RED WAVE

Bolsonaro asked,"What is that system? Electronic voting with an individual printed record of each vote, ensuring the secrecy of the ballot while allowing the votes to be recounted. Let me ask you something: Does Brazil's current system allow votes to be recounted? No," he answered.

"What's happening in Brazil is that the technology experts who have been there for years, through several elections, and who are themselves under suspicion, are simply taken at their word. Whatever they say becomes the truth," he claimed.

"Nobody has any way to conduct an audit. If we ask for an audit, will it be authorized? No. So, whatever they say becomes the truth. They tell the Superior Electoral Court, the TSE, and the court repeats what they say without even fully understanding whether it's true or not."

With Bolsonaro in political exile in the United States, all eyes will turn to Sao Paulo Gov. Tarcisio de Freitas, who cruised to re-election last month, and stepped aside this election cycle to clear the field for Flavio Bolsonaro on the right. 

Yet election experts disagree with Bolsonaro's assessment over the safety of the nation's voting system. 

Karina Stange Calandrin, a political scientist and professor at Instituto Brasileiro de Mercado de Capitais (IBMEC), recently told Fox News Digital, "It is an extremely secure and safe system. The machines never connect to the Internet and even the central database system used to transmit tallied votes to TSE must match results issued physically and locally by each individual machine without human interference." 

Corrupting it, she, would require breaking the seal of each machine and installing software that wouldn’t match the TSE’s version, automatically disqualifying its tally — a scale of collusion so large that it "simply could not pass undetected."

BRAZIL’S RAPID ELECTION COUNT PUTS SPOTLIGHT ON VOTING SECURITY AHEAD OF US MIDTERMS

While acknowledging the strength of a potential de Freitas candidacy, Bolsonaro is leaving the door open to running in 2030, provided that his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, is still ineligible to run.

"Look, thanks to President Bolsonaro, the right in Brazil has many strong leaders with the potential to become president of the republic. Not just Tarcísio de Freitas, but several others."

He said, "In a scenario in 2030 where President Jair Bolsonaro is still ineligible to run, I am a candidate. My name is on the table as a candidate for 2030, provided that Congress makes improvements to the electoral system."

He continued, "But that is still far in the future. In four years, a lot can happen in politics. With the two years remaining in Donald Trump's presidency, a lot can happen. The political landscape could change completely. So it's still much too early to make those plans."

Bolsonaro said "the right has what I call a good problem. Imagine a soccer team with 11-star players ready to take the field. How does the coach decide which player to put in each position? The right has many stars. It has many qualified people, strong candidates capable of running in any election in Brazil."

He added, "That's not what happens on the side of evil, on the side of the left, on the side of communism. Over there, the only leader who still exists is the current president of the republic himself, who isn't allowing any prominent figure to emerge as a possible successor."

BOLSONARO DECLARES HIMSELF 'LEADER' OF BRAZIL AFTER FLEEING COUNTRY, ARRIVING IN MIAMI

Although the 2026 election saw right-wing candidates dominate in the Senate, Chamber of Deputies, and in gubernatorial races, Bolsonaro is calling on his supporters to oppose the re-election of the current speaker of Brazil's lower chamber.

"Look, Hugo Motta was never someone from my political camp. He has always been a very pragmatic politician, including in his dealings with left-wing parties."

He said, the "problem with Hugo Motta, and the reason I'm advocating against supporting his re-election as president of the Chamber of Deputies, is that two years ago, when he was elected with the support of my party, he promised, for example, to grant amnesty to those being persecuted in Rio de Janeiro. And did he keep that promise? No."

He said, "Then they came up with an intermediate proposal, something called ‘dosimetria,’ or sentence recalculation. What is that? It's a new process that doesn't amount to an amnesty at all. It simply reduces, to some extent, the sentences of people who were convicted."

He said, "That was approved by the Chamber of Deputies, and the Supreme Federal Court simply suspended it with the stroke of a pen. And whose pen was it? Alexandre de Moraes. So he didn't deliver what he promised."

Bolsonaro said the political movement founded by his father is stronger than ever, while maintaining that the United States is the best place for him right now, because he can speak freely, while working with allies in the Brazilian Congress.

"The last hope we have is in the National Congress, especially the Federal Senate. Once again, this demonstrates the strength of the right and of the Bolsonaro movement. A lot of people said in the past that they had defeated the Bolsonaro movement… But the results of the 2026 elections, and the votes I officially received, nearly 60 million votes, almost 50% of the valid votes cast for president of Brazil, tell a different story. Look at the number of center-right deputies and senators we helped elect."

He noted, "All of this shows that the right and the Bolsonaro movement are stronger than ever. But we're facing a system that is working very hard to prevent Brazil from prospering and to stop the right-wing agenda from advancing."

He added, "So, as I often say, I didn't lose to my opponent. I lost the election to the system. And that's what makes me so outraged. I'm going to remain here in the United States, continuing to speak out, saying exactly what I think, without holding anything back."

He concluded, "I hope not only that God will intervene in our country to save Brazil from communism, but also that our institutions will return to functioning normally."

Fox News Digitall's Solly Boussidan and Sydney Finver contributed to this report.

articles.title: What really happens when you need help restoring your identity
articles.summary:
Identity theft restoration takes more than one phone call. It often means securing accounts, documenting fraudulent activity and working with several companies to correct inaccurate records.

The term "identity restoration" can sound complicated until you suddenly need it. Maybe someone opened a credit card in your name, took over your bank account or used your personal information to get medical care. Now you're dealing with unfamiliar charges, paperwork and companies that all seem to have different requirements.

Fortunately, knowing what happens during recovery can make the process easier to manage. Here's how identity restoration typically works, what you may need to do yourself and where professional help can make a difference.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

IDENTITY RESTORATION: WHAT TO DO AFTER IDENTITY THEFT

Identity restoration usually starts with understanding the problem. A specialist may ask when you first noticed suspicious activity, which accounts someone accessed and whether you lost money or personal information. These details help identify the type of identity theft involved. Someone opening a credit card in your name requires a different response than a criminal taking over your phone number or using your medical information. A restoration specialist can help you separate confirmed fraud from suspicious activity that still needs investigation. As a result, you can focus on the companies and accounts that need attention first.

Before tackling paperwork, focus on preventing additional damage. Depending on what happened, you may need to contact your bank, lock a credit card, change passwords or secure your mobile phone account. If someone accessed your email, make securing that account an early priority. Criminals can use compromised email accounts to reset passwords and gain access to other services. You may also want to place a fraud alert or freeze your credit.

Neither option fixes fraud that has already occurred. However, both can help reduce the risk of additional new-account fraud.

One of the most frustrating parts of identity theft recovery is having to explain the same problem repeatedly. A case file helps you keep track of important information and avoid starting over with every phone call. Include dates of suspicious activity, copies of statements, confirmation numbers, correspondence and the names of representatives you've contacted. Also, record what each company promised to do and when you should expect a response. This becomes especially helpful when several organizations are involved. For example, your bank might close an account while a fraudulent balance still appears on your credit report. Having documentation gives you a clear record of the steps you've already completed. Keep those records somewhere secure. Additionally, avoid sending sensitive documents through unverified email addresses or links.

Depending on the type of fraud, identity restoration may involve banks, creditors, credit bureaus, mobile carriers, medical providers or government agencies. Each organization follows its own procedures. A bank may ask you to complete a fraud affidavit, while a credit bureau may request an identity theft report before blocking fraudulent information. A restoration specialist can explain those requirements and help you navigate the process. In some situations, the specialist may also coordinate communications or work with institutions on your behalf. However, you may still need to verify your identity, provide documents or authorize certain actions. Restoration assistance helps you work through the process, but the affected institutions remain responsible for reviewing claims and correcting their records.

Once you secure your accounts and identify the affected organizations, the next step involves correcting the damage. If someone opened a fraudulent credit account, you may need to dispute the information with the creditor and the credit bureaus. The Federal Trade Commission recommends reporting identity theft through IdentityTheft.gov, where you can create an FTC Identity Theft Report and receive a personalized recovery plan. An FTC Identity Theft Report can also help you exercise important rights, including requesting that credit bureaus block information resulting from identity theft. Medical identity theft may require contacting healthcare providers and insurers to correct inaccurate records. Meanwhile, tax identity theft generally involves working directly with the IRS. Keep copies of every document you submit. Whenever possible, request written confirmation after an organization resolves an issue.

Identity theft recovery rarely happens all at once. Your bank might reverse a fraudulent transaction before a credit bureau finishes investigating a related account. Similarly, a phone carrier may restore your number, but you may still need to strengthen account security to prevent another takeover. That's why follow-ups are so important. Set reminders for promised responses and continue checking your statements, accounts and credit reports after the initial incident. You can review your credit reports for free each week at AnnualCreditReport.com. Even after you resolve a case, additional suspicious activity can surface if criminals continue trying to use your stolen information.

WAS YOUR IDENTITY STOLEN? WHAT TO DO IN THE FIRST 24 HOURS

Not every identity theft case follows the same path. The type of fraud determines which organizations need to get involved and what steps you should take. For example, new-account fraud often involves creditors and credit bureaus. An existing bank-account takeover requires immediate attention from the financial institution, while medical identity theft may involve correcting treatment and billing records. Tax or government benefits fraud can require separate reporting procedures. And if a scammer convinced you to authorize a payment, your options may differ from those available for unauthorized account transactions. That's why identifying the problem early is important. A credit freeze may help protect against new credit accounts, but it cannot correct a medical record or recover money sent to a scammer.

Identity theft recovery can feel slow, especially when you're waiting for several companies to respond. However, you can track progress by focusing on specific actions rather than expecting everything to happen immediately. Have you secured the compromised account? Did you report the fraudulent charge? Has the credit bureau acknowledged your dispute? Each completed step helps move the case forward. If a company misses a deadline or provides conflicting information, your case file will help you explain the situation without starting the conversation from scratch.

Before speaking with a restoration specialist or fraud department, gather any suspicious statements, letters, alerts or emails connected to the incident. The company may also ask you to provide identification, an FTC Identity Theft Report or written authorization allowing someone to assist with your case. Always verify that you're communicating with the legitimate organization before sharing sensitive information. Also, ask why a document is necessary and how the company plans to handle it. Ultimately, you should understand what information you're providing and what actions someone may take on your behalf.

If you've experienced identity theft, handling multiple disputes and follow-up calls yourself can become overwhelming. That's where an identity protection service may help. Some services provide access to identity restoration specialists who can guide you through the recovery process. Depending on the provider and your plan, specialists may help organize documentation, explain next steps and assist with communications involving affected institutions.

Identity protection services may also monitor certain personal information, credit reports and financial accounts. Alerts can help you discover suspicious activity before it leads to additional problems. However, identity monitoring cannot detect every form of fraud, and restoration assistance cannot guarantee that every dispute will end in your favor. The benefit comes from having experienced support when you're trying to work through a complicated situation.

Beyond restoration assistance, some identity protection services offer tools that help you identify suspicious activity, reduce the exposure of personal information and respond when something looks wrong. Features vary by provider and plan, so it's worth checking what's included before signing up.

Some services offer tools that help you identify merchants and websites that may have your payment card information on file. Reviewing these connections can help you decide where to remove stored payment details, especially if you no longer use certain accounts. However, these tools cannot automatically confirm whether someone has stolen your card information.

Certain identity protection services can monitor eligible financial accounts and flag transactions that appear unusual or potentially fraudulent. These might include unfamiliar purchases or unexpected charges. An alert gives you an opportunity to review the transaction and contact your financial institution if necessary. Keep in mind that these services may not detect every suspicious transaction.

Some identity protection services include tools that search covered data broker websites for your personal information and submit removal requests on your behalf. Reducing publicly available information may help limit your exposure to identity theft and scams. However, no removal service can erase your information from every website or guarantee that it will never reappear.

Some providers offer access to support specialists or online tools that can help you evaluate suspicious messages, websites and financial activity. Depending on the service, you may receive guidance on reporting scams, securing accounts and taking steps to recover from identity theft.

Certain plans may also include reimbursement benefits for eligible losses or expenses, subject to coverage limits and exclusions. However, these services cannot guarantee that you'll recover money you sent to a scammer. Always review the terms before relying on a particular benefit.

See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com

When someone steals your identity, discovering the fraud is often only the beginning. The real work comes afterward, when you're trying to secure accounts, correct records and get answers from companies handling different parts of the problem. I've always believed that knowing what to do next can make a stressful situation much easier to handle. Start by protecting the accounts you still control, document everything and use the free recovery tools available through the FTC. If you want additional help, an identity protection service with restoration specialists may help you navigate the recovery process and stay organized. No service can promise an instant fix, but having experienced support can make a difference when you're dealing with identity theft.
