articles.title: Indonesia candy factory fire leaves multiple dead, dozens missing
articles.summary:
A massive fire tore through a three-story candy factory in Indonesia's Banten province, killing at least three workers and likely more, and leaving dozens of others unaccounted for as emergency crews fought persistent hotspots into Sunday.

Indonesian police removed 24 body bags amid battling the smoldering fire and pausing a search for missing workers overnight, which will resume Monday morning. There were reportedly as many as 300 present for their Saturday shift, but the factory said 24 of the 65 workers involved had returned home, four were receiving medical treatment, 29 remained missing and the whereabouts of another eight had yet to be confirmed.

Body bags might contain remains from several people because the intensity of the fire had rendered the recovered victims unidentifiable, police said.

The fire broke out at 5 p.m. local time Saturday at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia facility in the Cikande area of the Serang district, which borders the capital, Jakarta.

CHINA FIREWORKS FACTORY EXPLOSION: VIDEO CAPTURES DEVASTATING AFTERMATH OF BLAST THAT LEFT AT LEAST 26 DEAD

"We have concluded that the victims of this fire cannot be identified through visual inspection," Wahyu Hidayati, a police disaster victim identification official, said.

Authorities are collecting DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings of the missing workers. The identification process could take two to three weeks, Hidayati added.

WASHINGTON PAPER MILL CHEMICAL TANK IMPLODES, KILLING AT LEAST 1 AND LEAVING 9 MISSING

Flames engulfed the structure and sent thick black smoke billowing into the sky, leaving behind twisted metal and blackened, corrugated iron roofing.

FIRE ABOARD CARGO SHIP UNDERGOING REPAIRS AT BUSY CHINESE PORT LEAVES 25 PEOPLE DEAD, FIVE MORE INJURED

"The figure of 50 refers to those whom we have not yet been able to account for," the factory owner said during a news conference.

More than 12 hours after the fire started, 15 fire trucks backed by water cannons were still working to douse hotspots concentrated in the central and rear sections of the building. A joint response team comprising police, military personnel, the Indonesian Red Cross, and volunteers was there, though structural instability made their work difficult.

SEATTLE FIRE CREWS RESPOND TO 3-ALARM INDUSTRIAL DISTRICT WAREHOUSE FIRE, ROOF PARTIALLY COLLAPSES

"We are conducting sweeps in the areas that have already been brought under control, " Tubagus Mahfud, operations chief of the Serang fire department, said. "Parts of the structure had collapsed, while poor lighting conditions required firefighters to proceed cautiously."

Mahfud warned that the factory's production materials posed a high risk of reignition, making thorough cooling operations critical before crews can access the entire building.

MASSIVE CHEMICAL FIRE ERUPTS AT ELECTRICAL TRANSFORMER PLANT IN MISSISSIPPI, FORCING EVACUATION

"Authorities continue to coordinate with families and the company to determine the whereabouts of employees believed to have been inside the factory when the fire broke out," the Banten Search and Rescue Agency's Rizky Dwianto said.

While police said the cause of the fire remains under investigation, survivors told Indonesian media the flames originated from a cooling unit on the third floor.

The facility is part of Indonesia's United Family Food company – founded in 1981 and employing roughly 5, 000 people – and manufactures Milkita, a popular Indonesian brand of milk-based candies and snacks. The tragedy adds to a string of deadly industrial fires in Indonesia in recent years that have raised ongoing concerns over workplace safety and emergency preparedness.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: Social media users are eating huge amounts of carrots and shrimp for a natural tan
articles.summary:
Some social media users are "carrotmaxxing," "tomatomaxxing" and "shrimpmaxxing," in the hopes of getting a sun-kissed glow that lasts them all winter long.

The trend, which calls for eating large quantities of carrots, tomatoes and shrimp, or taking supplements packed with their compounds, relies on carotenoids, natural pigments found in certain foods, the New York Post recently reported.

The outlet highlighted wellness creators promoting raw carrots as a way to get a "carrot tan," including one who said she no longer gets fake tans, and followed two Atlanta moms who said they take a daily carotenoid supplement for a "healthy glow."

COULD 'HUMANMAXXING' ACTUALLY HELP YOU LIVE LONGER? HERE'S WHAT EXPERTS SAY

The supplement they take is a blend of three carotenoid pigments: beta-carotene, lycopene and astaxanthin, the compounds that give carrots, tomatoes, shrimp and salmon their color.

Wellness influencer Lee Tilghman Pollis, meanwhile, recently said on Instagram that raw carrots have given her "the best skin of my life and I will die on this hill."

Another influencer went viral on TikTok for her carrot tan, telling followers that she no longer gets fake tans or stays out in the sun and instead eats three to four large carrots a day for several months to build up her tan.

DOCTOR REVEALS 4 HIDDEN HEALTH RISKS OF SPENDING TOO MUCH TIME INDOORS

Experts say the skin-color change is real and generally harmless, but it's no substitute for basic sun-safety measures.

"Beta-carotene, lycopene and astaxanthin are fat-soluble pigments, and when you eat a lot of them they build up in the outermost layer of the skin," Dr. Navin Arora, a board-certified dermatologist and medical director of Borealis Dermatology in New York, told Fox News Digital.

NEW CALIFORNIA LAW WILL RESTRICT SALES OF SOME MUSCLE-BUILDING SUPPLEMENTS TO MINORS

The buildup can create a yellow or orange tint, often first visible on the palms, soles and around the nose.

There is no reliable dose for achieving a cosmetic change, Arora said. Small studies have found visible changes after about six weeks of eating extra servings of fruits and vegetables, though results can vary. The color also fades gradually after a person cuts back, he noted.

That pigment buildup, known as carotenemia, is generally harmless, Arora said, but skin that turns yellow-orange without a dietary change should be evaluated by a health care professional.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The food trick does avoid skin damage caused by UV exposure, which also raises the risk of skin cancer and premature aging.

"The carotenoid glow involves no UV damage at all, but it also gives you no meaningful sun protection," Arora warned. "'Carrot color' is not a substitute for sunscreen."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Arora cautioned against taking high-dose carotenoid supplements for appearance, though. High-dose beta-carotene supplements have been linked to increased lung cancer risk in people who smoke or used to smoke, according to the National Institutes of Health’s Office of Dietary Supplements.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

For people seeking a bronzed look, Arora recommends self-tanners, professional spray tans, bronzers or tinted sunscreen. He advises pairing them with broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every day.

"Eating a colorful, carotenoid-rich diet is great for your overall health," he said. "I’d treat the glow as a bonus, not the goal."

articles.title: Iconic MTV star turns 60, shares her no-guilt approach to fitness, food and aging well
articles.summary:
During her 1990s rise as an MTV icon and supermodel, Daisy Fuentes admitted that "being cute" was her top priority. 

Now, as she enters her 60s, the TV personality and lifestyle entrepreneur has traded superficial beauty pressures for a more grounded approach to health.

Speaking with Fox News Digital, Fuentes, who is primarily based in Los Angeles, opened up about embracing a guilt-free "anti-hustle era" — sharing her 20-minute workouts, a "magical" sleep trick and the surprisingly simple habits that keep her rested and strong.

JENNIFER ANISTON’S SECRET TO STAYING FIT AT 57 STARTS WITH ONE SIMPLE WORKOUT ROUTINE

Fuentes’ health and wellness priorities have shifted a great deal in the decades since she started modeling and appearing on TV in her late teens and 20s, she shared.

"In that era, I was more focused on, how can I look better? How can I lose a few pounds to look better in certain clothes? It was very superficial. And as the years have passed, health and wellness has started to become an inside job," Fuentes said.

"When you start realizing that most of your life has already happened, how you want to live your life now … becomes more about being present and being able to enjoy the time that you have left," she added.

LONGEVITY DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT MATTERS MOST FOR AGING WELL, BEYOND PRICEY BIOHACKS

Amid the litany of longevity-focused tips and tricks circulating online, Fuentes said she strives to keep it simple and not be "obsessive" about health and wellness.

"On social media, depending on your algorithm, you can get bombarded and overwhelmed with all the [things] that you're supposed to be doing and not doing," she said.

"Yes, some of those things are smart … I do a lot of the things, but I also realized at a certain point that it's much more important to have fun, to be present, to not obsess, and to leave a little room for the unexpected."

As Fuentes entered her 50s, she started to experience some sleep challenges, which she attributed to fluctuating hormones during menopause.

"Balancing out my hormones [and] going on HRT [hormone replacement therapy] helped tremendously," she said. "It got me feeling back to my old self, where the minute I got in bed, I would do a little scrolling and all of a sudden my eyes would start closing."

10-MINUTE FITNESS HABIT CAN HELP ADULTS OVER 40 MAINTAIN MUSCLE AND STAY STRONG

Although Fuentes admits that she breaks a few traditional "sleep hygiene" rules — such as scrolling on her phone in bed – she does wear red-light-blocking glasses and strives to keep her social media algorithm strictly positive.

Fuentes said she relies on what she describes as a total "sensory experience" to stay asleep, including wearing a silk eye mask.

"Right as I'm going to sleep, I pop that mask on, and it's almost like magic," she said. "It does something to your brain. It relaxes you." She also uses an air purifier that provides white noise.

"Our room is set up for sleep," Fuentes said. "We don't hear anything, we don't see anything and it is a sensory experience … a routine that instantly prepares your mind for what it needs to do."

When it comes to fitness, Fuentes said she strives for consistency, but, above all, listens to her body.

A key component of her routine is strength training, which she does four or five times a week. "That doesn't mean it has to be long … I can do a full-body weight training in 20 minutes, and that's what's important to me right now," she said.

WOMEN WHO START COMMON HORMONE THERAPY IN THEIR 50S MAY HAVE 23% LOWER DEMENTIA RISK

Other mainstays of Fuentes’ fitness regimen include Pilates, walking and staying active outdoors. "That's what keeps me and my mind really feeling better," she said.

"Sometimes I get on a vibration plate with my weights and just do 15 minutes of that, doing a plank, doing some sit-ups on it, some squats — I just try to do whatever I can," Fuentes said.

"Some days I have more energy, some days I don't, and I don't beat myself up about it. I do what I feel like doing and as long as I'm doing something, I'm OK."

When it comes to nutrition, Fuentes’ biggest shifts over the last decade were driven by physical changes during menopause. Noticing stubborn weight gain around her midsection in her mid-50s, she said she scaled back to about two meals a day and eliminated mindless snacking.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"I try to make it very protein-based," she said. "I start my day with a coffee that already has 20 grams of protein in it ... And if I'm having a snack in the middle of the afternoon, it's going to be protein-packed yogurt with some nuts and berries."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

While Fuentes adopted a vegetarian, plant-based diet in her mid-40s, she emphasized that healthy eating doesn't require an "all-or-nothing" mindset, encouraging others to lean into more whole foods that match their lifestyle and preferences.

After decades of fast-paced working – both on and off-screen – Fuentes made a conscious decision in her late 40s to embrace a slower pace of life.

"Ambition that never ends is something that I think needs to be adjusted as we flow through life," she said, adding that she no longer desires to "be out there and be chosen" the way she did in her 30s.

"I started embracing the fact that I am in this era of my life where I don't want to work like when I was 30 … and it's OK to feel proud of myself for what I have accomplished," she said. "I don't want to feel guilty for enjoying the fruits of my labor, for enjoying my life now."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

When it comes to decompressing, Fuentes said she recharges by spending quiet time in the home spaces she loves decorating. Some of her favorite ways to unwind include reading, having tea with a friend, sitting in her backyard or taking an hour-long walk.

Fuentes shared her gratitude for being able to enjoy time with her husband, musician Richard Marx, whom she met in her mid-40s.

"Finding love and finding your person later in life made me feel so grateful to have the time to spend with him," she said. "Why would I want to pretend to be busy doing something when what really fills my heart is to be with him, to have fun, to do what I want to do right now?"

While Fuentes acknowledged that she is in a "privileged" and fortunate position, she pointed out that she spent decades sacrificing to earn it. 

Stepping into her "anti-hustle era" in her 50s and 60s, she said, is about questioning whether you are staying busy out of habit — or are ready to embrace a new, more fulfilling stage of life.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Russia strikes hometown, criticizes Putin-Trump meeting
articles.summary:
A Russian strike on Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown of Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 58 others, the Ukrainian leader said Saturday.

A 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were killed in the attack Friday night in the central Ukraine town, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration.

Zelenkskyy said in a social media post the woman was an emergency medical worker and the boy was named Tykhon.

PUTIN LAUNCHES UKRAINE BARRAGE HOURS AFTER TRUMP MEETING AMID ALLEGED RUSSIAN MISSILE BREACH OF NATO AIRSPACE

"He was born in 2019, and, sadly, most of his life was lived during a war like this. And the Russians took his life with their strike. My condolences to their families and loved ones," Zelenskyy said.

On top of the civilian deaths and injuries, the strike sparked four fires and damaged roughly 25 apartment buildings, along with a hospital, schools, an industrial facility, businesses and vehicles.

RUSSIA'S PUTIN VOWS A RESPONSE 'FAR MORE PAINFUL' AFTER UKRAINE ATTACKS PRIZED BRIDGE IN CRIMEA

Zelenskyy claimed the Russian strike hit an area of the city with no military targets.

"The strike hit an ordinary civilian area of the city – there are no military facilities nearby, and there never have been," he wrote. "Russia is waging war against life, and there can be NO justification for this."

TRUMP WILL FACE REPORTERS AFTER HISTORIC XI-PUTIN TALKS AS WAR QUESTIONS LINGER

The Ukrainian leader later commented on President Donald Trump's recent meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Putin didn't get his 'Yalta 2,'" Zelenskyy wrote, referring to the famed 1945 Yalta Conference between former U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin.

TRUMP’S PROPOSED RUSSIA DEAL RAISES NATO ALARM AS EX-COMMANDER WARNS PUTIN SEEKS INFLUENCE OVER EUROPE

"As far as I understand, he recently commented: 'What's wrong with Yalta? Those were the victories over Nazism, over fascism, and so on, that were sealed there.' First of all, indeed, this was no Yalta. Did Putin want a real Yalta? Yes. 

"In the sense of carving up the world and changing borders. China didn't let itself be drawn into it. I don't know what happened between the United States and Russia in their bilateral, but Ukraine wasn't discussed. Nothing came out publicly. So the redrawing of borders didn't happen," Zelenskyy wrote.

"If there really was an intention to reaffirm the victory over fascism now, then the participants at this summit would have to be the United States, Europe, and Ukraine. Definitely not Russia. I think this trilateral summit turned out very badly for Russia. Not only did Putin fail to get the results he wanted, but we also saw his reaction.

"And, unfortunately, we saw that reaction in Ukraine. There was a massive attack that night – 111 missiles. If Putin wanted to remind the world once again who he is, there was no need – we haven't forgotten that he's a terrorist and a killer."

UKRAINE HITS PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE IN RECORD DRONE BLITZ AS KREMLIN TELLS LAWMAKERS TO PREPARE FOR 'VICTORY'

The strike on Zelenskyy's hometown is far from uncommon, with periodic Russian attacks targeting the industrial steel town dozens of times since the start of the war in 2022.

The incident also occurred as a Russian ship was struck by drones on Saturday, setting it ablaze in the Gulf of Finland.

The Russian-flagged Sparta II was struck by a drone shortly before 9 a.m., according to Finnish Coast Guard Commander Mikko Simola.

"Generally it should be noted that it is known that this Sparta II vessel has been used for transports for the Russian state, including the armed forces," Simola said.

As a result of its damage, the craft entered Finnish territorial waters. Simola also noted that Finland believed a Russian helicopter crossed Finland's sovereign borders as well.

Finnish officials believe that Ukraine was behind the attack.

"It is likely that Ukraine ... is behind (the attack)," Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen said.

Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to kill Ukrainian American rapper on Danish soil
articles.summary:
Denmark's security and intelligence agency (PET) accused Russia of attempting to kill Ukrainian American rapper Kyivstoner on Danish soil in September.

Authorities arrested two individuals on charges of attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service.

As a result of the alleged plot, Denmark will expel Russia's defense attaché from Copenhagen, the Danish foreign minister said. 

NATO MEMBER BOOTS 10 RUSSIAN DIPLOMATS

"We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and notified him of the government's decision to expel the Russian defense attaché from Denmark [within seven days]," Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said during a press conference Friday.

Russia denied any involvement in the alleged plot, calling the accusations "unsubstantiated" in a statement.

RUSSIAN SPIES ORCHESTRATED $40K MURDER PLOT IN NATION’S CAPITAL, US ALLEGES

Russia's intelligence agency, FSB, accused Kyivstoner, whose real name is Albert Vasilyev, of plotting a drone attack on Moscow in July, an accusation Vasilyev denied, according to Russian media outlet Meduza.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen reproached Russia for the alleged scheme.

SHE GREW UP UNDER SOVIET RULE; NOW, EU'S TOP DIPLOMAT WARNS EUROPE AGAINST GIVING RUSSIA WHAT IT WANTS

"I strongly condemn the assassination attempt against a U.S.-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, orchestrated by Russian intelligence services," she said in a statement.

"This was an attack on EU soil. And it is unacceptable," she continued. "Russia's hybrid threats are becoming less and less hybrid, and more and more real."

GERMANY BLAMES RUSSIA AFTER EXPLOSIVE-LADEN DRONE FOUND NEAR UKRAINIAN CARGO PLANES AT MAJOR AIRPORT

Danish security services said the pair who tried to carry out the attempted hit were affiliated with the Danish gang Loyal to Familia, which is "known for extensive, serious and violent criminal activity," according to PET.

Danish police stopped three individuals in a car near a music venue in Hellerup, where Kyivstoner was performing in September. Inside the vehicle they found guns and knives. Both men charged pleaded guilty.

TRUMP SIDELINES SWEEPING RUSSIA SANCTIONS AS GOP ALLIES WARN PRESSURE ON PUTIN IS SLIPPING

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said Denmark would issue fewer visas to Russians as a result of the incident.

"Toughen the sanctions against Russia, including a halt to all non-essential visas to Russian citizens, and these visas should only be valid in the issuing country," Frederiksen said.

The foreign ministries for Ukraine, Russia and Denmark did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital for comment.

Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: ASRA Q. NOMANI: Communist, hard-left groups mount global youth strike to bring 'socialist revolution'
articles.summary:
Red hammer-and-sickle flags flew over Europe at protests across the continent Friday, but media coverage barely mentioned them.

Media outlets described the day's demonstrations as "youth protests" over wages, schools, climate, "austerity" and the alleged "genocide" in Israel.

The streets told a different story.

A Fox News Digital investigation reveals that a transnational network of self-described communist, Marxist and socialist groups organized the protests with an explicitly ideological appeal of using party banners, mass-produced recruitment posters and calls for a "communist mass movement" and "socialist revolution."

CHAOS INC.: WHO'S WHO IN THE GLOBAL MAYHEM NETWORK? COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE

Officials in Hamburg, Germany, warned that "left-wing extremist" groups were behind Friday's actions.

In Milan, a young woman wore a red hammer-and-sickle shirt, raising her fist among demonstrators holding placards that read "FIGHT FOR OUR FUTURE" above small branding for Youth International Strike Against War, the socialist coalition that organized the day's actions.

By late Friday, the protests were promoted by BreakThrough News, a nonprofit funded by Neville Roy Singham, an American-born communist tech tycoon living in Shanghai, supporting the Chinese Communist Party and President Xi Jinping's "new world order."

According to a Fox News Digital analysis, the International Youth Strike brought together 114 communist youth organizations, revolutionary Marxist and socialist groups alongside far-left student unions, climate campaigners and anti-Israel activists. The official website lists actions in 24 countries.

A Fox News Digital tracker of groups involved in the International Youth Strike finds that most of them self-describe as communist, Marxist, Trotskyist, socialist or far-left. The remaining entries include education, environmental and other issue-based organizations, as well as groups whose ideology hasn't been established.

FROM 'RED SPROUTS' TO SCHOOL BOARD RACES, DSA'S YEARS-LONG EFFORT TO REACH CHILDREN GAINS MOMENTUM

The mobilization in Europe comes after the Democratic Socialists of America celebrated its midterm election victories by declaring that voters had "emphatically endorsed socialism."

In the U.K., members of Socialist Students, one of the lead organizers, marched behind bright red banners that read, "FIGHT FOR A SOCIALIST FUTURE."

Also in the U.K., the Revolutionary Communist Students urged members to walk out of school under the slogan "SMASH IMPERIALISM / FIGHT FOR REVOLUTION."

A wing of Revolutionary Communist International, a global organization that runs Marxist.com, the group promoted the protest with a video of members holding copies of their newspaper, the "Communist." And their members turned out in Cambridge, Liverpool, Leeds, Newcastle and Brighton in the U.K.

The platform framed the protests as "YOUTH-LED STRIKES ACROSS EUROPE AGAINST WAR AND LIVING COSTS." It featured a representative of Sindicat d’Estudiants in Spain without identifying the group's revolutionary Marxist politics as "revolutionary communists" with Barcelona headquarters at Casal Marxista, or "Marxist House."

The protests played into anti-West narratives, and Press TV, Iran's official propaganda network, published a story about youth protests "over wages and living costs."

The mobilization follows student blockades and nationwide demonstrations in France, where Fox News Digital established that a network of far-left groups, including communists, socialists and Antifa, helped orchestrate the unrest.

The strike's manifesto seeks NATO’s "dissolution" and "radical system change," placing students alongside the working class as a "revolutionary force." In Rome, one sign featured the silhouette of Marxist guerrilla Che Guevara and demanded, "CHE IS DEAD / STEP UP."

BEHIND FRANCE'S STUDENT RIOTS: COMMUNISTS, UNIONS AND A GLOBAL PROPAGANDA NETWORK

In Hamburg, the Ministry of the Interior and Sport's State Office for the Protection of the Constitution published a report Wednesday warning about "linksextremistische," or "left-wing extremist" groups playing a "significant role" in coordinating the protests.

Hamburg government officials said protest organizers weren't concerned about legitimate debate over policy issues, like the economy or conscription, but warned about "enemies of the constitution who attempt to exploit these and other legitimate causes for their anti-democratic ideology, for example, through relevant images and videos on social media."

For example, Young Struggle, a Europe-wide socialist group, founded in Stuttgart, Germany, said its members are "struggling against a system of capitalism, of endless exploitation, of war, imperialism and patriarchy." In another report, Hamburg officials warned that Young Struggle is a wing of a Turkish left-wing extremist group, the Marxist-Leninist Communist Party.

Young Struggle blasted its triumphs from the protests on social media with menacing fast-cut videos as Hamburg officials warned they would do from Lyon, France, Austria and elsewhere, and the message: "LA JEUNESSE PRÉPARE LA RÉVOLUTION (THE YOUTH PREPARES THE REVOLUTION."

"What we're witnessing in Europe is part of a pattern of malign actors using students and youth as foot soldiers in protest movements," Brandy Shufutinsky, director of education and national security at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a think tank based in Washington, D.C., told Fox News Digital.

"In the U.S. we've seen these entities attempt to connect things like climate justice, immigration and workers' rights to boycotts and sanctions against Israel," said Shufutinsky, a trained social worker.

"Often, these organizations form 'youth' wings as a way to garner support for their movements amongst younger generations. This happened with the formation of the Soviet Union, Nazi Germany, Communist China and Islamist Iran."

Many of the European strike organizers explicitly call for revolutionary changes to governance, ownership, wealth, taxes, laws and political power, much like in the U.S.

Germany’s Socialist German Workers’ Youth, another protest organizer, says it grounds its mission in "Marx, Engels and Lenin." Its theory page invokes Vladimir Lenin’s declaration, "Without revolutionary theory there can be no revolutionary movement."

Fellow signatory REVOLUTION, operating in Germany, Austria and elsewhere, describes itself as an "independent communist youth organization." Its mission advocates "revolutionary overthrow," a "communist mass movement" and a "world party of socialist revolution."

Sweden’s Revolutionary Communist Youth, which led protests, identifies its ideological foundation as "Marxism-Leninism" and describes organizing through "class struggle."

Symbols of the far-left Antifa movement, which the Trump administration declared a terrorist group, also appeared at protests.

In Tel Aviv, Israel, the far-left emerged with an "ANTIFA ACTION" flag, much like one that fluttered in Cologne, Germany, where protesters flew a flag with the message, "ANTIFASCHISTISCHE AKTION," meaning "Anti-Fascist Action" in German, commonly associated with Antifa. The name originated with a campaign launched by Germany’s Communist Party in 1932. Today, its familiar two-flag emblem is used by antifascist groups and activists worldwide.

In Italy, demonstrators marched beneath communist party flags, hammer-and-sickle emblems and historical resistance banners.

In Turin in northwestern Italy, near the French border, members of the Confederazione Generale Italiana del Lavoro, or the Italian General Confederation of Labour, filled a square, waving red hammer-and-sickle flags and protesting beside members of the Partito Comunista dei Lavoratori, or Workers' Communist Party, a far-left, Trotskyist political party.

Italy’s Giovani Comunisti, the Communist Refoundation Party's youth organization, joined the protests, too. The group describes its members as "proudly communist." 

Its website promotes Marxist political education under the instruction: "Educate yourselves. Agitate. Organize."

Others marched behind a banner marked "FC-FGC," referring to the Communist Front (Fronte Comunista, FC) and the Front of Communist Youth (Fronte della Gioventù Comunista, FGC).

In Rome, a flag with the hammer and sickle and the name "Partito Comunista Rivoluzionario," Italian for "Revolutionary Communist Party," flew at a protest, along with a flag of Cuba, a symbol of support for the Communist Party of Cuba.

Nearby, members of the Garibaldi Brigades, named after a formation of the Italian Communist Party that fought in the resistance during World War II, waved their flag with a red star over the Italian tricolor.

A demonstrator also carried a flag of the former Soviet Union over his shoulder, while a red hammer-and-sickle flag appeared beside Palestinian flags at the monument to Giuseppe Garibaldi, a 19th century revolutionary who led guerrilla fighters called "Redshirts."

Activists of a Marxist–Leninist party, Fronte Comunista (Communist Front), unfurled their hammer-and-sickle flag on the streets.

In Milan, a protester dressed as Karl Marx, the communist theorist, carried a depiction of his treatise, "Das Kapital."

The mobilization also drew support from American communist and socialist organizations.

In Los Angeles, the Party for Socialism and Liberation held a Friday evening forum to discuss global student protests. The communist group works closely with the nonprofit network funded by Singham.

In Denver, Denver Communists, Colorado Revolutionary Communists and other far-leftists descended on the Colorado State Capitol with demands expressed by the "youth strike" movement: the "abolition of all forms of military conscription," solidarity with the "struggles of oppressed peoples around the world, starting with the Palestinian people," "climate justice and social justice," "radical transformation of the system we live in" and a challenge to "authoritarianism, repression and the far right."

In Britain, political organizations used recruitment placards, newspapers and advertisements to reach potential supporters with Marxism 101.

At King's College London, a protester carried a copy of the "Socialist Worker" newspaper alongside fliers promoting "MARXISM IN A DAY!" – a Nov. 28 event sponsored by the Socialist Workers Party.

"Revolts have broken out across the world. From Paris, to Mumbai, from Madrid to Milan, from Tirana to Lisbon — the youth is taking to the streets to fight for a better world," the event promotion says.

"Now more than ever, revolutionary Marxist ideas are crucial to the fight backs against a world of capitalist catastrophe," it continues.

The promotion promises "socialists and anti-fascist campaigners from France," including Zoé Lewkowicz, a French socialist and "anti-fascist" organizer with Autonomie de Classe, a revolutionary socialist organization based in Paris.

In London, a man held a red flare in front of signs that declared "FIGHT FOR SOCIALISM," while demonstrators covered their faces with keffiyehs and surgical masks beside red hammer-and-sickle flags and Socialist Worker placards declaring, "FOLLOW FRANCE: FIGHT THE SYSTEM."

Like professional protest organizers do in the U.S., Socialist Worker activists piled pre-made signs at a lamppost for demonstrators to pick up just before the 9 a.m. The placards were bundled with tape around their wooden handles and grouped by message. An image of a Malcolm X appeared on one design bearing the demand: "FIGHT FOR SOCIALISM!"

Others said: "JOIN SOCIALIST STUDENTS."

Soon, the recruitment message was moving through the crowd. Surrounded by police in reflective vests, marchers carried the signs piled moments earlier against the lamppost.

In Bremen, Germany, marchers carried a flag marked "ANTIFA" behind a banner depicting a clenched fist holding a pencil in front of a globe with the message "NOT THEIR WARS." They marched in front of a flag that said, "JUGEND GEGEN WEHRPFLICHT, AFSK LEIBNIZPLATZ."

"AFSK" refers to the Antifaschistisches Schüler:innen Kollektiv, an "antifascist" collective in Bremen that mobilizes students to join "red blocs," or "roter block."

"Jugend gegen wehrpflicht" means "Youth against conscription."

Researchers at Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung, a center-right think tank, have also warned that far-left groups use these student demonstrations to channel youth frustration toward broader far-left, pro-Russian foreign policy narratives.

In Bochum, a man with a white beard and mustache carried a sign bearing the initials "DKP" for the German Communist Party.

His poster read, "Stoppt die Kriegsvorbereitungen," or "Stop the preparations for war."

It also bore the message, "Nein zur Wehrpflicht," or "No to conscription." It continued: "Bundeswehr raus aus Schulen und Universitäten" — "German armed forces out of schools and universities."

In Bochum, students carried a banner, "GenZ Regelt," as "GenZ sorts it," beside another banner, "Sozialismus regelt," translated as, "Socialism will sort it out" or "Socialism fixes it," with generational branding while downplaying explicit socialist messaging.

From London to Berlin, the Palestinian flag and keffiyeh scarf, representing Palestinian "resistance" to a Jewish state of Israel, was a fixture at protests, even flapping outside the Colosseum in Rome beside the tricolor flag of the Garibaldi Brigades.

In the West Bank and Gaza, 11 Palestinian groups associated with the boycott, divest and sanctions movement, whose officials have said they seek the end of a Jewish state of Israel, issued an announcement supporting the youth actions and called for the "right of our refugees to return to their homes and receive reparations."

The mobilization's planning meetings show ambitions extending beyond Friday.

According to Britain’s Socialist Party, 12 organizations from eight countries met in Cologne on June 14, months before France’s autumn unrest. Socialist Students proposed the campaign’s slogan, "Fight for Our Futures, Not Their Wars." Its own mission seeks a "socialist transformation of society."

By the time of an Oct. 17 meeting in Paris, participation had grown to 27 organizations from 11 countries. Delegates discussed connecting national grievances under the international banner, joined the street demonstration and agreed to continue organizing after Nov. 20, according to Socialist Students’ account. A larger conference is planned in Italy in February 2027.

Socialist Students urged that gathering to establish an "international socialist youth network," making the walkouts a potential recruiting ground for a continuing political action.

In the United Kingdom, Shabbir Lakha, a national spokesman for the "Stop the War Coalition," stood on a stage at Downing Street, accusing governments of having "facilitated the genocide in Gaza" and urging demonstrators to unite to "break their imperialist power." The coalition doesn't list its donors.

At day's end, Stop the War Coalition shared a Guardian article, headlined "Young people across Europe stage coordinated 'fight for our future' protests." There was no mention of the communist and socialist ideological underpinnings of the protests or the hammer-and-sickle flags and revolutionary banners that defined the day on the streets.

The coalition also promoted another mobilization for Jan. 23, calling for yet another "mass movement against war, militarism and austerity" – and socialism and communism.

Fox News Digital's Reagan Schroeder contributed to this report.

articles.title: FBI Ten Most Wanted cartel leader 'Chapo Isidro' captured by Mexico's 'elite military forces' after US help
articles.summary:
One of the FBI's Ten Most Wanted fugitives has been captured in Mexico after a joint U.S.-Mexico operation during which the arresting force "came under attack with gunfire and explosives," authorities announced Saturday.

Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, described by the FBI as the "alleged leader of the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization, a heavily armed, major drug-trafficking organization based in Sinaloa, Mexico," was detained in the city of Guasave. 

The State Department previously issued a $5 million reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of Meza-Flores, who went by the alias "Chapo Isidro."

ALLEGED JALISCO CARTEL LEADER ACCUSED OF DRUG TRAFFICKING AND FUEL SMUGGLING ARRESTED IN MEXICO

Mexico's Secretariat of National Defense said Meza-Flores was detained during a military raid carried out by special forces personnel. U.S. and Mexican intelligence agencies coordinated in the lead-up to the operation, which also netted the arrests of the cartel's second in command and a financial operator.

"The operation to carry out these arrests was conducted by elite military forces, which, after precisely locating the target using various technological tools, carried it out in three phases, as follows," the Secretariat of National Defense wrote on X. 

"Arrival in the target area: this was carried out using stealth and surprise via different land access routes to the arrest area.

"Establishing security and capturing the target: this was carried out near the detainees’ location by setting up an internal and external security perimeter to prevent escape or the arrival of reinforcements," it continued. "The arresting force came under attack with gunfire and explosives, prompting it to enter the house to capture the individuals in question.

"Evacuation of the target: after the detainees’ identities were confirmed, they were evacuated to Mexico City aboard a Mexican Air Force aircraft to be placed at the disposal of the competent prosecutorial authorities," it also said.

Video released by the Secretariat of National Defense showed Mexican military personnel moving a handcuffed suspect into a truck.

KASH PATEL DEFENDS FBI'S ‘MOST WANTED’ BUSTS AMID MANIPULATION ACCUSATIONS, HIGHLIGHTS 'SUMMER HEAT' SUCCESS

In its Ten Most Wanted Fugitive poster, the FBI said Meza-Flores "is allegedly responsible for the possession, distribution and importation of large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the United States, and has predominately controlled drug production, transportation and distribution in several locations throughout Mexico.

"Meza-Flores was originally indicted on May 2, 2012, in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia. On November 26, 2019, a federal superseding indictment and federal arrest warrant were issued for Meza-Flores in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia after he was charged with multiple counts of Drug-Trafficking Violations and Use and Possession of a Firearm," it added.

The operation surrounding Meza-Flores' arrest forced the cancellation of a Mexican Pacific League baseball game in progress in Guasave on Friday, with video on social media purportedly showing players and fans running for safety at Kuroda Park while gunfire rang out in the background.

Another video shared by a Mexican media outlet purportedly showed a helicopter firing at a target in Guasave during the operation, while other videos on social media depicted trucks burning as part of roadblocks in the region.

articles.title: Jennifer Aniston’s secret to staying fit at 57 starts with one simple workout routine
articles.summary:
At 57 years old, Jennifer Aniston seems to be defying the laws of aging — but it doesn’t come without hard work.

The "Friends" actress has been public about practicing PVOLVE, a functional fitness method grounded in movement longevity.

The workouts prioritize mobility and stability through twisting and reaching motions that translate directly to everyday life. Combining sculpting, cardio and weight training, the method is designed to build muscle mass and support bone density.

10-MINUTE FITNESS HABIT CAN HELP ADULTS OVER 40 MAINTAIN MUSCLE AND STAY STRONG

According to PVOLVE trainer Melanie Ramos, what keeps Aniston looking and feeling her best isn't a specific workout buzzword, it's consistency.

"She's very consistent," Ramos told Fox News Digital. "She trains about three to four times a week doing PVOLVE, and she trains in all our modalities. … She specifically is adding a lot more weight training into her routine."

As people age, especially women, muscle mass begins to decline, according to Ramos, who serves as lead trainer at PVOLVE Soho in New York City.

"So, I think for [Aniston], the consistency and just adding that extra weight training really helps her look amazing," she said.

WANT TO AGE BETTER? RESEARCHERS SAY 4-MINUTE ROUTINE MAY HELP PREVENT DANGEROUS FALLS

According to research published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology, only about 20% of women regularly engage in strength training, with many opting for aerobic exercise instead.

While walking offers major benefits for overall health, pairing cardio with simple resistance work can lead to significantly stronger heart and longevity outcomes.

Rather than feeling pressured to commit to a full-hour workout to see results, Ramos advised simply getting started, adding, "Something that [Aniston] really prioritizes is even just getting 15 minutes of movement. "

Starting with "baby steps" — aiming for at least three workouts per week, even if they're short — will help you feel "like you can achieve the goals you want," the trainer said.

YOUR WALKING SPEED MAY HOLD A CLUE TO HOW LONG YOU’LL LIVE, STUDY SUGGESTS

"And then build more of that lifestyle habit where it feels that you need that movement every day," Ramos continued. "Movement is a part of life, and as we age, we have to look at how we're moving our body."

Prioritizing strength training and gradually increasing muscular load helps build lean mass and improve bone density, according to the trainer.

As the body naturally stiffens with age, Ramos noted, targeted mobility and stability exercises become essential for maintaining balance and independence.

To show how simple it is to get started, Ramos demonstrated three signature moves from Aniston’s routine — targeting mobility, strength and stability, using just a pair of dumbbells.

Modification: Bring the legs closer together for a smaller and softer squat.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Modification: If twisting is hard on the back, hug the dumbbell closer to the chest instead of over the shoulder for smaller movement. Limit the bend in the supporting leg.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Modification: Hold the weight with two hands, tucking the elbows in and bringing it up in an uppercut punch style.

Always consult a doctor or healthcare provider before starting any new fitness routine, especially if you have preexisting injuries or medical conditions.

articles.title: $500M investment could bring AI robots to your workplace
articles.summary:
What if a robot could learn how to do your job simply by watching you work? That's what Genesis AI is working toward, and some of the biggest names in tech are betting big on it. The robotics company has raised $500 million to bring its general-purpose robot, Eno, into more workplaces. The investment values Genesis at $3.5 billion and puts some serious financial muscle behind its plans.

But what really caught my attention is how these robots learn. Genesis is developing technology that allows people to teach robots physical skills without having to program every movement. Workers wear special electronic gloves while doing their regular jobs. The gloves capture their hand movements and turn that information into training data that helps robots learn to perform similar tasks.

Eventually, Genesis wants these robots to handle complex work without someone constantly supervising them. The company plans to bring Eno to customer sites in 2027, starting with industrial workplaces. So, how close are we to robots that can actually do our jobs, and what happens to the people teaching them? Let's take a closer look.

AI BUILDS VIRTUAL HOMES WHERE ROBOTS LEARN FROM THEIR MISTAKES

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

Genesis AI announced a $500 million Series A funding round at a $3.5 billion post-money valuation. Premji Invest, Khosla Ventures and Eclipse co-led the investment. Other backers include Nvidia, AMD Ventures, Samsung Next and Zoom. Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, Zoom CEO Eric Yuan and Yahoo co-founder Jerry Yang are also among the investors. T. Rowe Price-advised accounts and several other major financial and technology firms participated. That's a significant vote of confidence in a company developing robots that can perform physical work across different environments.

Genesis plans to use the funding to expand robot training and improve its artificial intelligence. The company is also increasing production of Eno while hiring additional researchers and robotics engineers. 

"Our mission is to remove the physical limits on human ambition," said Zhou Xian, co-founder and CEO of Genesis AI. The company wants to move beyond robots programmed to repeat a single task. Its larger goal is to build machines that can adapt to changing conditions and eventually handle entire workflows.

Eno takes a different approach from humanoid robots designed to closely resemble people. Genesis has focused on giving the machine useful physical capabilities rather than recreating every aspect of human appearance. The robot combines dexterous hands with a body designed for practical work. Its hands can handle tools and objects that require careful control, while its AI helps it respond to different physical tasks.

At the center of the technology is GENE, the company's AI foundation model, which acts as the robotic brain. The system helps robots interpret their surroundings and control precise physical movements. We previously covered Genesis AI's robotic brain and its ability to perform complex hand movements.

Now, the company is working to bring that intelligence into Eno for commercial use. For now, Genesis has demonstrated several advanced skills using a test robot powered by GENE. Those capabilities are expected to move to Eno as development continues.

How does a robot learn to handle delicate objects or perform tasks that require precise finger movements? We asked Genesis AI co-founder and President Théophile Gervet to explain how its electronic gloves make that possible.

"The electronic gloves are worn while people are performing their regular work so we can collect massive amounts of real-world data about how humans perform physical tasks in order to train GENE, our robotic brain," Gervet explained. 

"The gloves capture detailed finger movements and the pressure applied when handling different materials. Genesis designed its robotic hands to closely match human hands, creating what the company calls a 1:1:1 mapping between the human hand, glove and robotic hand. This process enables Eno to learn complex physical skills without having to manually program every movement.

Genesis also uses small cameras worn on workers' heads to record tasks from their point of view. 

"This lets GENE see exactly what someone sees as they perform a task, including how they use their hands and interact with their surroundings," Gervet said. The company also trains GENE using existing videos of people performing physical work. Together, these sources help the AI develop more complex physical skills.

Genesis has another training advantage. Its robots can practice inside Genesis World, a simulation platform that recreates physical environments. For example, a robot learning to play the piano can study movements collected from someone wearing the electronic gloves. It can then repeatedly practice those movements inside a virtual environment.

Gervet explained how the training process can speed up learning. 

"Also, instead of practicing at the piano for an hour or so a day like you and I might, the robot can train in our hyperrealistic simulation, Genesis World, helping it master its task, like playing the piano, much quicker than it would in the real world." 

That approach allows developers to test movements without relying entirely on expensive physical training sessions.

AUTONOMOUS EXCAVATORS ARE DIGGING WITH EMPTY CABS

Genesis has demonstrated its GENE robotic brain performing several complex activities. These include preparing meals, handling laboratory equipment and assembling wire harnesses. Gervet also cited manipulating a Rubik's Cube as an example of a skill learned through human demonstrations. These activities require precise control of robotic hands.

However, there's an important detail here. These demonstrations currently use a test robot rather than Eno itself. 

"Today, GENE allows robots to tackle a wide variety of tasks, including preparing a meal, lab pipetting, wire harnessing, packaging and more. These tasks are currently being demonstrated in a test robot and will be exported over to Eno very soon," Gervet told us.

That means Genesis still needs to show how well Eno performs these skills during extended operation in actual workplaces. One investor says the technology has already shown encouraging progress. 

"What stood out to us was watching Genesis robots complete long, multi-step tasks on their own at the same speed a person would, with smooth and natural movement," said Vedant Agrawal, partner at Premji Invest.

Genesis began proof-of-concept projects and customer pilots in 2026. Now, the company is preparing to bring what it learned into its next phase of commercial deployment. 

"We started proof of concepts and pilots with customers in 2026 and received valuable insight by working with the customers. Now we are taking these lessons learned and heading to customer sites in 2027," Gervet told us.

 The first deployments will focus on manufacturing facilities, logistics operations and laboratories. Genesis has also announced a strategic partnership with LG CNS, LG's consulting and AI transformation business.

The companies plan to evaluate Genesis robots for manufacturing and logistics work at LG operations in the United States. Their partnership could eventually expand to additional industrial customers. 

Gervet confirmed the relationship and said, "We will share more on our work with them in the coming months." 

After industrial deployments, Genesis plans to expand into hospitality and healthcare. Home robots and outdoor applications are further down its development roadmap. However, the company has not announced a firm timeline for bringing Eno into people's homes.

As Genesis works toward robots that can handle entire workflows independently, there's an important question about the employees helping train them. Could those same robots eventually take over some of their jobs? We asked Genesis how employees participate in its training program and who owns the data collected through the electronic gloves and cameras. The company says participation is voluntary and that people involved specifically agree to the work. 

"All employees who participate in data collection have chosen to opt in and have agreed and consented," Genesis told CyberGuy.

The company added that participants understand how the information is collected and that Genesis does not capture personally identifying information. It also says people receive clear information before providing consent. As for ownership, Genesis was direct: "We own the training data that we capture with our gloves and cameras."

That answers an important question about the program. However, the larger issue remains how this technology could eventually affect employment. Workers may voluntarily help train robots today, but those same machines could eventually perform some of their responsibilities without constant human supervision.

Teaching a robot to perform an impressive task under controlled conditions is one thing. Making that same robot work reliably every day inside a busy workplace is another. Industrial environments change constantly. Equipment moves, objects may end up in unexpected locations and people work nearby.

For general-purpose robots to become practical, they need to respond safely when something goes wrong. Genesis believes developing its hardware and AI together will help address those challenges. The company also controls its training systems and simulation technology, allowing engineers to improve different components together. But the biggest unanswered questions involve long-term performance.

Genesis has not provided detailed commercial pricing or independently verified reliability results for Eno across extended customer deployments. Gervet acknowledged the challenge when discussing the future of robotics. "The challenge is making sure these robots can operate reliably and safely in the real world, not just perform impressive demonstrations in controlled environments." Those are exactly the questions businesses will need answered before trusting robots with more responsibility.

You probably won't see an Eno robot rolling into your workplace tomorrow. However, this technology offers an early look at how physical jobs could change over the next several years. If you work in manufacturing or a laboratory, robots like Eno could eventually handle tasks that require constant repetition. That could reduce physically demanding work while changing the skills employers expect from their teams.

For employees, the bigger question is how companies will introduce these machines. Will robots work alongside existing teams, or will businesses eventually use them to reduce staffing? Genesis sees opportunities to make workplaces more productive, but the long-term impact on jobs remains uncertain.

For people outside those industries, the longer-term possibilities include robots that help with household chores or assist in healthcare settings. Those applications remain further away and will require additional safety testing.

HYUNDAI TO SEND 25,000 ATLAS ROBOTS TO THE US

There's something fascinating about the idea of teaching robots to do our jobs simply by putting on a pair of electronic gloves. But I can't help wondering what happens when those robots become capable of performing the same work without us. That's a conversation I think we need to start having now, before this technology becomes commonplace. The $500 million investment shows how much confidence major tech investors have in Genesis AI. 

The company has ambitious plans to bring Eno into workplaces, and we're getting closer to seeing how robots like these could change the way businesses operate. Genesis says people participating in its training program voluntarily opt in, which is important. But I think there's still a bigger conversation to have about what happens after these robots learn the job. If companies eventually use them to take over certain responsibilities, employees deserve to understand how that could affect their future.

Would you be comfortable wearing special gloves that teach a robot how to do your job if that same robot could eventually replace you? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

articles.title: Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan customer data leaked
articles.summary:
You trust your bank to protect your money. But how much do you know about the outside companies that also handle your personal information? That's a question worth asking after a ransomware group leaked customer data linked to Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase.

On Nov. 19, 2026, The Wall Street Journal reported that hackers had leaked information allegedly linked to thousands of customers of the three financial companies. The reported exposure involved third-party service providers that work with financial companies. Now, customers are left wondering what information hackers obtained and whether they need to take action.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

A SCAMMER HAS YOUR NAME, PHONE NUMBER AND ADDRESS; WHAT CAN THEY ACTUALLY DO?

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

A cyber extortion group known as n0n claimed to have stolen information associated with the three financial companies. According to Reuters, the group posted claims on Nov. 16 about obtaining cardholder engagement records. These allegedly included extensive marketing activity associated with tens of thousands of email addresses. The group also posted claims involving Visa and Mastercard that same day.

The reported cyberattack involved outside service providers that handle information for financial institutions. Some of the records appear connected to customer marketing activities and cardholder benefit programs. However, several important questions remain unanswered. The companies have not publicly identified all the affected vendors, and investigators have yet to establish whether one compromised provider was responsible for all three reported exposures.

JPMorgan Chase confirmed that third-party service providers were targeted in a cyberattack. In a statement to CyberGuy, a JPMorgan Chase spokesperson said, "Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses."

The bank says its services remain operational. It also plans to contact affected customers where appropriate and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring. Addressing the transaction processing delays that affected multiple banks earlier this week, the spokesperson added, "There is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week."

According to Reuters, leaked records appeared to contain more than 16,000 JPMorgan Chase customer email addresses and 124 bank employee email addresses. Some entries also included phone numbers and postal codes. Reuters could not independently verify the authenticity of the records.

Mastercard also acknowledged an incident involving an outside provider. However, the company says the exposed information was limited to email addresses belonging to a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program. In a statement to CyberGuy, Mastercard said the incident involved non-payment information.

"There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards," Mastercard said.

The company also confirmed that the exposure has been contained. Its teams are working with the affected provider to support cardholders as needed. Mastercard has not publicly identified the benefit program involved or disclosed an exact number of affected customers. The company also has not indicated that payment card numbers were exposed.

Visa has responded to CyberGuy about the reported cybersecurity incident involving a third-party service provider in the Asia-Pacific region. The company says its own systems and payment information were unaffected.

In a statement, the company said, "Visa is aware of these claims. They are associated with an incident involving a third-party service provider in Asia Pacific. Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected. This is unrelated to any of the system disruptions across different industries this past week."

However, Visa has not identified the service provider or disclosed how many customers may have been affected. The company also has not specified what non-payment information, if any, was exposed.

So far, the companies' statements point primarily to customer information held by outside service providers. Mastercard says its payment network remains secure, while Visa says payment card numbers were unaffected. JPMorgan Chase has identified potentially exposed marketing data. There has been no verified indication that customer banking passwords were stolen or that hackers accessed funds through this incident.

However, stolen contact information can still create problems. Criminals may use names or email addresses to make phishing messages appear more convincing. You could receive an email claiming your bank detected suspicious activity related to the recent cyberattack. The message might direct you to a fake website designed to steal your login information. We've covered how convincing these scams can be in our article about fake bank security alerts that trick customers into sharing personal information.

9 WARNING SIGNS OF IDENTITY THEFT YOU SHOULD NEVER IGNORE

You do not need to assume your account has been compromised. However, there are several practical steps I recommend taking to reduce your exposure to follow-up scams.

Be cautious of unexpected emails or text messages claiming your Visa, Mastercard or JPMorgan Chase account needs immediate attention. Scammers may reference a real cyberattack to make their messages more convincing. They could also claim that your card will be suspended unless you verify your information. Don't click links or open attachments in suspicious messages. 

Instead, open your bank's official app or type its website address directly into your browser. You can also call the number printed on the back of your card. Using strong antivirus software can provide additional protection by helping detect malicious links and downloads before they cause damage. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com

A scammer may call pretending to be from your bank's fraud department. The caller might already know your name or email address and claim that a recent breach put your account at risk. The scammer may then ask you to read back a one-time verification code sent to your phone. 

That code could allow someone to access your account or approve an unauthorized transaction. Never share a verification code with someone who contacts you unexpectedly. Also, never transfer money to another account because a caller claims it will keep your funds safe. Legitimate bank representatives will not ask you to move your money to a supposedly safe account.

Enable transaction notifications through your bank or credit card app. These alerts can help you spot unfamiliar purchases without waiting for your monthly statement. Check your recent activity and report anything suspicious immediately. Even though the companies have not reported a compromise of their payment networks, monitoring your accounts remains a useful security habit.

Make sure your banking and primary email accounts use unique passwords. If you have reused passwords across accounts, replace them with strong alternatives. A password manager can help you generate and store them securely. Turn on multifactor authentication wherever available. If your bank supports passkeys or security keys, consider using them. 

An authenticator app is generally a stronger option than SMS codes, although it can still be vulnerable to certain phishing attacks. There is currently no verified evidence that passwords were exposed in this incident. These precautions can help protect your accounts against separate attacks. For more details, see our guide to whether bank text codes are enough to protect you.

JPMorgan Chase says it will contact affected customers where appropriate and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring. If you receive a breach notification, confirm that it came from your financial institution before clicking an enrollment link or sharing personal information. Credit monitoring can help you identify suspicious changes to your credit reports. However, it cannot stop someone from sending phishing emails or impersonating your bank. You should also be suspicious of anyone demanding payment to activate complimentary protection offered after a breach.

A credit freeze makes it harder for criminals to open new credit accounts in your name. You can place one for free through Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. You must contact each credit bureau separately. A freeze does not affect your credit score, and you can temporarily lift it when you need to apply for credit. If only your name and email address were exposed, a freeze may not be necessary because of this incident alone. However, it can provide broader protection, especially if a breach involves more sensitive identifiers such as a Social Security number.

An exposed email address becomes more useful to scammers when they can connect it with other personal details found online. Consider removing unnecessary information from public profiles and checking what data broker websites have collected about you. A personal data removal service can also help request the removal of information from participating people-search sites. These services cannot erase information already stolen in a cyberattack. 

However, reducing the amount of personal information publicly available may make it harder for criminals to build convincing profiles for targeted scams. You should also use your phone's spam filtering features and reputable antivirus software to help block suspicious messages or malicious downloads. Get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web: Cyberguy.com

If you clicked a suspicious banking link or shared personal information, take action quickly. What you do next depends on what happened.

You can also report suspected fraud through ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

I've always believed that protecting your financial information requires knowing who has access to it. This latest incident shows how complicated that has become. You can do everything right with your bank account, yet an outside company handling your personal information could still experience a cyberattack. Most of us have little say in which vendors our financial institutions use, and we rarely know how much information those companies collect. 

I appreciate that Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase provided statements about the incident. It's reassuring that payment services remain operational, but I'd like to see more transparency about the outside providers involved and exactly what customer information they were holding. Until we have those answers, I would pay close attention to unexpected messages claiming to be from a financial institution. If someone contacts you about a problem with your account, verify it yourself before taking action.

If your bank shares your personal information with outside companies, shouldn't you have a right to know exactly who has it? And would a data leak like this make you reconsider which financial institutions you trust? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com
