articles.title: "You’re right"—LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
articles.summary:
Many studies over the years have examined how people encounter climate science information. Some focused on the top results that Google surfaced (back when Google was still in the business of serving links), while others examined social media content or newspaper and TV news coverage. With large language models (LLMs) now forming a share of the public information diet, it's worth looking at how they handle climate change.

But there’s no direct way for researchers to look at the information people have seen. It is served ephemerally to individual users, confined to their chat session. A study led by researchers from University College London and the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) tried to tackle this question from multiple angles, testing LLMs with different prompts and evaluating their output. They started with benchmarks of simple factual questions (benchmarks that might even be in models’ training data at this point) but also analyzed more complex interactions—including when users think they’re right to push back on an answer.

CO2 Q&A

LLM research often faces (no-true-Scotsman-tinged) criticism for focusing on a particular model rather than some other frontier model that may have been released after the experiment concluded. In this case, the study used 33 models, including multiple versions of the major frontier and open-weight models. The flagship frontier models used were Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Gemini 3.6 Flash, and GPT-5.6 Sol. (You can find the full list in the report.)

articles.title: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
articles.summary:
Google announced Android developer verification last year, and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead. It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven't registered their apps to do so soon.

The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google's new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won't be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure. Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps.

In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously said verification would go global in 2027, and it's not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within "several months."

articles.title: Mouse fight club might explain why we like to watch violent things
articles.summary:
Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026

Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026

There's something about watching violent events that broadly appeals to us, whether it's the latest John Wick movie, a video game, or a live UFC bout. Scientists have debated whether watching violent things could make us more aggressive, but it could also be an adaptive survival strategy. Male mice, for instance, who watched other mice fighting learned enough about how to fight to better protect themselves (compared to mice who didn't watch fights) when pitted against stronger, more aggressive opponents, according to a paper published in the journal Nature.

The team randomly assigned male mice to three groups—fighters, spectators, or novices—and then subjected each group to eight days of training with three 10-minute sessions per day. The novices played with stuffed mice in isolation, while the spectators watched various pairs of fighter mice battle from a raised platform behind a transparent barrier—a set-up chosen to let them smell and listen to the fights as well as observe them.

The ninth day was "fight night," when all the mice had to face a daunting opponent in three 4-minute rounds. Each fight was filmed from above so that the mouse behavior could be analyzed. To monitor corresponding changes in brain activity, the team engineered the rodents' excitatory brain cells to glow green whenever they were activated, while inhibitory brain cells glowed red. They also implanted tiny optical fibers into 12 interconnected brain regions so they could track changing activity in every brain region simultaneously.

articles.title: How to tell a cyberattack from a plain old outage
articles.summary:
Over the past week, anyone could be forgiven for wondering whether a Diehard IV–style cyberwar had finally arrived in the US.

Across just four consecutive business days, a mass Microsoft exchange outage broke IT services for thousands of companies, a Federal Aviation Administration tech screw-up grounded airplanes across the country, a software problem affecting JPMorgan Chase caused another round of disruption, a United Airlines system glitch delayed flights yet again, and an NSA classified network’s downtime left the agency’s staff sitting at home waiting to return to their office at Fort Meade. In the midst of a US war with Iran and rising fears of AI-enabled hacking, this still-unfolding comedy of IT errors colliding across American infrastructure felt to plenty of observers like more than a coincidence.

Yet there’s still no evidence that any one of these clustered technological failures were related, much less caused by hackers. Their improbable, sequential timing left Americans anxiously doomscrolling for signs of foul play. But in cases like these, it’s the job of cybersecurity analysts (and reporters at WIRED) to determine—vibes aside—whether the latest tech outage was actually an accident or the result of a cyberattack.

articles.title: Cayetano wants to let ‘generous’ Filipinos cover gov’t debt. Any takers?
articles.summary:
Senator Alan Peter Cayetano is concerned about the national debt.

So concerned, in fact, that he wants the government to set up a mechanism so that even you — yes, you, individual taxpayer — can directly pay your share of more than P170,000.

That’s P170,598.03, to be exact, which Cayetano calculated as each Filipino’s share of the country’s enormous debt. It’s not money you owe or any citizen personally owes the government, of course, but if you’re feeling particularly generous, the senator thinks you should have a way to chip in. Are you game?

During Senate deliberations on the proposed 2027 budget, Cayetano asked economic officials where exactly he could hand over his contribution.

“If I want to be a good citizen and I want to pay my share, P170,000, where do I go?” he asked.

Play Video

For a moment, Senator JV Ejercito, who chairs the Senate finance committee, seemed perplexed. He grinned, turned to the economic team for help, and suggested that perhaps the best contribution Filipinos could make was simply to pay the right taxes.

“That’s not true because I’m already paying the right taxes. I want to go beyond that,” Cayetano responded. “I want to pay my P170,000 — and you won’t accept it?”

The senator went on to paint a vision of how wealthy businessmen might wish to pay for themselves and their families. 

“What if they’re feeling generous, and they have one or two kasambahay and they want to pay for it?” he added.

Even overseas Filipino workers might contribute smaller amounts over time — a few hundred dollars here and there, he imagined.

And if you’re wondering where this sudden wave of generosity might come from, Cayetano made an appeal to divine intervention.

“If we pray but we do not act, the Bible says faith without action is dead. So we cannot keep praying for a miracle without doing anything to open the door for that miracle,” he said, hoping the government would pave the way for a little divine intervention and a flood of donations.

Must Read

Escudero calls out fire effect in Sara Duterte trial livestream

As unusual as the proposal sounds, Cayetano does reference a historical example.

During the 1997 Asian financial crisis, millions of South Koreans famously gathered their gold jewelry to help their country overcome a severe foreign currency shortage. Around 3.51 million citizens contributed some 227 metric tons of gold, either donated or sold, to raise much-needed dollars.

Of course, South Korea’s campaign was about easing a foreign currency crisis, rather than paying off government debt, and it was only one part of the country’s economic recovery.

“Why can’t it happen to us?” Cayetano asked.

“If our debt were low and our debt payments were small, I wouldn’t be proposing that we bayanihan our way out,” he added in Filipino.

Of course, the good senator’s proposal, however well-intentioned, takes a few liberties with how national debt actually works. But let’s indulge the thought experiment. Can Filipinos really bayanihan their way out of debt?

Philippine government debt had reached P19.66 trillion as of end-September and is projected to reach P21.48 trillion by end-2027. Even if one million generous Filipinos each contributed P170,000, that would raise P170 billion, less than 1% of the projected debt.

Interest payments alone are programmed to reach P1.114 trillion next year, eating up more than 15% of the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget.

Economists previously told Rappler that the country’s debt remains manageable for now, although its rising size and cost are becoming concerning, especially as economic growth slows.

And besides, even Cayetano himself acknowledged what is perhaps the bigger problem with his proposal. Why would Filipinos voluntarily give the government more money when so many already distrust how it spends what they pay in taxes?

“The sentiment now is that everyone in government is a thief, that you’re all thieves, that we’re all thieves, and that no one wants to donate,” he said in a mix of English and Filipino.

And with a sitting vice president on trial for unexplained wealth, a proposed national budget riddled with red flags — roads whose coordinates lead straight into the sea and an overabundance of multi-purpose buildings — who exactly would be lining up to fork over another P170,000? – Rappler.com

articles.title: Senate begins plenary deliberations for 2027 national budget
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – The Senate on Monday, November 23, began plenary deliberations on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, with lawmakers proposing P204.634 billion in amendments that prioritize “basic needs,” including health care and education, while cutting billions of pesos in infrastructure projects.

Senator JV Ejercito, chairperson of the Senate finance committee, sponsored Committee Report No. 131 on House Bill No. 10858, or the General Appropriations Bill (GAB), formally bringing the proposed budget to the plenary for deliberations.

In his sponsorship speech, Ejercito bat for a “back to basics” approach in the proposed P7.2 trillion national budget, emphasizing the need to prioritize essential services.

“Health care, food security, education, livelihood, employment, and security — these are the things that we want to focus on during our outlining and deliberations of the 2027 national budget. Back to basics,” Ejercito said.

“Before we focus on complicated matters, we should focus what limited resources we have on ensuring that the basic needs of our people are provided,” he said.

The Senate’s P204.634-billion proposed amendments include a P97-billion reduction in the allocation for 3,463 projects of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).

These include 36 DPWH buildings, 295 projects deemed noncompliant for lacking proper documentation under the National Expenditure Program, and 3,132 noncompliant projects that appeared only in the House-approved GAB. 

Ejercito previously said the reductions in the DPWH budget would be realigned to foreign-assisted infrastructure projects, which saw a P130-billion decrease in the House-approved GAB.

Budget watchdogs People’s Budget Coalition and BetterGovPH had earlier flagged nearly 7,000 projects worth P190 billion that lacked published project attachments in the House-approved 2027 budget. PBC also tracked some 6,200 DPWH projects worth P170 million that were inserted into the budget.

“This, Mr. President, is the direction we want to pursue in the 2027 national budget. Back to basics, but with a clear vision for economic recovery and nation-building,” said Ejercito. 

Health, education get funding boosts

Under the Senate version of the budget, the health sector received a P52-billion increase, with funding partly sourced from realignments within the Department of Health (DOH).

State health insurer Philippine Health Insurance Corporation, or PhilHealth, received an additional P19.8 billion, raising its allocation from P74.4 billion under the House-approved GAB to P94.2 billion in the Senate version.

The DOH Office of the Secretary received an additional P9.6 billion, increasing its budget to P378.6 billion. This includes P5.49 billion for the Health Facilities Enhancement Program, P1.09 billion for health promotion programs, P1.5 billion for immunization programs, and P736 million for the Sulu transition.

The Senate realigned funding for medical assistance to the Zero Balance Billing program, allocating P1 billion for local government-run hospitals.

The education sector, meanwhile, received P915.4 billion in the Senate’s budget bill. Of this amount, P11.8 billion will go to the Department of Education, including P11 billion for the School-Based Feeding Program to support the universal feeding program for kindergarten to Grade 1 students.

State universities and colleges will receive P138.2 billion for the continued construction and improvement of their school buildings, with each SUC receiving P7.5 million for the Smart Campus Project — a program that would provide internet connectivity to over 100 campuses.

Funding restored for foreign-assisted projects

The Senate budget bill also provides additional P33.1 billion in funding for foreign-assisted infrastructure projects, primarily to restore funding cuts in the House-approved GAB.

Among these are P4.7 billion to restore the government’s counterpart funding for the Metro Manila Subway Project and P15 billion in loan proceeds for the North-South Commuter Railway project.

A combined P146.5 million will also be allocated for the NCR Busway Project, Active Transport Bike Share System, and Safe Pathways Program.

Agriculture, housing

The Senate also allocated budget to enhance food security and ensure productivity of farmlands amid the threat of Super El Niño, earmarking P251 billion for the Department of Agriculture (DA).

This includes an additional P4 billion for the DA’s Rice Program to help boost rice production; a P250 million fund for programs helping farmers amid the impending drought; and an augmentation of P1 billion for the DA’s Quick Response Fund to “assist our farmers the earliest time the streams and wells show signs of drying up.”

More than P1 billion was allotted for the establishment of the storage facility Benguet AgriPinoy Trading Center, while P50 million and P200 million were allocated for the construction of a cold storage facility in Barlig, Mountain Province and Oriental Mindoro, respectively.

The Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development will also receive P4.04 billion to support the Expanded Pambansang Pabahay para sa Pilipino Program.

Maritime, defense

Meanwhile, senators provided an additional P1.73 billion to the Department of National Defense, hiking its budget to P326.9 billion. This is on top of the P50 billion earmarked for the continued modernization of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. 

Ejercito also underscored the need to strengthen the capabilities of the Philippine Navy to improve maritime patrols and reinforce the country’s presence in the West Philippine Sea. The Philippine Coast Guard, for its part, will receive P45.6 billion, including an additional P146.8-million allocation, to support its operations and maritime security efforts.

Ejercito filed the committee report on November 20. It was signed by 18 senators, including senators Tito Sotto, Migz Zubiri, Bam Aquino, Bong Go, Risa Hontiveros, Kiko Pangilinan, Erwin Tulfo, Joel Villanueva, Ping Lacson, Chiz Escudero, Lito Lapid, Raffy Tulfo, Imee Marcos, Robinhood Padilla, Mark Villar, Pia Cayetano, and Camille Villar.

In a manifestation, Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano explained why he did not sign the committee report.

“My signature is not on that committee report not because I did not want to sign but because it is physically impossible to come up with a good judgment, even if I do trust the chairman of the committee on finance, Senator JV,” Cayetano said.

Budget ratification eyed by December 17

Senators are working on a tight schedule to ratify the budget bill and avoid a reenacted budget in 2027.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said over the weekend that the country could not afford another reenacted budget, arguing that a fresh spending plan would help stimulate the economy.

“If we have a new budget, we will have new spending, because if we analyze it, one of our country’s economic problems is slow spending. So, the 2027 budget will serve as a stimulus program to it,” Gatchalian told DZBB Super Radyo.

The Senate is eyeing holding an open bicameral conference committee on the proposed 2027 budget on December 13, with ratification targeted for December 17.

Apart from the budget, the Commission on Appointments (CA) is also racing against time to process the appointments of at least 35 presidential appointees, including Cabinet secretaries, ambassadors, and military officers, before its December 17 adjournment.

Gatchalian said the CA would hold three hearings before the break, from 8 am to 12 pm, ahead of the Senate’s plenary budget deliberations at 1 pm.

Senators are hoping to conclude the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte before the end of the year. The trial is currently on a brief break and is scheduled to resume on December 1.

“Whatever the ruling is — be it conviction or acquittal — the consensus is we want to finish the trial before end of the year,” Gatchalian added. – Rappler.com

articles.title: [Rappler’s Best] ‘Be very, very afraid’
articles.summary:
We humans spent the last few days dissecting what’s been keeping us listless these days — artificial intelligence and the future of news. 

Renowned historian and philosopher Yuval Harari warned us to be “very, very afraid” at this period in history. “AI is not a tool, it is an agent. It is something that can make decisions by itself. So it is taking power away from us,” he said.

But nothing is inevitable, Harari told Nobel Peace Prize laureate and Rappler CEO Maria Ressa in a pre-recorded fireside chat that aired on Saturday, November 21, at Rappler’s annual Social Good Summit (SGS) at Shangri-La The Fort in Taguig. “There are still choices to be made.” 

With the theme, “We, The Humans: Reclaim our Future,” this year’s SGS brought together global, regional, and local perspectives on how AI has been both a boon and a bane to humanity — and what governance can do to stem a seeming point of no return.

We’re in a “new imperial age,” Harari said, warning the Philippines that it risks losing control of critical infrastructure because of its dependence on foreign technology. Read more.

Staunch human rights advocate Agnès Callamard, secretary-general of Amnesty International, pushed for collective resistance to Big Tech’s unfettered and opaque inroads into our personal and professional lives. To do that and to fight back, humans must first understand AI, Ressa said.

Singaporean economist and AI executive Leslie Teo outlined ways to develop AI as a positive force for society. Read more. (We will be publishing more stories and videos from the summit in the coming days. Watch out for them.)

AI was also raised as a “growing concern” by the parliamentary body of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), which held its 49th Summit in Manila last week. But whether the region intends to address it collectively is unclear. 

In fact, the ASEAN Summit itself still failed to resolve critical regional issues that have been pending at the leaders’ desks: the civil war in Myanmar and the protracted negotiations for a South China Sea Code of Conduct. Read more.

In Turkey, the Antalya AI Pledge was launched on the sidelines of the COP 31 climate talks. It calls on governments and companies to take voluntary measures to power AI with cleaner energy. But China’s Alibaba is the only big tech company that has so far signed off on it.

Worse, the climate talks collapsed on Sunday, November 22, after leaders from the European Union and other countries rejected the final draft of a declaration that some deemed unambitious. 

The draft acknowledged — for the first time — that global warming was on course to exceed the 1.5°C that countries had vowed to preserve. Read more.

The draft deal published on Thursday, November 19, removed any reference to ending the use of fossil fuels, prompting negotiators to extend their meetings to Sunday.

The first draft of the deal had already signaled tough negotiations ahead. 

In Manila where realpolitik reigns, defense lawyers of Vice President Sara Duterte in her impeachment trial continued to mock the public with witnesses who are neither experts in their field, forthright in their answers, nor transparent in their practices. One was grilled over his “useless testimony.”

They got backups from ghosts — as the defense panel showed archived videos of the late senator Miriam Defensor Santiago and the late chief justice Renato Corona, who was convicted by the Senate impeachment court in 2013. 

Huwag mong buhayin ang patay (Don’t resurrect the dead), wrote senior editor Herbie Gomez in his Pastilan piece. 

Last week’s trial also miffed Thought Leader Chito de la Vega, who noted how he had been looking forward to what Duterte’s counsels boasted as a bombshell defense of their client. “Hanggang ngayon, nganga pa rin ako,” Chito wrote here. (I’m not sure that an English translation would do justice to that phrase.)

Former central bank deputy governor Diwa Guinigundo laments the lost opportunity to ferret out the truth about the allegations against the Vice President. Read more.

As far as the other Duterte is concerned, here are the key dates of the trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte at the International Criminal Court in The Hague, which begins on November 30. Rappler will be there to cover it.

articles.title: Dela Rosa seeks dismissal of absenteeism complaint
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa has asked the Senate ethics committee to dismiss a complaint against him over his prolonged absence from the Senate.

In a response submitted to the Senate committee on ethics and privileges, Dela Rosa, through his legal counsel Israelito Torreon, sought the dismissal of a complaint filed by anti-corruption group Wag Kang Ku-corrupt in February.

The group had asked the Senate panel to investigate the senator’s prolonged absence, determine whether he violated Senate rules and ethical standards, and impose appropriate sanctions if warranted.

In a notice, the Senate ethics panel informed dela Rosa that they had found the complaint to be compliant with requirements “both in form and in substance” following an executive session on October 22. The panel directed Dela Rosa to submit a written response within 15 days of receiving the notice.

Dela Rosa’s office confirmed receiving the notice on November 19.

In his response, Torreon argued that the complaint should be dismissed for “insufficiency in form and substance, and for failure to state any offense cognizable by the Committee.”

Dela Rosa also asked the committee to hold the proceedings in abeyance pending the resolution of his camp’s motion for reconsideration of the Supreme Court ruling that denied his plea for a temporary restraining order (TRO) against the enforcement of the International Criminal Court warrant.

He also asked the committee to deny the motion included in the complaint, seeking the suspension of his Senate office’s operations, including the release of salaries and operational expenses.

“In the event the Committee proceeds further, furnish respondent with copies of all records on which it intends to rely, and afford him a hearing, through counsel, with the opportunity to examine the complainants and their witnesses and to present evidence,” he added.

Senate ethics committee chairperson Vicente “Tito” Sotto III confirmed receiving Dela Rosa’s response.

“I received the answer via email on Saturday, November 21, 2026, 8:51 pm. It was submitted through his counsel and not signed by him personally. This answer will be considered in the next Ethics hearing that will be scheduled at the soonest time,” Sotto told reporters in a Viber message.

Dela Rosa’s ICC case

In October, Dela Rosa again asked the SC to reverse its earlier ruling denying his plea for a TRO against the enforcement of the ICC arrest warrant.

Dela Rosa is among the former officials of the Rodrigo Duterte administration implicated in the bloody anti-drug campaign, which human rights organizations say resulted in nearly 30,000 deaths.

The ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I issued an arrest warrant against the senator in November 2025 over his alleged role in the drug war. The court identified him as a co-perpetrator in the case, saying those involved “controlled a structure of power” that enabled them to “direct and control the actions” of those who carried out the killings.

The warrant remained under seal until May 11 of this year, when it was made public.

Dela Rosa had been absent from the Senate for months before appearing on May 11 to support Senator Alan Peter Cayetano’s bid for the Senate presidency. He then remained inside the Senate building for three days as he sought refuge from possible arrest.

A shooting incident erupted on the night of May 13, allegedly triggered by Senate Sergeant-at-Arms Mao Aplasca, Dela Rosa’s Philippine Military Academy classmate. Hours later, at around 2:30 am, Dela Rosa left the Senate building, accompanied by his political ally, Senator Robin Padilla.

Dela Rosa has since stayed out of public view.

In seeking a reconsideration of the SC ruling, Dela Rosa’s lawyer argued that the enforcement posture against the senator had “escalated” while the motion remained unresolved.

The motion also cited developments since the original petition, including the Department of the Interior and Local Government’s declaration of Dela Rosa as “armed and dangerous” and the P50-million bounty offered for his arrest. – Rappler.com

articles.title: COP flop triggers backlash in Australia; Pacific nations express despair
articles.summary:
The finger-pointing to assign blame for the collapse of UN climate talks in Turkey began on Monday, November 23, with calls for the resignation of the Australian minister leading them, while the Pacific island nations most at risk expressed their despair over the failure of countries to collectively address global warming.

For the first time since the 2009 meeting in Copenhagen, the COP climate conference could not reach a final agreement from its talks after the EU and others rejected a final deal that did not include any mention of fossil fuels’ role in global warming because of pressure from Saudi Arabia and other oil-producing nations.

This was the first meeting since the UN’s environmental body confirmed global temperatures were set to exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) level scientists have said will cause extreme weather impacts to intensify, and the lack of collective action has increased a sense of impotence around the multilateral COP process.

Turkey hosted the latest talks, called COP31, in Antalya but shared leadership with Australia. Australian Energy Minister Chris Bowen was the COP31 president of negotiations, and opposition politicians in his home country blamed him for the failure.

“This energy minister’s got to go because he’s a complete and utter failure,” Angus Taylor, a member of the Australian parliament who leads the opposition, told reporters on Monday.

“Chris Bowen was responsible for it. He should go,” Taylor said.

Speaking after the COP31 talks, Bowen blamed the very strong red lines many parties had on climate change.

Inside the Australian parliament, other opposition members asked Prime Minister Anthony Albanese why he would not sack Bowen after the country had spent A$150 million ($99.23 million) on COP31. Albanese did not comment directly on whether he would ask Bowen to step down.

“We believe that climate change is real. We believe in the science,” Albanese said. “Whether it’s environmental security or national security, we act in Australia’s national interest.”

Multilateral process

The COP31 talks began on November 9, but the lack of a final agreement extended the summit to a record overtime on Sunday, November 22. There was already some contention before their start as Australia, which has been at the forefront of efforts to act against global warming, fought with Turkey over hosting duties.

More than 190 countries were represented, and more than 92,000 people had registered, making it provisionally the largest UN climate conference on record. The United States did not send a delegation.

Last year’s talks in Belém, Brazil, produced a deal but no commitment to phase out fossil fuels.

China is the world’s biggest emitter of carbon dioxide, the main cause of global warming, and a spokesman for the country’s foreign ministry, Guo Jiakun, expressed disappointment at the COP31 outcome during a news conference on Monday but said it “should not lead to a loss of confidence in multilateral process.”

Guo added that addressing climate change is a “shared undertaking for humanity” and the global trend toward low-carbon development is “irreversible.”

Bhupender Yadav, who led India’s delegation at COP31, said India engaged constructively and tirelessly with the presidencies and other parties.

“While concerns remain over certain elements of the cover decision, we remain committed to dialogue and constructive engagement until the very end to build consensus,” he said.

Most Pacific island nations, which are facing rising sea levels and other existential threats from climate change, expressed deep disappointment.

“We have been let down on all sides,” the delegation from the Marshall Islands at COP31 said in a statement.

Tuvalu, the Pacific island nation that hosted a pre-COP event in October highlighting its exposure to rising sea levels, called out the absence of engagement and transparency in trying to reach a decision on a final statement.

“Listening to parties who diminish the credibility of signs of climate change is disappointing,” said Maina Talia, Tuvalu’s climate minister, expressing concern about the lack of commitment to put the world back on track for the global temperature goal. – Rappler.com

$1 = 1.5117 Australian dollars

articles.title: Duterte’s drug war was state-sanctioned, killed over 8,000 – Truth Commission
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – A week before former president Rodrigo Duterte’s historic trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC) on November 30, a local truth commission released its initial report on his war on drugs.

The Philippine Truth and Reconciliation Commission (Truth Commission) said on Monday, November 23, that the so-called drug war was systemic and inflicted by Duterte’s government on thousands of victims.

“Preliminary, but enough to say plainly [that] the killings were state-organized. The official account cannot be accepted at face value. In the cases families brought to us, no one has been held to account,” said Truth Commission chairperson and former ICC judge Raul Pangalangan.

“When killings jump in the weeks after a president tells police he will protect them if they kill, when they fall almost to nothing each time the police are pulled out of the campaign, and when they continue through Christmas and All SoulsDay, the pattern points away from chance and toward policy,” the commission said in its report.

Duterte’s campaign promise in 2016 was to eliminate illegal drugs and criminality.

After he was sworn in as the 16th president in July, he immediately launched his drug war led by the Philippine National Police (PNP) and now fellow ICC co-accused, Senator Bato dela Rosa.

On his first day as president on July 1, 2016, Duterte told the PNP that even if they killed a thousand people in line of their duty, he will protect them.

Must Read

Duterte to PNP: ‘Do your duty and I will die for you’

Launched in May, the Truth Commission seeks to provide credible documentation of the killings linked to Duterte’s drug war. It held truth-telling sessions with the victims’ families to humanize drug war victims, analyze evidence, and demand accountability and reforms. Some of the findings came from these sessions, as well as from other sources.

On Monday, the commission said there were 8,230 people killed in the drug war, based on its initial count. This number is much higher compared to the government’s count.

“The governments most cited figure, 6,252, covers only deaths in police and PDEA (Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency) operations. The 12,000 to 30,000 range cited by the ICC Prosecutor draws on several published estimates. These figures count different things; no consensus exists on the number of the dead,” the commission explained.

Apart from the initial count, the commission also released the following key findings:

96.6% of the victims were men in their working and parenting years.

More than half or 56% of the killings were in Metro Manila and Central Luzon

Killings fell when police were pulled out from drug war operations.

24 of 46 exhumed victims had been shot in the head, while many killings bear the marks of execution.

People arrested during the drug war campaign remain in congested jails and prisons.

Play Video

The Truth Commission said its initial report will be available to everyone, including the Philippine government. Pangalangan said these findings will be shared to anyone who will find it useful, even national and international government and nongovernmental organizations.

Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, who served as one of the reactors during the Truth Commission’s event, said they will look into the findings once transferred to the Department of Justice.

“These administrative investigations…. These are these are technically not final and definitive, right? As the pieces of evidence come along or made available, right? You adjust based on what’s…the truth and what’s available,” Vida said in a mix of Filipino and English.

Duterte has been detained in The Hague, the Netherlands, since March 2025 after he was arrested due to crimes against humanity. His case stemmed from his drug war and the killings allegedly committed by the Davao Death Squad.

On November 30, the former president will be the first Asian head of state to face a trial due to crimes against humanity before the ICC. – Rappler.com

articles.title: AI cheating puts Korea's decades-old exam system under scrutiny
articles.summary: Korea’s decades-old testing system, especially the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), is facing growing scrutiny amid fears of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered cheating. However, even as calls for reform grow, proposed changes face practical hurdles and offer no guarantee of preventing increasingly sophisticated AI-driven cheating. President Lee Jae Myung's call on Friday for a swift overhaul of the national testing system accelerated efforts to move beyond multiple-choice exams and introduce written response and essay-based questions to Korea's high-stakes college entrance exam. In August, the National Education Commission presented Lee with a plan to consider introducing absolute grading and written response and essay-based questions to the CSAT. The commission has since sought public input, including through discussions with its citizen participation committee. However, experts warn that changing the exam format alone would do little to stop AI-assisted cheating. articles.summary: South Korea will offer rewards of up to 500 million won ($370,888) for reporting cheating on the annual college entrance exam, the anti-corruption agency said Monday, as authorities step up efforts to crack down on cheating aided by artificial intelligence (AI). The government will offer 100 million won for each tip-off that leads to the detection of a cheating case, up to a maximum of 500 million won, according to the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission (ACRC). Those who confess to cheating and report accomplices will also receive the full reward, while facing reduced penalties for their own misconduct, the commission said. "The measure is aimed at safeguarding the fairness and credibility of the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) by encouraging the public to report cheating," it said. The commission is accepting reports of cheating through Jan. 19 as part of a two-month campaign. articles.title: Naqvi complicated provinces debate by 'irrelevant speech at irrelevant forum', says Rana Sanaullah
articles.summary:
PML-N Senator Rana Sanaullah on Monday said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi “complicated” the matter of creating new provinces by making an “irrelevant speech at an irrelevant forum”.

In his fresh remarks, Sanaullah stood by his criticism of the interior minister’s choice to start the debate on provinces while addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit in Islamabad in July. Naqvi had whipped up a political storm by calling for creating new administrative units in the country to “reset” the current “system” of governance.

Following recent remarks by his predecessor, Naqvi, without naming Sanaullah, warned, “The day I comment on this minister, he will not be able to show his face.”

Subsequently, appearing on Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath’ on Monday, Sanaullah said it was his right as a colleague and as a political worker to express his opinion on Naqvi’s work.

Sanaullah, also the prime minister’s political adviser, contended that Naqvi’s decision to make the remarks at the business forum “complicated this issue, and today this matter is in such a state that it has become extremely controversial”.

“And now if it comes to Parliament, it will arrive in a controversial state,” the senior politician observed, affirming that his party will make all possible efforts to build a consensus.

“There should have been a very healthy discussion on this issue. [But] he chose the wrong method, the wrong procedure, the wrong forum, and then made such a speech right at its inception that the whole system collapsed,” Sanaullah said, observing that those remarks had diverted attention away from the actual debate of new provinces.

In a noteworthy observation, Sanaullah seemed to back PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s stance that the system was “made to collapse”.

Asked about his comments from Aug 1, Sanaullah said: “No, this is not a personal matter. When he said that the system has collapsed, I do not accept this notion. I believe that the system did not fail or collapse; it has been made to fail, it has been collapsed.

“In making it fail, politicians, political parties, the establishment, our worthy judges and the judiciary, [and] bureaucratic circles have played a part. All of us together have made it fail. There is no flaw in the system, nor has it collapsed [on its own]; it has been made to collapse.”

The PML-N leader clarified that it was his “version”, adding: “If someone has another version, that’s fine, let them hold it, but I also have full right to present my stance and speak about it.”

Sanaullah maintained that he never commented on Naqvi’s “personality and thoughts” and never will do so.

“Is he Quaid-i-Azam that for two and a half to three years, I have supposedly been commenting on his personality and thoughts, and it just doesn’t seem to end?” he quipped.

“Whenever I have expressed an opinion, I have done so while keeping his respect and honour in mind. I have never addressed him as anything less than the worthy interior minister,” Sanaullah said, reusing the term from his previous interview.

Upon the programme host asking if he meant “worthy” — following chatter on social media about Sanaullah’s remark — the PML-N leader responded in the affirmative: “Definitely, worthy as in English.”

Expressing his opinion on Naqvi’s July speech, Sanaullah said the interior minister made “completely irrelevant remarks regarding the prime minister”.

He claimed that later, Naqvi also made indirect remarks about the military chief: “Field Marshal is a national asset and a national hero; [but] attributing this kind of talk to him indirectly, that he is a red line and that he does not want to cross it, so I objected to these things.”

The PML-N leader reiterated his stance that the matter of creating new provinces has to come before the Parliament sooner or later.

The PM’s adviser stressed the importance of building consensus among political parties, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached when the matter is debated in the Senate and the National Assembly.

On whether there were still chances for a consensus considering PPP’s objection, Sanaullah said the interior minister “mishandled” the matter and that he should have taken the PPP on board first.

Responding to Naqvi’s reported remarks from a day earlier, Sanaullah questioned what the need was to be “so short-tempered” and issue “threats”.

Asked about other federal representatives, including Khawaja Asif, Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and Tallal Chaudhry, voicing their support for new provinces, Sanaullah said each minister was entitled to their opinion.

“Nothing has been achieved from [discussing] this at forums and seminars, apart from making this issue controversial,” the PML-N senator said.

Sanaullah also commented on Bilawal’s stance that neither he nor his father, President Asif Ali Zardari, had been approached by the government about the matter after the debate began.

“Then what have you (Naqvi) been doing for four months? At the place where you are present all the time, and he (President Zardari) is your benefactor as well and he holds you so dear; if you could not even take him on board, then this is your total failure,” he asserted.

Asked whether his calling Naqvi a “son” of President Zardari was a personal comment, Sanaullah said, “I have personally heard, with these very ears of mine, Zardari sahib say more than once that ‘Mohsin is my son’.”

The programme host said Naqvi was invited to present his response on the show if he wanted to.

articles.title: Pemra bans ads, promotions for commercial infant formula on electronic media
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (Pemra) on Monday banned advertisements and promotional activities for commercially manufactured infant formula milk on electronic media with immediate effect, directing television channels and other regulated broadcasters to stop airing such advertisements.

The ban will remain in force until the required legal compliance and no-objection certificate, approval or permission is obtained from the concerned department or health regulatory body.

According to an order issued by Pemra, the decision was taken following a letter from the Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination dated Nov 18, regarding implementation of the Protection of Breastfeeding and Child Nutrition Ordinance 2002.

The order said that Pemra’s committee deliberated on sections 7, 8 and 9 of the ordinance, which prohibit certain advertisements, promotional activities, distribution of free samples and direct marketing of designated products.

The committee also reviewed relevant provisions of the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan Act 2012, the Pemra Ordinance 2002 and the Pemra Electronic Media (Programmes and Advertisements) Code of Conduct 2015.

Invoking Section 27 of the Pemra Ordinance 2002, the authority declared that “advertisement(s) of infant formula products (commercially manufactured formula powder milk) shall be prohibited forthwith”.

The authority has also referred the matter to its Council of Complaints for recommendations in accordance with the provisions of the Pemra Ordinance.

Pakistan is among the 118 countries that voted in favour of adopting the International Code of Marketing of Breast-milk Substitutes during the World Health Assembly in May 1981.

It enacted a national breastfeeding law in October 2002 in the shape of a presidential ordinance to enforce the code, which also envisaged a National Infant Feeding Board.

The Senate Standing Committee on National Health Services called on Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal earlier this month to enforce the ordinance, warning that weak implementation undermines child health. The committee chairman, Senator Amir Waliuddin Chishti, expressed concern over the law’s lack of enforcement despite being in place for over 20 years.

The Sindh government in August launched World Breastfeeding Week with a renewed commitment to strictly enforce the province’s law against the promotion of infant formula.

Sindh Health and Population Welfare Minister Dr Azra Fazal Pechuho said breastfeeding remained one of the most effective interventions for protecting newborns, improving child nutrition and reducing infant mortality.

articles.title: Petrol price reduced by Rs3 per litre; diesel remains unchanged
articles.summary:
The government on Monday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3 per litre while keeping that of diesel unchanged at Rs357 per litre, after snapping a 12-day streak of consecutive reductions in the rate of petrol the previous week.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs319 per litre on Nov 24 (Tuesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17, the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

articles.title: ‘Rights at stake, not privileges’: Opposition leaders write to SC, FCC, IHC chief justices on Imran, Bushra’s health
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: National Assembly and Senate opposition leaders, Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, on Monday wrote to the chief justices of the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), the Supreme Court (SC) and the Islamabad High Court (IHC), urging them to take notice of the health condition of PTI founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi.

Imran has been in prison since August 2023. The IHC has allowed him twice-a-week meetings — on Tuesdays and Thursdays — with his family, lawyers and other associates. But despite multiple court directives, the PTI founder has been restricted from meeting visitors. Concerns about his health have also arisen in the past year, with the PTI demanding he be given medical treatment by his personal physicians, a demand as yet unheeded by the government.

In an open letter to the same three judges last week, Imran appealed for medical treatment for himself and Bushra Bibi.

Advocate Khalid Yousuf Chaudhry, counsel for the incarcerated PTI founder, told Dawn on Monday that the letter by Achakzai and Abbas urged the SC to convert the application into a petition and hear it as a case of basic human rights.

Chaudhry said the joint letter was written by the opposition leaders in their constitutional capacity by invoking the high judiciary’s jurisdiction and requesting that the letter be treated as a petition for the enforcement of fundamental rights.

It also demanded that a writ of mandamus be issued regarding the non-implementation of the SC’s Aug 18 order for shifting Imran to Shifa International Hospital, and the concerns regarding Imran and Bushra Bibi’s health and detention.

In the seven-page letter, seen by Dawn, the two opposition leaders argued that Imran’s life was in danger in state custody.

“An order of the SC made to protect that life has been flouted and ignored for three months now,” it said.

“The threat to Imran’s life has increased, not diminished.”

Recalling the PTI founder’s open letter on Nov 16 from Adiala jail in which he described being denied fundamental rights and the impact on his health, they demanded that his plea be answered “through a writ of mandamus that compels the state to do what the Constitution and the SC already require of it”.

It said that Imran suffered from cardiac and blood pressure issues, loss of sight and solitary confinement with access largely denied to his lawyers and family and medical recommendations to improve his well-being ignored. In particular, it pointed out that solitary confinement of over 15 consecutive days was prohibited under the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners.

Imran, the letter said, had been held in these conditions for nearly 11 months.

The letter added that Imran’s case was “no longer a domestic matter that the government can wish away”, as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk had taken notice of the issue and called for Imran’s release and proper treatment, as well as defusing of political tensions around the case.

It also recalled that Pakistan, as a party to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights as well as the Convention against Torture, had made these commitments to human rights in its own name and was bound to uphold them.

“The high commissioner’s statement is a warning to the government. It is also a reminder to all of us that the reputation of Pakistan’s institutions, including its courts, is now being judged by how this case is handled.”

The opposition leaders said that the Aug 18 order by the SC was “defeated” within 72 hours: the PTI founder was instead taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), then returned to the jail before dawn, while the ordered medical board was never constituted.

“The hospital and the independent doctors were the substance of the order,” the opposition leaders argued.

“An order to provide independent care is not implemented by providing care that is not independent.”

Now, three months after the order was made, they said, it remained “unimplemented in every essential respect” while Imran’s condition had grown worse, the letter said.

It also highlighted that Bushra Bibi needed a second eye operation to prevent permanent loss of sight and her access to her doctors was being restricted.

“The rights at stake are not privileges of a prisoner. They are guarantees the Constitution makes to every person, which no conviction and no executive convenience can suspend,” the letter stressed.

The letter demanded that the chief justices, within their respective constitutional jurisdictions, “treat this letter as a petition for the enforcement of fundamental rights and issue a writ of mandamus, or such directions as are necessary”, to the federal government, the Islamabad chief commissioner, the Punjab inspector general of prisons and the superintendent of Adiala jail.

They asked that the writ of mandamus direct these authorities to move Imran to Shifa International Hospital within 24 hours and keep him there as long as the medical board advised; to constitute this board “exactly as ordered” and carry out the treatments and investigations it recommended without delay; and to place his examination and treatment under the supervision of his own physician, Dr Faisal Sultan, as well as his sister Dr Uzma Khan, with continuous access and complete medical records to be provided within 24 hours.

In addition, it called for his solitary confinement to be ended immediately and his rights to weekly meetings, regular calls with his family, unhindered access to his lawyers, and access to “books, newspapers and recreation” to be restored, and transferring Bushra Bibi to a specialised eye hospital for her second operation under specialists of her family’s choice and the release of her full medical record to her family and counsel.

The letter also urged that a court officer or local commission be appointed to oversee and report on compliance within seven days; that the pending contempt petition, appeals and applications be fixed for urgent hearing while holding those who “defeated” the Aug 18 order to account; and that the federal government be directed to bring Imran and Bushra’s detention conditions into conformity with Pakistan’s obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights as well as the Convention against Torture.

“Every day that the court’s order remains unimplemented diminishes the authority of the court and the promise of Article 9 and every day it is noticed far beyond our borders,” the letter stressed.

“If harm comes to Imran or to Bushra Bibi in state custody, the responsibility will rest on the state, but history will also ask what the courts did when they were told, in plain words, by the elected representatives of the people in both Houses of Parliament, that a life was at risk.”

Imran and Bushra Bibi’s health

Imran has been in prison since August 5, 2023, while his wife was arrested on January 17, 2025, in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced.

Imran’s eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion — came to light in late January, following which he has been taken to hospital multiple times.

On Aug 18, the SC directed the government to shift the jailed ex-premier to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, a day after the superintendent of the Adiala jail — where Imran is imprisoned — submitted a report to the court on the ex-premier’s health condition.

However, the government took the PTI founder to Pims and subsequently transported him back to prison. At the time, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar had blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside” the hospital for the diversion. The PTI has denied the allegations and accused the government of deliberately flouting the court’s orders.

Meanwhile, Bushra Bibi suffered a retinal detachment in April and was taken to the hospital for surgery. She has since approached the courts seeking an immediate medical examination by an ophthalmologist and permission to receive treatment from doctors of her choice at her own expense amid concerns over her deteriorating eyesight.

According to the former first lady, doctors who examined her had diagnosed her condition as a “mature cataract” and advised that another eye surgery would be required.

articles.title: AB de Villiers makes new claim about Australian 'Sandpapergate' ball-tampering scandal
articles.summary:
Former South African batsman AB de Villiers has alleged that Australia engaged in ball-tampering from the first match of their 2018 “Sandpapergate” tour of South Africa.

De Villiers alleged in a post on his YouTube channel that the ball-tampering, which culminated in Cameron Bancroft being caught using sandpaper in the third Test in Cape Town, actually began in the first Test in Durban.

He also said the Australian bowlers, who have denied any involvement, must have known what was going on.

A fierce debate about the eight-year-old events was triggered in Australia this month when Usman Khawaja claimed the whole team knew about the plot to alter the flight of the ball.

Bancroft, who was banned along with captain Steve Smith and David Warner after the incident, said in a recent article that sandpaper was first used in the second Test in Port Elizabeth.

But De Villiers said: “It started in Durban, by the way, not in PE. I’m very happy for people to quote me on that.

“I see everyone is sort of admitting that in Port Elizabeth it also happened. I can very much tell you Durban was no different, in the first Test.

Go look at the footage. Absolutely no doubt in my mind.”

He added: “We lost that first Test match in Durban with the ball reversing at a very, very interesting time. Way too early for anyone to reverse a ball at Kingsmead. Trust me, I’ve played a lot of cricket there.”

De Villiers added: “So whatever they did there, whether it was sandpaper or [a] nail, I don’t care. The fact of the matter is they were caught and everyone knew. Just stand up and say ‘we were wrong’. A lot is at stake now because they lied.

“The bowlers in particular knew because the ball doesn’t just reverse. It’s not your first Test match for Australia. So just stand up and say, ‘guys, we were wrong’.”

De Villiers was a central figure in a bad-tempered series. He was run out in Durban and Australian bowler Nathan Lyon appeared to drop the ball on him — one of several incidents that inflamed tensions during the series.

The then-South African captain Faf du Plessis revealed in his autobiography that he had persuaded the normally mild-mannered De Villiers to lead an aggressive response in the second Test to what Du Plessis saw as bullying tactics by Australia.

“I spoke to AB and said that the only way we were going to win the series was if he was willing to lead the fight against the Aussies with me. ‘You and I will fight fire with fire. The rest of the team will follow, but only if the two of us lead the charge’.”

Du Plessis wrote that his former schoolmate took up the challenge, not only by aggressively “sledging” Smith but by scoring an outstanding century, which helped South Africa win the match and go on to win the series.

Cricket Australia on Saturday threw its “unanimous support” behind Pat Cummins to remain the current Test captain, rejecting any suggestion his integrity had been compromised by the lingering “Sandpapergate” scandal.

Cummins has been under huge pressure since Khawaja claimed the whole team knew about the ball-tampering plot, but he strenuously denied being aware of what was going on in a press conference last week.

articles.title: 'No national security risk': Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after affair scandal
articles.summary:
Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior US government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal.

The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candour and ability to lead,” the company said in a statement.

Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board.

Nvidia shares surged on the news, jumping more than 25 per cent in premarket trading.

The decision came three days after US President Donald Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance”.

Trump described Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions,” and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart.” Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused.

Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family.

“I can’t wait to get back to work.”

Huang, 63, stepped down on Nov 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia.

US intelligence services reportedly concluded she passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations.

Board chair Harvey Jones said Monday that directors now believe Huang “is the right person to lead Nvidia” and that his return serves the interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers.

Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive who was named Nvidia’s first-ever board chair during the crisis, will stay in the role. Chief financial officer Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, will continue as CFO.

Nvidia said a committee of independent directors set up earlier this month to investigate whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort will see its probe through to the end. Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating, the company said.

Trump, who had previously called on the AI giant to reinstate Huang, congratulated him in a post on Truth Social.

“The Nvidia board of directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy,” he wrote.

The US president clarified that the US government had “no reason” to believe that Huang’s reinstatement posed risks to national security, adding that the US attorney general had confirmed that the government did not possess evidence against Huang.

Trump further said that he had gotten to know Huang, describing him as a “great patriot and national treasure”. Trump directed that Nvidia should continue its internal investigation into compliance with US export controls.

Trump told CNBC on Monday that Huang “didn’t know about” advanced Nvidia chips going to China.

The US president described him as a “genius” and a “brilliant guy”, adding: “Losing the brainpower of somebody like Jensen — to me, that would be a far bigger threat than anything we’re talking about.“

“As far as the woman is concerned, every time you have a Chinese woman that’s good-looking or beautiful, they say she’s a spy. Now with Swalwell, she probably was a spy — but with Jensen, I don’t believe that’s true,” Trump said.

Jack Gold of J. Gold Associates called the reinstatement “a big mistake”, noting that the investigation into whether Huang was compromised by the alleged spy was still under way.

“This action further amplifies the notion that big ‘tech bros’ don’t need to play by the rules like the rest of us do,” Gold said, adding that the board’s decision appeared “driven more by financial influences than ethical practices”.

US Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer vowed to investigate potential wrongdoing surrounding Huang’s reinstatement, accusing Trump of putting personal financial interests ahead of national security.

“Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other Nvidia executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain,” said the veteran New Yorker, who is seen as likely to remain in his position when Democrats take control of Congress in January.

Alice Huang had contact with China spy agency: NYT

Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant’s former chief executive, the New York Times reported on Sunday.

She was in contact with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the intelligence.

According to the Times, Alice Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency correspond to the affair as well as a period when Megaspeed was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips.

The Times also reported that US intelligence agencies have gathered evidence that Alice Huang’s business partner Kang Wei — who the newspaper said was often introduced as her husband — worked with the same Chinese spy agency.

He is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz vows no cap on homes for poor, sets Rs1,000bn disbursement target under Apna Ghar scheme
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday set a target of Rs1,000 billion in disbursements under the Prime Minister Apna Ghar Programme over the next six months.

He declared that there was no limit on the number of homes the government would build for the poor, vowing to construct millions if needed.

Addressing a ceremony held to mark the milestone of over Rs100bn in loans reaching citizens under the scheme, PM Shehbaz said it was a matter of deep concern that while a few enjoy every comfort, a vast number of people are deprived of shelter, education, healthcare and dignified employment.

This, he said, was not the Pakistan envisioned by Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

The premier said that housing schemes in the past had mostly served the elite, who did not need bank loans, while the real need was among labourers, widows, orphans and low-income families across Pakistan, including Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan.

“If the state cannot provide even a roof to such families, it has no right to rule.”

The prime minister recalled that the programme was launched in April 2026.

“In about six and a half months, banks have disbursed Rs112bn against loan sanctions of about Rs500 billion,” PM Shehbaz said, calling this a good start. However, he maintained that the journey ahead is long and must be covered at “lightning speed”.

He directed the finance and housing ministers, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) governor, and banks to aim for Rs1,000bn in disbursements in the next six months.

“Any hurdles and legal impediments will be removed jointly, without exposing banks to undue risk,” he assured the banks.

The premier noted that banks had initially been reluctant to enter this segment because of comfortable returns on treasury bills and government deposits.

He praised those that came forward and said he was told the scheme was free of corruption and nepotism.

The ceremony also featured the presentation of awards to the top five high-performing banks: United Bank Limited Deputy CEO Abdul Aleem Qureshi, Habib Bank Limited President Muhammad Nassir Salim, Bank Alfalah President Atif Bajwa, Meezan Bank Retail Acting CEO/COO Ziaul Hasan, and Mobilink Microfinance Bank Chief Business Officer Attaur Rehman.

Announcing recognition for the top five high-performing banks, he said its leaders would be given blue passports, with a notification to be issued the same day.

He said it would be for each bank’s owners or CEOs to decide who would hold them. He added that the recognition also carries responsibility, as any delay in genuine loan approvals would now be attributed to them.

“An unencumbered and clear title property is the main requirement for a loan, and that other documentation should be handled by banks by helping applicants rather than turning them away,” the prime minister stated.

He said some banks had claimed to be unaware of the scheme, which he described as unacceptable, and urged them to set up dedicated cells.

Responding to the suggestions of the Association of Builders and Developers (Abad) chairman, PM Shehbaz said he welcomed a proposed tripartite coordination involving Abad, the SBP governor, the builders and banks, and directed the finance minister to hold a meeting with the housing minister and housing secretary.

“We want results,” he said, adding he was ready to support the effort if it truly helped build homes.

He thanked Housing and Works Minister Riaz Hussain Pirzada, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema, and SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad for their efforts, and appreciated Information Minister Attaullah Tarar for the publicity.

Abad Chairman Hanif Kohari appreciated the prime minister for turning the housing initiative into a practical programme, and said it had created opportunities for the construction sector.

“Abad, representing about 1,500 members nationwide, is working with the government and banks,” Kohari said. He expressed confidence that the target of 500,000 homes would be met through continued cooperation.

The programme beneficiaries also shared their experiences, including Musarrat Qamar (AJK), Dr Asad Ali (Quetta), Anam Akhtar (Rawalpindi), Jameela Bibi (Rahim Yar Khan), and Karachi couple Babar Zaib and Tayyaba Qazi, along with others from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. They said the financing helped them complete or buy homes after years in rented accommodation.

articles.title: Peshawar to host opening ceremony, inaugural match for 12th edition of PSL: PCB chief
articles.summary:
PESHAWAR: Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) Chairman Mohsin Naqvi said on Monday that Peshawar will host the opening ceremony and the inaugural match for the 12th edition of the HBL Pakistan Super League (PSL) scheduled for next year.

Naqvi made the announcement while addressing a press conference alongside Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi in Peshawar.

“The biggest announcement today, for which I congratulate both the governor and Peshawar Zalmi, is that after 12 years, PSL will hold its opening ceremony and first match in Peshawar,” the PCB chief said.

He added that multiple matches will be held in the provincial capital, with the schedule to be finalised later by PSL.

The 12th edition of the cricket tournament will be held from March 18 to May 2, 2027.

The announcement by Naqvi came shortly after Kundi — whose administration now runs the province under governor’s rule — said the name of Arbab Niaz Stadium would be restored, reversing the PTI government’s decision to rename it to Imran Khan Stadium.

In its press release, PCB stated: “The announcement marks a defining moment for cricket in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and for the thousands of supporters who have followed the league, and their team, from afar since the very first season in 2016.”

The board noted that fans in Peshawar “have filled stands, packed streets and carried their colours across the country for more than a decade, without once watching an HBL PSL match in their own city”.

“That changes with HBL PSL 12. Peshawar’s supporters will finally experience the league’s electric atmosphere at home, with the world’s best T20 talent on show in front of a crowd that has earned its moment,” the statement declared.

“This is a moment the league, and above all the fans of Peshawar, have been looking forward to for 12 years,” PSL Chief Executive Officer Salman Naseer was quoted as saying.

“Peshawar’s love for cricket is unmatched, and HBL PSL 12 will finally give that passion the stage it deserves. Adding a sixth venue is a major step in the growth of the league, and we look forward to delivering a memorable experience for every fan who walks into the stadium.”

Speaking to the media, the PCB chairman noted that Peshawar Zalmi and its owner Javed Afridi had also been wishing for the tournament to come to the city.

Naqvi, also the interior minister, stated that matters related to law and order in the province were “improving very rapidly”.

He recalled that Governor Kundi would call for “reviving cricket in KP” whenever the two met, even before the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in the province on Oct 11.

“This province has produced amazing stars for the cricket team, and I strongly believe that with some promotion and streamlining, […] along with joint efforts, we will see positive results from here in months, not years,” the PCB chief said.

He also announced holding a week-long cricket tournament between the U-19 team, Pakistan Shaheens and the national team.

Peshawar was supposed to host a PSL match on March 28 in the previous edition, but matches were restricted to Karachi and Lahore as part of austerity measures after the US-Iran war broke out.

Asked about that, Naqvi maintained that “best efforts” were made so a match could be staged in Peshawar, but it could not happen due to “purely administrative issues and some concerns”.

He clarified there was no “political reason” for not holding the match, adding that Peshawar was an option for one of the venues but it was not announced as such.

Responding to a query, Naqvi said that there were plans underway to build an academy for tribal districts, with the specifics of its location and construction timeline to be finalised in the next two weeks.

“Those districts are also very important for us,” he affirmed. The merged districts are among the 12 districts where special emergency measures were imposed on Oct 11 as the areas were deemed to face intense security challenges.

Speaking on district-level cricket grounds, Naqvi said the PCB planned to work in collaboration with the government to maintain grounds at “whatever level possible”.

‘Preserving Peshawar’s history’: Kundi on reversing stadium name change

Announcing his administration’s decision to restore Arbab Niaz Stadium’s name, Kundi said on X: “In 13 years, despite KP’s immense sporting talent, the PTI could not build a single new cricket stadium, even though the Pakistan cricket team boasts a significant number of Pathan players. Yet, they were quick to rename the one we already had.”

He contended that the decision was about “preserving Peshawar’s history, respecting its heritage and honouring those who have genuinely contributed to the province’s sporting legacy through their work and achievements”.

The stadium was named after Arbab Niaz, a former federal minister for sports. In Feb 2025, the PTI government in KP, led by then-chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur, renamed it after PTI founder and ex-premier Imran Khan.

Speaking on the matter during Monday’s press conference, Kundi termed the renaming of the stadium as a “huge injustice to the people of Peshawar”.

The governor highlighted that Niaz had the cricket ground built in the 1980s, stating that putting one’s plaques on past projects completed by others was inappropriate.

“If they had built it themselves and named it after him, that would have been fine,” the PPP leader said, adding that the name would be restored within a few days.

Speaking about provincial matters, Kundi reaffirmed that countering terrorism remained the top priority.

He stated that 70 per cent of a Rs160 billion package announced by the federal government will be allotted to the 12 designated districts, while the remaining 30 per cent will go to the rest of KP.

He also highlighted his administration’s crackdown on encroachments and illegal placer gold mining, and a cleanliness campaign.

articles.title: Pakistan has Portugal's 'full support' for GSP+ status, visiting FM says during talks in Islamabad
articles.summary:
Pakistan has Portugal’s “full support” for the European Union’s (EU) GSP+ status, Portuguese Minister of State and Foreign Affairs Paulo Rangel said on Monday during delegation-level talks between the two countries held in Islamabad.

The Portuguese minister arrived in the capital on Sunday on a two-day visit. Pakistan’s current GSP+ status is set to expire in 2027, after which Islamabad will seek a renewal.

GSP+ status is a special incentive awarded to developing countries to “pursue sustainable development and good governance” in exchange for cutting import duties to zero on two-thirds of the tariff lines of their exports.

The status was granted to Pakistan in 2014, resulting in a 108 per cent increase in Pakistani textile exports to the EU due to concessional tariffs.

In October 2023, the European Parliament unanimously voted to extend the GSP+ status for another four years until 2027 for developing countries, including Pakistan.

The upcoming GSP+ monitoring mission will scrutinise Pakistan’s record on 32 international conventions tied to the trade scheme. Maintaining GSP+ status is critical for Pakistan to keep export costs low.

Rangel, in his remarks, stressed that both Pakistan and the EU would mutually benefit from cooperation, adding that “we should not hesitate on developing these bilateral platforms”.

The Pakistani delegation was led by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

In his remarks, DPM Dar said, “Our focus is on strengthening our political ties, expanding bilateral trade and promoting investment.”

He proposed that the two countries regularly convene the Pakistan-Portugal Business Forum to help Pakistani and Portuguese companies “identify trading partners and explore joint venture opportunities”.

He also suggested that the two delegations identify proposals for progress and review implementation through bilateral political consultations.

The two ministers also agreed to set up a joint ministerial commission (JMC) between Islamabad and Lisbon. Dar said the JMC would help promote business, trade and investment between the two countries by identifying the “hurdles” for consideration.

Dar added that he and his Portuguese counterpart agreed that parliamentary exchanges between the two countries should be considered as well.
