Rangel said this was the first visit to Pakistan by a Portuguese delegation in 19 years.

“We look forward to enhancing our bilateral relationship in the economic area,” he said. He elaborated that a JMC would help “boost the economic dynamics of our relationship”.

Rangel praised Pakistan for its role as a “peace-building actor at a global level” as well as its efforts in Middle East diplomacy and the Palestine issue.

The visiting dignitary said that Portugal had a lot to learn from Pakistan, as it enters the United Nations Security Council.

The Portuguese FM added, “We really want to keep this bilateral political dialogue very intense during the two years that we will be holding a mandate in the Security Council of the United Nations because we know how attached Pakistan is to multilateralism, to the Charter of the United Nations, and to building peace and prosperity across the world.”

Referring to Pakistan’s mediation efforts in the US-Iran conflict, Rangel said: “Without your mediation, we are fully aware that things would have been much more difficult than they are.”

He also acknowledged the Pakistani diaspora in Portugal, describing it as a “quite dynamic and well-integrated community”.

Concluding his remarks, the Portuguese FM described his visit to Pakistan as “very fruitful and very positive”.

According to a separate Foreign Office (FO) statement, DPM Dar and Rangel signed an agreement on the mutual exemption of visa requirements for holders of diplomatic passports between the two countries.

“The agreement will facilitate high-level engagement, diplomatic exchanges and further strengthen the longstanding and friendly relations between Pakistan and Portugal,” FO said.

Pakistan values Portugal as important EU partner: President Zardari

The visiting dignitary also met with President Asif Ali Zardari, who said Islamabad values Lisbon as an important partner within the EU and sees “considerable scope for expanding bilateral cooperation in several sectors”, the Presidency said.

President Zardari emphasised the potential to further bolster bilateral ties through greater cooperation in trade, investment, agriculture, labour mobility, renewable energy, education, technology and parliamentary exchanges during the meeting at Aiwan-i-Sadr.

The president highlighted the importance of diversifying bilateral trade beyond traditional textiles and exploring opportunities in agriculture, processed foods, pharmaceuticals, engineering, sports goods and IT services.

He proposed the establishment of a Pakistan-Portugal joint working group on trade and investment to address trade barriers, identify opportunities and facilitate commercial cooperation, the statement added.

President Zardari also highlighted potential for greater collaboration in education, research, technology and sports, including university partnerships, faculty and student exchanges. He welcomed the partnership between FC Porto and Sialkot Football Academy and encouraged further exchanges in coaching, youth tournaments and training programmes.

The president expressed hope for the early finalisation of the proposed memorandum of understanding (MoU) on agricultural cooperation and the establishment of a bilateral technical working group.

He also appreciated Portugal’s support for Pakistan’s GSP+ status and sought continued cooperation for the welfare, integration, consular access and protection of the rights of the Pakistani community in Portugal.

Meanwhile, Rangel described relations between the two countries as “excellent and aligned, emphasising the need to translate this goodwill into stronger economic and cultural cooperation”, according to the Presidency.

He noted that more than 60,000 Pakistanis living in Portugal were well integrated into Portuguese society and highlighted the potential for greater exchanges between the two countries. He also noted that over 600 Pakistani students were studying in Portugal, with dozens benefiting from Portuguese scholarships.

He informed the president that Portugal’s agriculture minister would soon visit Pakistan to explore opportunities for cooperation in the agriculture sector.

The Portuguese delegation included Ambassador of Portugal Paulo Domingues; Ana Coelho, deputy director-general for foreign policy; Filipe Ramalho Ortigão, diplomatic adviser to Rangel; and Caetano Xavier.

The meeting was also attended by Dar, Senator Sherry Rehman, Senator Saleem Mandviwala and the foreign secretary.

PM Shehbaz invites Portuguese investment at business forum

FM Rangel also met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who appreciated Portugal’s acceptance of Pakistan’s offer to establish a JMC for a multisectoral partnership.

According to a statement by the PM Office, the premier noted that the JMC would provide a structured mechanism to identify shared priorities and follow up on practical cooperation.

“The meeting focused on giving fresh political and economic impetus to Pakistan–Portugal relations and expanding cooperation across the full spectrum of bilateral relationship,” the statement said.

PM Shehbaz appreciated Lisbon’s recognition of Islamabad’s role in facilitating regional dialogue and its support for Pakistan’s continued access to the GSP+ scheme.

Both leaders welcomed the Pakistan–Portugal Business Forum, held on the sidelines of the visit, which brought together around 20 Portuguese companies, PMO noted.

The prime minister encouraged Portuguese companies to consider Pakistan’s potential in areas including renewable energy, agriculture and food processing, textiles, technology and tourism.

The two sides discussed strengthening political contacts and widening cooperation in trade and investment, agriculture, information technology, textiles, tourism, education, and cultural exchanges.

They also discussed cooperation in agriculture, including olive cultivation, processing and technology transfer, and ways to strengthen links between Pakistani and Portuguese textile institutions, PMO said.

The meeting also covered labour mobility and skills development, academic cooperation, cultural exchanges and regional and international developments.

“The two sides looked forward to working with each other to build on the visit and to deliver concrete outcomes for both countries,” the statement concluded.

Speaking at the Pakistan–Portugal Business Forum, DPM Dar underscored the role of the Special Investment Facilitation Council in facilitating investment, FO said.

He invited Portuguese businesses to explore opportunities in Pakistan and encouraged business communities on both sides to pursue concrete partnerships.

An MoU on investment protection between Pakistan’s Board of Investment and Portugal’s AICEP was also signed at the forum.

“The MoU will provide a framework for strengthening investment cooperation and promoting closer business linkages between the two countries,” FO said.

Pakistan ‘important economic player’ in EU

Later in the day, addressing a joint press stakeout, Rangel underscored Pakistan’s position as an “important economic player” in the European Union, reiterating Lisbon’s support for the country’s relationship with the bloc.

“We have to do everything that we can to [ensure] that we can even become closer and closer,” he said.

At the outset of the press conference, Dar said the two sides had also explored avenues for improving shipping and logistics for exporters in both countries.

Speaking about visa exemption for diplomatic passport holders, Dar hoped that the exemption could be extended to official and regular passports as well.

Dar announced that the two sides will be signing a Memorandum of Understanding on investment protection between Pakistan’s Board of Investment and the Portuguese Trade & Investment Agency (AICEP).

“Together, these arrangements will provide a stronger foundation for closer bilateral engagement and expanded business and investment ties,” he said, adding that the two sides also reviewed progress on the protocol to amend the convention on double taxation.

We agreed to work towards the early conclusion of the other agreements and MoUs under discussion as of today, he added.

Dar also thanked his counterpart for lending support to Pakistan’s GSP+ status.

“The scheme remains a cornerstone of Pakistan-EU economic cooperation. It supports trade, employment and sustainable development in Pakistan,” Dar said, reiterating commitment to implementing relevant international conventions and continued engagement with the EU.

Dar added that the two leaders had discussed expanding legal pathways for migration.

“I invited Portugal to consider our proposed labour mobility partnership. I also flagged the opportunities that Portugal’s Green Path Mechanism could offer to skilled Pakistani workers to meet its requirement of recruitment.”

Dar said that the two countries had discussed ways to expand people-to-people ties as well as research partnerships, cultural exchanges, parliamentary exchanges and tourism.

Here, he welcomed a partnership between FC Porto, a Portugal-based football club, and the Sialkot Football Academy for a training programme.

“We propose building on this partnership through coaching exchanges, youth tournaments, training camps, and cooperation in sports science, and with closer links between clubs and academies in football and other sports,” Dar said.

Dar also congratulated Portugal on its election to the UN Security Council for the 2027-28 term.

Dar added that the discussion with his counterpart also included Pakistan’s “unwavering support” for the Palestinian people as well as the country’s commitment to a peaceful resolution of the dispute in Jammu and Kashmir.

“On Afghanistan, I stressed that Afghan territory must not be used for terrorist activities against any country, particularly Pakistan,” he said.

On India, DPM Dar reiterated the country’s stance on the Indus Waters Treaty and stressed that India’s unilateral decision to hold the treaty in abeyance constitutes a “material breach of international law and a dangerous attempt to weaponise shared water resources”.

Concluding his address, Dar hoped that the two countries can build on their “long-standing friendship [..] to shape a forward-looking partnership”.

Rangel, in his address, described Monday’s engagement as a “landmark” in Pakistan-Portugal relations, expressing “full trust” in the economic dimension of the two countries’ relationship.

He also acknowledged Pakistan’s mediatory role in the US-Iran war.

“Everybody knows in the world the role that your government, your prime minister, and especially the DPM had in this conflict in the Middle East. Things are not fantastic there; they are difficult. But the truth is that they would be much worse without Pakistani mediation and systematic [outreach] to try to bring all sides and all stakeholders to a very reasonable position.”

He also lauded Pakistan’s tripartite defence pact with Turkiye and Saudi Arabia — the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement — as well as the R4+E4 framework with the UK, France, Germany, and Italy.

Rangel stressed the need for expanding ties in culture and economy and invited DPM Dar to visit Lisbon.

Rangel-Dar meeting

Separately, Rangel reaffirmed his country’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations with Pakistan in his bilateral meeting with Dar, the FO said.

Both ministers reviewed the “longstanding and friendly relations between Pakistan and Portugal as the two countries mark 77 years of diplomatic relations”, the FO statement said.

It added that DPM Dar stressed the importance of enhanced diplomatic engagement, parliamentary exchanges and regular consultations through existing bilateral mechanisms.

For his part, Rangel reaffirmed Portugal’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties, thanked Pakistan for its support at the United Nations and appreciated the contribution of the Pakistani diaspora in Portugal to promoting closer ties between the two countries, the statement said.

“Both leaders also exchanged views on regional developments and discussed cooperation at the UN and within the European Union framework,” it said.

Moreover, Rangel appreciated Pakistan’s “constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability”, the statement said, adding that the two leaders also emphasised the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and effective multilateralism in addressing shared challenges.

The FO earlier said companies from both countries would hold business-to-business meetings to explore commercial partnerships and investment opportunities in agri-food, renewable energy, pharmaceuticals, information technology and textiles.

Following his arrival on Sunday, Rangel praised Pakistan’s peace efforts in recent months during the US-Israeli war on Iran.

“The world needs you. We have been seeing in the very recent months that the role of Pakistan is decisive for global peace, so we count on you to help all the peoples of the world, reaching peace and prosperity,” he said while speaking to state-run Pakistan TV.

articles.title: Bilawal calls for restoring supremacy of Parliament and trust in judiciary, electoral system
articles.summary:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Monday called for restoring the supremacy of Parliament as well as trust in the judiciary and the electoral system.

He made the remarks while addressing the inauguration ceremony to mark the launch of the Sindh Youth Card in Karachi.

“To restore the trust of Pakistan’s youth, if any reset is to take place, it must be a democratic reset,” the party leader said.

“If a democratic reset happens, then the people’s stake will remain, and through that reset, we must restore the supremacy of our Parliament. We must restore confidence in our judiciary, and the election system we have, we must restore trust in it now.”

Bilawal’s remarks come as the debate over a “system reset” in the country has intensified over the past few months. In July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stirred a political storm by calling for the creation of new administrative units, arguing that the current system of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

Last week, in a hard-hitting speech, the PPP chairman asserted that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”.

“Every child in this country hates corruption. The youth [of Pakistan] want to see a country where there is no corruption. They want it, and we also want to join together and build such a Pakistan,” he said on Monday.

According to Bilawal, to achieve that objective, two things needed to be done: the first was to use modern digital technology, whether it was the Youth Card or Kissan Card, to build systems that shut down avenues for corruption.

“Along with that, we have to build a system that functions without discrimination,” he added.

“Instead of taking revenge, [the system] works to fix our situation.”

Bilawal stressed that the restoration of trust would have to be a “joint effort” — to restore the opposition’s trust in the government and vice versa, and the public’s trust in the country’s system, its parliament, judiciary and media.

He said if such conditions were created, Pakistan could achieve unity for the first time, enabling it to confront economic hardships, terrorism and climate change-related disasters.

“I know that a Pakistan that is united, [will] have the ability to face any crisis, any disaster, any catastrophe.”

“At the same time, I fear that if we keep fighting among ourselves and remain divided further, and [spread hatred] in society instead of hope, then we will not have the capacity to face any crisis,” Bilawal added.

“Then whatever happens to Pakistan, whatever negative consequences occur, the youth will hold us accountable, asking, ‘You were there, what did you do to save us from this trouble?’ And at least I want when that question is asked, I can proudly, with my head held high, say that my intentions were good,” he said.

The Bhutto scion claimed he had poured his blood and sweat into resolving the nation’s issues.

“I made this effort so conditions would be created in this country enabling us to serve you,” he said.

“And if I succeed, then it will be for the benefit of Pakistanis, for the benefit of our country. Even if I fail, history will remember that a young man stood up and tried.”

At the outset of his speech, Bilawal said he had been a part of Pakistan’s politics for 20 years, during which he maintained ties with all political parties and politicians.

“Given the circumstances we face today, and the position we are in, if I myself am disillusioned, one can only imagine how the people of Pakistan, especially the youth, must feel,” he said.

The inauguration ceremony was attended by Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, Sindh Sports Minister Sardar Mohammad Bux Khan Mahar, and other PPP leaders.

Speaking at the event, CM Murad said the Sindh Youth Card would establish an “effective means of direct engagement” with young people and create a database.

He said that the card had been initially launched for 100,000 young people, with the programme’s scope to be expanded over time.

“With Sindh’s youth population estimated at approximately 13 to 14 million, further measures are being taken, including youth development centres and public-private partnerships, to secure young people’s futures while providing them with better opportunities for growth and a supportive environment,” the CM said.

articles.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang — the indispensable godfather of AI
articles.summary:
Chips designed by Nvidia push the boundaries of artificial intelligence, and its leather-jacket-wearing co-founder Jensen Huang built the company into one of the world’s most important brands over his 33 years at the helm.

Unknown to the public just four years ago, he rapidly emerged as a public entrepreneur, drawing stadium crowds as he presented cutting-edge components essential to the development of AI tools like ChatGPT.

On Nov 12, Huang was forced out of the company when a scandal exploded over his personal life as he admitted to having an affair with a woman who US officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence.

But on Monday, he was reinstated as CEO in a move that underlined his apparently indispensable role in an industry that has fueled a tech revolution and a global economic boom.

Huang, 63, reportedly had an affair with Alice Huang — who is of no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia’s top-line chips.

Only on Sunday, the New York Times added further details to the allegations, saying Alice Huang was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during the secret relationship.

Meteoric rise

California-based Nvidia was catapulted to become one of the world’s most valuable companies by the insatiable appetite for chips known as Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) that it designs.

Its meteoric rise made Huang one of the world’s richest people — worth around $160 billion, according to Forbes — thanks to the roughly four per cent stake he holds in the company he founded three decades ago with two friends in a Silicon Valley diner.

He has become a close informal adviser on AI to Donald Trump, travelling with the US president on Air Force One to Beijing earlier this year.

That is an area of concern to US officials who believe he has been involved with the alleged spy, Alice Huang.

The drama of recent weeks is a long way from Jensen Huang’s birth in Taipei in 1963, and his life embodies the American success story.

At nine years old, he was sent away with his brother to boarding school in small-town Kentucky.

His uncle recommended the school to his Taiwanese parents, believing it to be a prestigious institution, though it was actually a school for troubled youth.

Too young to be a student, Huang boarded there but attended a nearby public school alongside the children of tobacco farmers. With his poor English, he was bullied and forced to clean toilets — a two-year ordeal that transformed him.

“We worked really hard, we studied really hard, and the kids were really tough,” he recounted in an interview with US broadcaster NPR.

But “the ending of the story is I loved the time I was there”.

Brought home by his parents, who had by then settled in the northwestern US state of Oregon, he graduated from university at just 20 and joined AMD, then LSI Logic, to design chips — his passion.

Megastar in Taiwan

He wanted to go further and founded Nvidia in 1993 to “solve problems that normal computers can’t,” using semiconductors powerful enough to handle 3D graphics, he said during an interview on the “No Priors” podcast.

Nvidia created the first GPU in 1999, riding the intersection of video games, data centres, cloud computing and now generative AI.

Always dressed in a black T-shirt and leather jacket, Huang sports an Nvidia logo tattoo and has a taste for sports cars.

One former high-ranking Nvidia employee described him to AFP as “the most driven person” he’d ever met.

He has rejected calls to deliberately slow down AI development even as some insiders warn the technology could threaten human existence within a decade.

“That kind of narrative is dramatic; it gets a lot of attention,” but “it’s not grounded in facts,” he told CBS News in September.

“We should go as fast as we can” on AI, he said.

On visits to his native Taiwan, Huang is received like a megastar, with fans crowding him for autographs and selfies as journalists follow him to the barber shop and his favourite night market.

Nvidia had taken care to project a drama-free image of Huang.

But the former employee described a “very paradoxical” individual, protective of his employees but also capable, within Nvidia’s executive circle, of “ripping people to shreds” over mistakes or poor decisions.

articles.title: MQM-P to deliberate on PPP’s request to postpone Nov 29 Karachi rally, says Farooq Sattar
articles.summary:
Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) leader Dr Farooq Sattar said on Monday that the party would deliberate on a PPP request to postpone its Nov 29 rally in Karachi, to be held in support of new provinces.

MQM-P had earlier this month announced the rally on Sharea Faisal as part of the party’s campaign for new administrative units. However, Sindh Taraqqi-pasand Party (STP) had also announced its own gathering against new provinces on Sharea Faisal on the same day.

Last week, MQM-P leader Mustafa Kamal had hinted that his party would not hold its planned rally as it does not want any confrontation. STP chief Dr Qadir Magsi on Saturday refused to postpone his party’s rally.

Speaking to the media after a meeting between the two parties at the Sindh Assembly, Sattar said the PPP had clarified that it was not opposed to any political or democratic gathering, public meeting or rally.

“They said that if you choose another date, we will extend our cooperation and permission will also be granted. However, our wish is that you postpone the rally scheduled for Nov 29,” he said.

Sattar said the PPP’s concern was that no one should take advantage of the prevailing situation.

“Given the current atmosphere, where many people are saying many things, people’s sentiments should not be hurt, no one should be offended, and a situation should not arise that could later become a major challenge for the government,” he added.

“We told them we will deliberate on this,” he said; however, he pointed out that postponing closer to the date would be a “difficult decision”.

Earlier, a delegation of the PPP arrived at the Sindh Assembly to meet the MQM-P leadership.

The PPP delegation comprised Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar, Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah, Nisar Khuhro and Waqar Mehdi.

From the MQM-P side, Sattar, Sindh Assembly Opposition Leader Ali Khurshidi and members of the provincial assembly participated in the meeting.

The two sides discussed the prevailing political situation in the province and matters of mutual interest.

Monday’s meeting came amid tensions between the two parties over the MQM-P’s demand for the creation of new provinces.

Last week, the local government minister had rejected the demand, saying it reflected the MQM-P’s political frustration and failure to regain public support. He urged the party to stand with the people of Sindh in protecting the province’s unity rather than calling for its division.

His remarks came after Kamal called for the creation of new provinces, saying December would be crucial for major decisions on the issue. He had also said a referendum would be held on the establishment of new provinces.

The MQM-P has repeatedly criticised the PPP-led Sindh government over its handling of Karachi’s affairs, including the city’s population count and allocation of resources.

The disagreement intensified after PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari warned that dividing Sindh could lead to bloodshed on its streets. His remarks, made during a speech in which he also called for a “political reset”, drew criticism from MQM-P leaders and other political parties.

MQM-P chief Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui subsequently urged the courts and the federal government to take notice of Bilawal’s remarks, saying his party expected to be countered with arguments rather than threats. He maintained that the MQM-P’s demand for new provinces was not limited to Sindh or Karachi but extended to the entire country.

Siddiqui also questioned the PPP’s opposition to the creation of new provinces, alleging that Karachi’s contribution to Sindh’s budget was behind the party’s resistance. He said the MQM-P would continue its constitutional and legal struggle through the assemblies.

Bilawal, however, later clarified that his remarks were not a threat but a warning about the possible reaction to any attempt to divide Sindh.

articles.title: Building near Karachi Press Club evacuated due to hoax bomb threat
articles.summary:
KARACHI: A bomb threat at a building near Karachi Press Club (KPC) drew a response from multiple authorities on Monday but was found to have been a hoax, according to police.

Rangers, police and rescue teams rushed to the scene after receiving information that explosive material had been placed at Lakson Square Building No. 2, located opposite the main gate of KPC.

The building was vacated and after a thorough search by bomb experts, it was declared safe.

Deputy Inspector General (South) Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that the building management had received a threat via email that explosives had been placed.

He said the police, Rangers, Rescue 1122 and Bomb Disposal Squad teams rushed to the site. He said that two teams of bomb experts conducted a search of the building premises and found it to be a hoax call.

The South police chief said the bomb experts searched the building completely from the first to the 10th floor, in the presence of the building security staff and the local police.

Other areas of the building were also searched in response to the bomb threat, but no detonating or explosive material was found, he said.

Raza said the police were investigating the case further.

Earlier this month, a train was stopped and evacuated at Punjab’s Khanpur Railway Station following a threat that a bomb was planted on the Peshawar-bound Khyber Mail, travelling from Karachi.

According to the railway authorities, a suspicious bag was reported in one of the coaches of the train but no bomb or explosive material was found.

articles.title: Let's get digital: Punjab introduces on-screen marking system with facial recognition for board exams
articles.summary:
LAHORE: The Punjab government has introduced a digital on-screen marking system with facial recognition to check examination papers in an effort to modernise the process and improve transparency across the province’s nine boards for intermediate and secondary education.

Under the system, students’ handwritten answer scripts will be scanned using advanced scanners and uploaded to a digital platform, where examiners assess them online through a real-time dashboard.

Punjab Minister for School and Higher Education Rana Sikandar Hayat announced the initiative in a post on X on Sunday, saying facial recognition technology would be used to verify examiners’ identities.

The system will automatically lock if it detects more than one face or the presence of an unauthorised person during the marking process, Hayat said.

He said artificial intelligence and digital monitoring would help make the examination process more transparent, secure and efficient.

Talking to Dawn, the chairman of the Lahore Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dr Badar, said the digital marking system was being implemented in the ongoing second annual examinations across Punjab.

He said officials of the Lahore board had developed the system and shared its technology and software with other education boards in the province to facilitate its implementation.

The Lahore board had also provided training to staff of other boards to enable them to operate the system, he added.

Dr Badar said the system would also be used in the next annual examinations, with all science subjects to be assessed through the digital platform.

He said the board was taking steps to modernise the system and make the entire examination and assessment process more transparent.

Under the digital assessment framework, answer scripts can be divided into individual questions or portions and assigned to different subject specialists.

This allows multiple examiners to assess different answers in the same script instead of one examiner checking the entire paper.

The system is also intended to bring greater uniformity to marking through standardised assessment criteria and digital monitoring of examiners.

Other measures outlined under the programme include biometric verification of candidates, digital attendance management, security features in question papers and changes to the assessment of practical examinations.

The government also plans to expand digital marking to major science subjects, including physics, chemistry, biology, mathematics and computer science, at matriculation and intermediate levels.

The reforms are aimed at reducing inconsistencies in manual marking, strengthening accountability and ensuring that students’ performance is assessed through a more standardised process, according to Dr Badar.

Earlier this year, it was reported that students appearing in the 2026 matriculation and intermediate exams in Punjab would be verified through digital biometric attendance, a first in the province, aimed at eliminating impersonation and strengthening transparency.

articles.title: Pakistan, Malaysia reaffirm commitment to strengthening bilateral defence ties: ISPR
articles.summary:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Monday reaffirmed their shared commitment to strengthening bilateral defence ties, the military’s media affairs wing said.

The development came as CDF Munir undertook an official visit to Malaysia, where he called on PM Ibrahim in Putrajaya, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement.

It said that the visit was aimed at further strengthening bilateral defence and military cooperation between the two countries.

“The meeting focused on bilateral relations, defence and security cooperation, and evolving regional and global security dynamics.

“Both leaders exchanged views on matters of mutual interest and underscored the importance of sustained engagement to promote regional peace, stability and security,” ISPR said.

According to the statement, the Malaysian premier “warmly welcomed” CDF Munir and acknowledged the “longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual trust and cooperation between Pakistan and Malaysia”.

“He reaffirmed Malaysia’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations, particularly in the fields of defence and security,” it stated.

Meanwhile, CDF Munir appreciated Malaysia’s constructive role in promoting peace and stability in Southeast Asia and reiterated Pakistan’s resolve to further deepen defence cooperation and institutional linkages between the Armed Forces of both countries, the statement said.

“Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to strengthening bilateral defence ties through regular high-level exchanges, enhanced military cooperation and sustained dialogue on regional and international security issues,” the ISPR said.

The statement added that CDF Munir also held a meeting with Malaysian Defence Minister Mohamed Khaled bin Nordin.

“Both sides discussed matters of mutual interest, with particular emphasis on expanding bilateral defence cooperation, strengthening military-to-military engagements and exploring new avenues of collaboration between the armed forces of the two countries,” it said.

Upon arrival at the Ministry of Defence in Kuala Lumpur, CDF Munir was accorded a ceremonial guard of honour, it said. The statement added that Malaysian Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Haji Malek Razak Sulaiman, along with the chiefs of the Malaysian Army, Royal Malaysian Navy and Royal Malaysian Air Force, were present on the occasion.

The ISPR said that CDF Munir would also visit the National Defence Studies Centre, where a formal ceremony would be held to induct him as the 21st member of its prestigious Hall of Fame.

articles.title: Naqvi calls on PM Shehbaz as debate on new provinces gains steam
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD/LAHORE: Amid growing debate on the issue of creation of new provinces, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

According to an official handout from the Prime Minister Office (PMO), the interior minister met the prime minister in Islamabad and briefed him on the law and order situation in the country.

The two also discussed the prevailing situation in the country, the statement said.

Earlier in the day, Naqvi had met with Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) chief Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain at his residence in Lahore. The debate over the creation of new provinces and devolution of powers came under discussion during the meeting.

The meetings came amid an ongoing political debate over the creation of new provinces, with several political leaders pushing for a nationwide referendum to settle the matter.

It was sparked by Naqvi’s July remarks, wherein he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

In Monday’s meeting, Naqvi and Shujaat discussed the overall political situation, measures to maintain law and order and the need to transfer power to the grassroots level, according to a statement issued by the interior ministry after the meeting.

During the discussion, Shujaat said the question of creating new provinces was directly linked to public convenience, good governance, administrative efficiency and the country’s future.

“Strengthening existing administrative units and making them more empowered can also be an effective way to address governance-related challenges. The biggest stakeholders of Pakistan are its ordinary people,” Shujaat was quoted as saying, adding that decisions should be made in accordance with the aspirations of the people.

“If we do not take steps in the right direction today, tomorrow will not forgive us,” he remarked.

Naqvi said it was imperative to take all decisions in accordance with the wishes of the people of Pakistan. The interior minister also briefed the PML-Q leader on the government’s counterterrorism and peacekeeping measures in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain and Punjab Minister for Industries Chaudhry Shafay Hussain were also present at the meeting.

Last week, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry insisted that a referendum on the formation of new provinces “will happen” amid the debate on new provinces.

In his remarks on Friday, Chaudhry had maintained that the PML-N would undertake “every last effort” to convince the PPP.

“A referendum is neither non-constitutional nor undemocratic; the public’s opinion can be sought on any important matter,” he had said.

Chaudhry’s remarks came after PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari delivered a no-holds-barred speech earlier last week that covered the question of new provinces.

Bilawal had expressed his opposition to Sindh’s division for any new province, as well as to the idea of holding a referendum for such a move. He cautioned that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly in Sindh, could lead to bloodshed.

However, the federal government maintains that a referendum is a legal and constitutional method of gauging public opinion on new provinces and that no political party should have reservations regarding it.

articles.title: PTI's Zafar says Karachi can become separate province, Imran Khan favours new administrative units
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: PTI parliamentary leader in the Senate, Barrister Ali Zafar, on Monday said that Karachi – Pakistan’s most populous metropolis – could be made a new province, claiming that party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan was in favour of it.

However, Zafar stressed that it should be done in accordance with the Constitution, as the referendum, albeit constitutional, was only to seek the public’s opinion.

Days ago, PTI’s Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram had dismissed proposals for a referendum as an absurd and futile exercise that could not replace a majority vote or a constitutional bill in the national or provincial assemblies.

The PML-N-led federal government has insisted on holding a referendum across the country on the establishment of new provinces or administrative units. However, the suggestion has faced severe backlash from its ally PPP.

Speaking to the media outside Islamabad High Court on Monday, Zafar said the PTI was waiting for legislation on the creation of new provinces to be presented.

“We will make our decision after analysing the draft of the 28th amendment,” he stated. While rumours of making changes to the Constitution have been circulating since at least May, a possible 28th amendment has not been officially proposed yet.

Zafar said that the PTI founder had given a “straightforward instruction” regarding the formation of new provinces.

“He (Imran) has said that as long as provinces are concerned, they should be made,” the PTI’s leader in the Senate said.

However, Zafar cautioned that it should be observed how “they” want to make the provinces. “We will look into it – whether they want to violate the law or follow the law – and then will decide about it,“ he stated.

“Khan sahib has said that whenever you get the draft, look into it […] and then come to me and share its pros and cons,” he added.

While replying to a question, Barrister Zafar noted that a referendum was a constitutional way to get the opinion of the masses. However, he stressed that only public opinion could be sought through it and provinces must be created in the way “already mentioned in the Constitution” — with the relevant provincial assembly’s consent.

Turning to another question, Zafar said that PTI was a political party and the opinion of Imran would be sought if it is asked to vote on new provinces.

Zafar said that while provinces could be established in Sindh, he personally believed that they should be made on an administrative basis rather than a linguistic basis.

Moreover, he said it should be analysed whether those provinces can generate enough revenue and can be run on their own.

“Karachi can be made a province. Similarly, interior Sindh and central Sindh can become provinces. In Punjab, south and north Punjab can become provinces. Similarly, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the Hazara region can become a province,” he suggested.

“We just want justice and if the government is ready to give justice, we are ready to talk about it,” he said, referring to the court orders related to shifting Imran to the hospital and providing access to his family and lawyers.

The PTI has maintained that its founding chairman has consistently advocated for smaller administrative units; however, the party says it would never endorse decisions imposed without “constitutional legitimacy, democratic consensus, and public consent”.

In September, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan cautioned against making any “hasty decision” regarding the creation of new provinces, saying it would weaken the federation.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has whipped up a political storm since July, when he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

On Nov 12, Naqvi floated the idea of holding a referendum to gauge public opinion on the issue, saying the exercise could settle the contentious debate once and for all.

Other federal ministers have also voiced their support for holding a referendum, with Defence Minister Khawaja Asif saying the process could likely move forward early next year.

articles.title: Analysis: Myanmar genocide judgment may bolster Gaza case against Israel
articles.summary:
The International Court of Justice’s landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya will strengthen South Africa’s genocide case against Israel over the war on Gaza, legal experts said, establishing a precedent that genocidal intent can coexist with a military objective.

While the conflicts in Gaza and Myanmar are legally distinct, both cases before the World Court are based on allegations that states breached their obligations under the 1948 Genocide Convention.

On Thursday, the court found that Myanmar had violated the convention on multiple grounds stemming from mistreatment of the Muslim Rohingya minority by the armed forces.

South Africa, which has brought a genocide case against Israel over its conduct in Gaza, welcomed the judgment.

Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola said it set an important precedent by establishing for the first time that a state had committed genocide.

He said it was of “great significance” to the case against Israel, which is not expected to be argued until 2029.

Both Myanmar and Israel have defended the actions of their armed forces as legitimate responses to insurgencies.

But a majority of nine judges on the 15-member bench found that around 10,000 killings, including of children, the razing of homes, widespread sexual violence and the forced exodus of more than 700,000 people in 2017 amounted to state-sponsored genocide.

The ruling also handed other major legal victories to Gambia, which brought the case seven years ago on behalf of Muslim-majority countries.

The judges found that Myanmar had failed in its obligation to prevent genocide and said it must facilitate the return of Rohingya refugees and pay unspecified reparations.

The court also adopted conclusions from UN fact-finding reports, including one stating that mass deaths and rapes showed genocidal intent.

Important precedent

Israeli legal scholar Yuval Shany said the ruling could broaden the arguments available to South Africa in its case against Israel.

He said the court maintained a requirement that genocidal intent be the “only reasonable inference,” but expanded the contextual factors it can consider beyond a pattern of conduct, to include the scale and systematic nature of acts and the history of persecution.

The approach “gives South Africa more avenues to argue for genocide” in Gaza, Shany said.

Proving genocide is notoriously difficult because it requires establishing an “intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group, as such.”

Five criminal acts can constitute genocide: killing members of a group, causing them serious bodily or mental harm, creating conditions calculated to destroy them, preventing births, or forcibly transferring children to ​other groups.

Lamola said South Africa would study the judgment carefully with a view to demonstrating, as the court had in the Rohingya case, that a state’s actions, including ethnic cleansing, the killing of children, sexual violence and destruction of civilian infrastructure, can fall within the definition of genocide.

Targeting of children, women

Another aspect of the ruling that could resonate in the Israel case was the court’s emphasis on the systematic nature and scale of the crimes committed in Myanmar, said Marieke de Hoon, professor of international criminal law at the University of Amsterdam.

South Africa alleges that Israel’s military operations created conditions intended to prevent births and disproportionately affected women and children in Gaza.

In its filing to the ICJ, it said an estimated 70 per cent of those killed were non-combatants. Israel rejects those allegations and says its operations have been conducted in accordance with international law.

“Arguments that a military intent or military objective would erase the idea that there could be a genocide intent are now rejected by the court,” said De Hoon.

She said the judges found that some acts, including attacks on children and women and sexual violence, could not be explained by military objectives alone, leaving genocide as the only reasonable inference.

The Hague Initiative for International Cooperation (Thinc), a think tank funded by pro-Israeli groups, said the judgment would fundamentally alter how courts assess allegations of genocide by imposing a “lower threshold for proving genocidal intent, with serious consequences for Western militaries engaged in confronting terror”, such as after Hamas’s Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

It is “not only a verdict in a particular case but a template”, Thinc’s director, Andrew Tucker, wrote in a reaction.

“Its propositions will be used in future cases: that genocidal intent may coexist with legitimate military objectives…that UN reports compiled without access can carry decisive weight; and that a state can breach the duty to prevent genocide without any finding that genocide occurred.”

While the World Court judgment unequivocally found Myanmar responsible for genocide, proving the crime in court remains difficult, said Richard Horsey, senior adviser for Asia at the International Crisis Group.

“The ICJ has never before found that a state committed genocide. The legal bar is extremely high, but what this case shows is that it is surmountable,” he said.

articles.title: 7 killed, 2 injured as stone-laden truck overturns onto mini-truck in Bahawalpur
articles.summary:
LAHORE: Seven people were killed and two others were injured when a stone-laden truck hit a mini-truck and overturned onto it in Bahawalpur’s Uch Sharif early on Monday morning, an official and Rescue 1122 said.

Bahawalpur District Police Officer (DPO) Rana Abdul Wahab told Dawn that the mini-truck, travelling from Dera Ghazi Khan to Khairpur Tamewali, was carrying 16 people and stopped along a highway due to fog.

“The driver was cleaning the windscreen of the stationary vehicle when another truck, laden with stones, hit it and turned over onto it,” the DPO said.

According to the official, the driver of the stone-laden truck, which was also travelling from Dera Ghazi Khan, had lost control of the vehicle.

Passengers in the mini-truck were left trapped, he said.

A Rescue 1122 statement said the passengers were trapped under the truck and the stones, and an excavator was used to clear the stones.

The DPO said police and rescue personnel were able to rescue nine people while seven died because of injuries.

According to Rescue 1122, two people have been injured among those rescued.

DPO Wahab said the driver of the stone-laden truck had fled the scene after the accident. “However, police have identified him and registered a case at Dhoorkot police station. Raids are being conducted to arrest the suspect,” the DPO said.

Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz expressed “deep grief and sorrow” over the loss of lives in the accident, Associated Press of Pakistan reported.

In a message, the CM extended her “heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the bereaved families,” praying for their strength and patience to bear the “irreparable” loss.

CM Maryam also sought a detailed report on the accident and directed relevant authorities to provide the necessary details, according to APP.

Earlier this month, a collision between a passenger bus and truck claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Pakpattan.

On Oct 21, ten people were killed and 44 others injured when a passenger bus overturned after hitting a road divider on the Indus Highway in Rajanpur district’s Rojhan tehsil.

On Oct 19, a road accident on Multan’s Bosan Road claimed the lives of five men in their 20s after their speeding Toyota Corolla hit a road divider before crashing into the wall of a nearby plot and catching fire.

articles.title: Asif says process for referendum on new provinces likely to move forward early next year
articles.summary:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said discussions on a possible referendum to create new provinces are expected to take a “definitive shape” by the end of this year, with the process likely to move forward early next year.

Speaking on ARY News programme ‘Sawal Yeh Hai’ on Sunday, Asif said the matter would not take long to reach a conclusion, though he refrained from giving a specific date.

Asked whether the PML-N and the federal government had reached a principled decision on holding a referendum, and what its timeline and outline would be, he said: “Perhaps by the year-end, all this debate and discussion that is taking place will take some definitive shape. What shape it will take, I cannot say, but it won’t take long. I can certainly say that it is not going to take two to four months.”

He said the date could be a few days earlier or later, but the process was expected to move forward soon.

“God willing, but it would not be appropriate for me to give a date. I cannot provide a definitive timeline, but, based on my understanding, the inevitability of this is becoming clearer day by day,” he said.

Asked how the referendum question would be framed, given opposition from one province and the fact that previous referendums had been held under dictatorships, Asif said everyone had the right to express reservations.

“You cannot deny someone that right if they have reservations about the entire matter and are expressing them. That is a fundamental part of a democratic society,” he said.

He said a joint document would be prepared with input from all stakeholders to ensure that the proposal was acceptable to everyone.

“It will be a joint document in which all the stakeholders will have their input. Rather than producing a document that falls prey to disagreement, my own view is that the efforts and back-and-forth meetings currently taking place will produce something that is acceptable to all,” he added.

Asked whether the government would seek consensus on the referendum question to bring the PPP on board, Asif said that was precisely the intention.

He said the question would outline the purpose and objectives of the proposed exercise, requiring people to respond with a yes or no. These objectives, he added, would also be defined through consensus.

Regarding the constitutional requirements for holding a referendum, he said the Constitution provided for such an exercise but also laid down the procedure for constitutional amendments, which could not be bypassed.

“There is room for a referendum in the Constitution; there is no doubt about that. However, the procedure for a constitutional amendment is also laid down in it, and no one can deviate from that procedure,” he said.

The defence minister said the proposed changes could have far-reaching positive consequences, noting that Pakistan had previously altered its administrative map through the creation of One Unit and the subsequent establishment of provinces.

He expressed confidence that the joint preparation of a document would address reservations and prevent major disagreements.

“I think politics is the art of the possible, and this will definitely be made possible, God willing,” he added.

Asif had made similar remarks a few days earlier, saying he believed that a consensus was being developed on the creation of new provinces and that the process was moving towards culmination.

Speaking on Geo News, he had said the new year would bring a new system and that reaching consensus could lead to a progressive change in the country’s political landscape. He had also advocated a robust local government system, saying smaller administrative units would help improve public service delivery.

The remarks come amid a debate over the proposed creation of new provinces, with Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry insisting last week that a referendum on the matter “will happen”.

The issue gained renewed attention after PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari opposed the creation of new provinces and the proposed referendum in a speech on Tuesday, warning that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly Sindh, could lead to bloodshed.

The federal government, however, maintains that a referendum is a legal and constitutional means of gauging public opinion on the creation of new provinces.

Over the past few months, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has whipped up a political storm since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

On November 12, Naqvi also floated the idea of holding a referendum to gauge public opinion on the issue, saying the exercise could settle the contentious debate once and for all.

articles.title: Bangladesh vows to arrest Hasina if she returns from India
articles.summary:
Bangladesh will arrest and jail former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina if she returns from India, a senior government minister said, as her plans to come home in December fuel political tension and renewed street violence.

Dhaka is instead seeking Hasina’s extradition from India, where she has lived since fleeing Bangladesh in 2024, and expects New Delhi to comply with an existing extradition treaty, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam told Reuters.

India’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In April, the ministry said it was examining Bangladesh’s request to extradite Hasina.

Hasina faces a death sentence in Bangladesh and her Awami League party is banned following the 2024 uprising that ended her long rule. The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.

Hasina fled Dhaka in August 2024 as protests demanding her resignation swept the country. She has since sought a new passport and identity card ahead of a planned return in December, requests the government has rejected.

“As soon as she tries to enter Bangladesh, she will be arrested. And she will be taken to jail, and the law will take its course,” Obaed said in an interview on Sunday.

“We would like India to honour the extradition treaty and return her as a convict, and the law will take its course. She (Hasina) will have to face the music.” The standoff has brought Hasina’s Awami League supporters out on the streets. The party this month announced a week of protests and rallies in support of Hasina’s return, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on November 19.

Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of arson targeting vehicles in at least 28 districts over the past 10 days, with several police officers and civilians injured, according to local media.

Obaed called the violence a survival tactic by Hasina’s “politically bankrupt political party.” Khalid Mahmud Chowdhury, a senior Awami League official, said the current political establishment was responsible for the violence.

The minister said there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring Hasina back, adding that Dhaka wanted balanced ties with New Delhi that did not compromise Bangladesh’s “dignity, self-respect and interests.” “India needs to decide what kind of foreign policy they need to adopt for Bangladesh,” Obaed said.

Rohingya verdict

Dhaka is also stepping up diplomatic pressure on neighbouring Myanmar over the return of Rohingya refugees after the UN’s highest court ruled that thousands of killings and widespread sexual violence by Myanmar’s security forces against the Muslim minority in 2017 amounted to state-sponsored genocide.

Myanmar has criticised the ruling by the International Court of Justice, saying Rohingya would only be able to return “when situations permit”.

“Now, this verdict gives us, Bangladesh, the strength, the Rohingya community the strength to fight,” Obaed said, adding that they deserved to return “with dignity and safety”.

About 1.2 million Rohingya live in Bangladesh after repeated repatriation attempts failed. Their return has been complicated by Myanmar’s civil war and the Arakan Army militia’s control of nearly all of Rakhine State, which is home for most Rohingya.

Obaed called for greater international pressure on Myanmar and the Arakan Army.

“Bangladesh did not create this crisis. Myanmar created this crisis, so Myanmar has to end it,” she said.

articles.title: India to give $1.62bn economic package to flood-hit Nepal
articles.summary:
India will give Nepal an economic package worth 240 billion Nepalese rupees ($1.62bn), Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Monday, after talks with his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.

Shah is in the Indian capital for a two-day visit, his first bilateral trip since coming to power in March, and in the aftermath of the devastating Himalayan flood in August that killed some 1,500 people, with another 5,200 missing and presumed dead.

“Today, to give fresh impetus to Nepal’s reconstruction and long-term development, we are announcing a development cooperation package worth 24,000 crore (240 billion) Nepalese rupees,” Modi said, addressing the media after the talks, with Shah standing beside him.

“Our commitment will be to help affected families get their lives back on track, create new opportunities and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” Modi said.

Shah thanked India for consistently acting as a first responder for Nepal “in times of natural disasters and difficult hours”.

“I warmly welcome Indian investors to Nepal to partner in the economic prosperity of our two countries in the coming days,” he said, and invited Modi to visit the Himalayan nation.

The two countries signed agreements to boost their economic relationship and Modi and Shah jointly opened a train link connecting the two countries.

The August 26 flood, caused by a glacier collapse on Nepal’s border with China, sent a mass of mud and rock crashing into the Trishuli river.

The resulting flood washed away villages, snapped highways, bridges and power lines, and buried homes in the mud in the impoverished country that is wedged between Asian giants India and China.

Nepal and India enjoy longstanding cultural, economic and people-to-people ties with an open border allowing hundreds of thousands of Nepalis to live and work in India.

New Delhi was the first to respond after the August flood, sending several plane-loads of aid to restore communication links that were severed in the mountains.

articles.title: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya
articles.summary:
President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv.

The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its strikes against Russia far from the frontlines.

But the United Nations condemned the strikes, warning against the prospect of a country still divided after the Libyan civil war becoming “a battleground for foreign conflicts”.

“It all took place off the coast of Libya. Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones. Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk,” Zelensky wrote on X.

The Ukrainian leader claimed the Merkury was “one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war”.

“Our second target was the Russian dry cargo vessel MV ANGARA, which the enemy used to transport weapons. Result: target hit,” he added.

A Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed in the strike on the Merkury, Zelensky said.

Sunday’s strikes came after a drone hit a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday, close to the waters of Finland, whose border guard said the strike was Ukrainian.

The UN mission in Libya expressed “serious concern” over the attacks, calling for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation”.

“Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts,” the UNSMIL wrote on X.

UN calls for probe into attacks

The United Nations called for an independent investigation into the drone attacks, expressing concern over the potential spillover of the Ukraine war into Libya.

Authorities said all crew members had been rescued and were receiving treatment for minor injuries. They said a merchant vessel had been targeted by explosive-laden sea drones off Benghazi but did not identify its country of origin. Reports said the second ship was sailing under a Maltese flag.

Libya Alhadath television later reported that naval and air force units had intercepted more than 12 explosive-laden sea drones off Benghazi.

Libya’s eastern administration did not identify those responsible for the attack but said the country was “not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war”.

Meanwhile, Ukraine said on Monday that Russian strikes had killed at least 12 people in its Kyiv region, including in a block of flats and at a supermarket.

The conflict, which began with Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.

‘Shadow fleet’

Earlier reports said a fire broke out inside an ammunition depot at a naval base, but authorities in Libya’s east said later “the explosion occurred on board a Russian ship docked in the port”.“It is suspected that the ship was attacked by drones,” an official statement said.

“The ship was en route back to Russia and its stop was for refuelling and resupply.” The eastern administration said it would launch a joint investigation with Russia.

The rival UN-recognised government in Tripoli said in a statement it was alarmed by “risks posed by involving civilian ports and facilities in activities linked to external conflicts”.

In March, a Russian liquefied natural gas carrier sank off the Libyan coast following an attack, which Russian President Vladimir Putin blamed on Ukraine. The vessel was part of Russia’s so-called “shadow fleet” of tankers that carry its oil and gas around the world, skirting Western restrictions.

Ukraine has at times admitted to attacking Moscow’s shadow fleet, including in the Mediterranean last December.

The Tripoli government said it rejected any attempt to turn Libya into “an arena for international conflicts” and the use of its territory “for any military or logistical activities that could jeopardise” national security or sovereignty.

Libya has been beset by violence and instability since the overthrow of longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.

It remains divided between the government in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah and a rival administration in the east backed by military commander Khalifa Haftar.

articles.title: ADB invests in Pakistan-based B2B fintech company Neem
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Monday said it invested an undisclosed amount in Neem, a Pakistan-based B2B fintech company that helps businesses receive, manage, and pay out money digitally.

In a statement, the Manila-based lending agency said its investment will flow through ADB Ventures, the venture capital arm of the ADB.

The seed investment will support Neem’s product development, help expand its team, and accelerate the onboarding of enterprise and merchant clients across Pakistan, the ADB said.

Pakistan has made strong progress in digitising consumer payments, with the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP)’s instant payment system, Raast, and mobile wallets bringing millions of people onto digital rails. Business payments, however, have not kept pace.

According to SBP, an estimated 71 per cent of retail transaction value is still settled in cash, and companies looking to go digital must integrate separately with banks, wallets, payroll providers and reconciliation tools, a process that can be slow, costly, and hard to scale.

Neem aims to close this gap by giving businesses a single platform to manage how money comes in, how it is tracked, and how it is paid out. Its API-first system combines collections, disbursements, a programmable ledger and finance workflows, and connects directly with a company’s existing operating systems to automate settlement and reconciliation in real time.

Neem currently serves more than 70 enterprise clients across logistics, utilities, insurance, manufacturing and retail.

“Pakistan is laying a strong foundation for digital payments, and the next step is ensuring that businesses of all sizes can fully benefit from this progress,” said Emma Fan, ADB Country Director for Pakistan.

“Neem is helping enterprises move away from cash and fragmented systems toward payment solutions that are faster, more transparent and easier to manage.”

The impact extends well beyond the enterprises Neem serves directly. As businesses digitise their payments, the suppliers, small merchants and gig workers they pay are brought into the formal financial system.

Neem’s solutions are built to meet the payment needs of businesses of every size, including women-owned businesses and micro-entrepreneurs, so access to modern financial infrastructure is not limited to large enterprises.

As part of its lending portfolio, Neem also gives employees responsible access to wages they have already earned. The offering focuses on blue-collar workers in industries that employ large workforces across Pakistan and helps reduce reliance on informal borrowing.

ADB Ventures invests in early-stage technology companies building solutions that address the most pressing challenges across Asia and the Pacific, with a focus on sectors including financial technology, agricultural technology, climate resilience and inclusive growth.

articles.title: Residents protest as work continues at Karachi's Nehr-i-Khayyam despite SHC order
articles.summary:
KARACHI: Residents of Clifton on Sunday expressed concerns that construction and development activities at Nehr-i-Khayyam were continuing despite recent clear directions from the Sindh High Court (SHC) to halt them.

The residents of the area held their weekly protest, marching from Do Talwar towards the under-construction site of a 46-storey building and the Nehr-i-Khayyam site under the banners of “Save Clifton” and “Liveable Clifton”.

They were protesting against the “unchecked transformation of residential neighbourhoods, violations of building regulations and the destruction of public spaces”.

They called upon the authorities to enforce building and zoning regulations, investigate the approval of high-rise buildings in residential streets and protect residential neighbourhoods by stopping “unauthorised commercial conversions and developments that compromise residents’ safety, access, infrastructure and quality of life”.

The residents also demanded the protection of public spaces and an end to the commercialisation and encroachment of parks, green belts and amenity plots. They further called for the restoration of civic infrastructure and greater transparency and accountability, with officials held responsible for violations.

Speaking to the media, Sohail Osman Ali said the “cancer” of high-rise buildings was spreading in the area, describing the trend as “madness”.

Expressing concern over the construction of a 46-storey building, another protester, Shiraz Qureshi, told the media that the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) had allowed the construction of a high-rise building in a residential area with narrow streets and inadequate resources to accommodate such a project.

He also alleged that the government was only interested in the commercialisation of Clifton Block 5.

He said that despite the high court’s orders, construction work at Nehr-i-Khayyam was continuing round the clock.

Rasha Tarek, a protester and member of the Karachi Residents’ Community (District South), said that “unregulated” high-rise projects in the area were threatening natural ventilation pathways that carry cooling sea breezes inland, potentially trapping heat and compromising the city’s environmental liveability.

Published in Dawn, November 23rd, 2026

articles.title: Lahore ranked after Islamabad, ahead of major cities in safety perception index
articles.summary:
LAHORE: Lahore has scored ahead of several major international cities, including New York, Paris and New Delhi but lower than Islamabad in the recent Numbeo’s 2026 Mid-Year Crime and Safety Index with safety and crime indexes at 63.8 and 36.2 respectively.

A report in this regard was presented to Punjab Inspector General of Police (IGP) Abdul Kareem during his visit to the Lahore Police Lines, Qilla Gujjar Singh here on Sunday, where he held a high-level meeting on the crime situation in the city.

Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Bilal Siddique Kamyana, DIGs Faisal Kamran, Zeshan Raza, all the SSPs, SPs and other senior police officers were present. A senior official told this reporter that the meeting discussed various other key issues including criteria of posting the station house officers (SHOs), deteriorating response time of police on helpline 15 calls, shortage of Dolphin Force bikes and mishandling of some cases, such as a police raid at the residence of Attorney General for Pakistan (AGP) Mansoor Usman Awan.

During the session, he said, the DIG operations presented Numbeo’s report which has placed Lahore in the “Low” to “Moderate” crime range based on user-submitted perception surveys.

“Lahore scores lower on crime than Karachi (Crime Index 57.8–57.9) and Rawalpindi (51.8), while Islamabad scores lower on crime (30.8–31.1)”, said Mr Kamran while quoting the report. He added that the provincial capital also scored lower on crime than many major Western cities.

“These figures are based on visitors’ perception on this website,” he said, adding that a total of 380 cities of the world were included in the surveys.

IGP holds high-level meeting and discusses posting of SHOs, deteriorating response on helpline 15, shortage of Dolphin Force bikes, mishandling of cases

The CCPO told the meeting that Lahore was the only city in Punjab without any no-go area, major land-grabbing mafia, gangsters or hooligans as the police had eradicated them to bring peace in the city. He told the meeting that the crime situation of the city had improved significantly during the last four years.During the meeting, the official said, the IGP expressed displeasure over the deteriorating response time of the police on 15 calls, saying that it had dropped to 22pc across the province. He declared it a matter of serious concern and said that as per reports, the callers were being asked to reach police stations to file their reports.

The official said that DIG operations clarified that the response time of the police in Lahore was recorded 66pc. However, Abdul Kareem declared the response time of the Lahore police at 15 ‘still insufficient’ as Lahore police possessed significantly more resources than those in other cities.

The official said that Mr Kamran cited shortage of bikes for Dolphin Force as a major reason for low response time. He further elaborated that the Dolphin Force were patrolling on bikes of various police stations as a makeshift arrangement.

Mr Kareem revealed that Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz had approved procurement of new bikes for the provincial police at a cost of Rs300 millions with Lahore Police getting as many as 300-400 bikes by December.

According to the insider, the IGP said that inspectors were complaining that they were not being considered for SHO posts in the provincial capital. He said that they were worried that a majority of junior officials, sub-inspectors, were serving as SHOs.

In response to these complaints, the DIG operations said that two-thirds of SHOs were sub-inspectors and it was meant to produce a pool of trained officials for sensitive jobs.

About the complaints of missing women, the DIG investigation told the IGP that out of thousands of such cases, less than 100 were yet to be traced.

Published in Dawn, November 23rd, 2026
