articles.title: Govt moves to overhaul ‘weak’ audit system
articles.summary:
• FBR task force flags weaknesses in existing review framework
• Cabinet approves SECP Amendment Bill 2026 after consultation
• Proposed legislation aims to strengthen independent audit oversight

ISLAMABAD: The government has decided to overhaul the country’s ent­ire audit system after the Prime Min­ister’s Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) Task Force described the existing framework as weak, saying it discourages local and foreign investm­ent and limits access to capital markets.

Documents seen by Dawn suggest the government plans to introduce legislative amendments in parliament to reform the existing audit system.

The proposed amendments will be introduced in the light of recommendations made by the Prime Minister’s FBR Task Force, which has already raised serious concerns over weaknesses in the existing audit framework, according to the document.

In this regard, the government will introduce legislation, including the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) (Amendment) Bill, 2026. A similar bill was passed by the National Assembly in 2021 after scrutiny and recommendations by the NA Standing Committee on Finance. However, it was withdrawn from the Senate in 2022 for resubmission. The federal cabinet has now approved the proposed bill again after extensive consultations and reviews by three ministerial-level committees.

The task force has also recommended amendments to the Audit Oversight Board (AOB) law to improve tax collection.

The process of reforming the AOB was already underway, but market-related concerns continued to highlight weaknesses in audits. Pakistan’s existing AOB law did not comply with international standards, an official briefing document said.

“Investors and lenders rely on audited accounts, but weak audits discourage local and foreign investment and access to capital markets.

“The International Organisation of Securities Commissions (IOSCO), the securities market standard-setter, declared Pakistan non-compliant with independent audit oversight. The European Union (EU) also withdrew Pakistan’s equivalence status for independent audit oversight,” it added.

The report cited Unity Foods and SE Foods as examples of companies affected by weak audits and prospectus disclosures. It also highlighted concerns over Hascol’s audited accounts.

The report said developed and developing countries had amended their laws and shifted from self-regulatory oversight by accountancy bodies to independent audit oversight. Even smaller jurisdictions, including Sri Lanka, Mauritius and Botswana, are compliant members of the International Forum of Independent Audit Regulators (IFIAR), it added.

It has been learnt that the proposed system will end the dominance of private auditors.

The document said the federal cabinet had approved the draft legislation following a comprehensive review by the FBR Task Force, IFIAR, SECP and AOB, along with extensive consultations with stakeholders. The proposed legislation is expected to strengthen Pakistan’s international recognition and establish an effective audit oversight system.

The salient features of the SECP Amendment Bill, 2026, are as follows:

The independence of the nominating committee responsible for appointing AOB board members will be strengthened by including the FBR chairman in place of the president of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan (ICAP).

AOB board members will not be permitted to have any association with audit firms.

The AOB board will be responsible for policy matters, while management, operations and adjudication will be handled in line with governance principles and the board’s regulatory functions.

The AOB will conduct regular, risk-based inspections of auditors of Public Interest Companies (PICs) to assess compliance with professional auditing standards.

Accountancy bodies will continue to conduct regular inspections and Quality Control Reviews (QCRs) of non-PIC audits under the oversight of the AOB.

The AOB will directly investigate complaints and references from the SECP, State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and FBR after approval by its board or a designated committee.

Standard action will be taken against individuals who refuse to provide required information, while the AOB will also be empowered to file complaints concerning criminal offences involving falsification.

Published in Dawn, November 23rd, 2026

articles.title: Conveyor belt failure at bulk terminal disrupts coal imports
articles.summary:
• Coal discharge rate falls from 30,000 to 3,000 tonnes per day
• Jamshoro Power Company warns of $2-3 million demurrage on five incoming vessels; fears Rs2.2 billion monthly capacity payment losses

ISLAMABAD: The one and only coal-handling conveyor system at Pakistan Intern­ational Bulk Terminal (PIBT) at Port Qasim has been out of operation since Nov 18, disrupting imported coal supplies to power plants and industries, including cement and textiles, at a time when the power sector is already facing LNG supply disruptions and reduced hydroelectric availability.

Public and private sector power plants and their coal suppliers face mounting demurrage charges as vessels wait to discharge cargo, besides potential power generation problems, penalties and revenue losses.

With coal discharge rates at the terminal falling to one-tenth of their normal level, PIBT has dec­lined requests from power producers and suppliers to declare force majeure, which they say would help them pursue insurance claims and avoid financial losses.

According to PIBT, the terminal’s conveyor was damaged on Nov 18 during the discharge of coal from the vessel ‘Pegasus 8’ due to the “excessively dusty nat­ure of the Tanzanian coal” and the presence of “foreign materials, particularly sharp pieces of iron mixed with the cargo”. Repairs could take eight to 10 days, it said.

The state-run Jamshoro Power Company (JPC) reported that “vessels are being discharged manually at a significantly redu­ced rate (3,000MT per day versus the usual 30,000 MT per day)”.

In a letter to PIBT and the federal government, JPC said it dep­e­nded on “uninterrupted coal rec­eipts” through the terminal and that “this disruption puts that supply at immediate risk with serious and compounding consequences”.

The company said delayed coal receipts threatened critical stocks at its plant and, consequently, its operations and electricity generation for the national grid, besides causing port congestion and demurrage charges.

Slower discharge would lengthen queues at PIBT and expose waiting vessels to demurrage, increasing the cost of imported coal and, subsequently, electricity generation.

The company warned that del­ays to incoming shipments would also disrupt critical supplies and raise future procurement costs due to demurrage on vessels already en route or ordered.

“Based on our five upcoming vessels, demurrage exposure is expected to exceed $2-3 million (Rs556m-Rs834m). Furth­ermore, the disruption could result in potential capacity payment losses of approximately Rs2.2 billion per month to JPC due to insufficient coal inventory,” it said.

Given these consequences, JPC called on PIBT to declare force majeure in view of the nature and scale of the failure.

“JPC requests that PIBT form­ally declare force majeure without delay,” it said, warning “all dem­­urrage, detention, additional exp­enses, damages and losses ari­sing out of or attributable to the disruption shall be borne by PIBT”.

A shipping line has warned that it would seek compensation for the prolonged wait for discharge as well as any damage caused to its vessel during conventional unloading.

However, PIBT rejected the requests, saying the breakdown was not “an event giving rise to any declaration of force majeure on our part, as the discharging operations are ongoing, albeit thr­ough conventional means”, which were “understandably going to be slower”.

Sources said the terminal’s dependence on a single jetty, coal berth and conveyor system had compounded the problem. A second conveyor proposed in 2021 to increase annual handling capacity from 12m to 17m tonnes has yet to be built.

articles.title: Why I walked away from restaurant business location – Social influencer Pamilerin Adegoke
articles.summary:
Social media influencer and entrepreneur, Pamilerin Adegoke has clarified the circumstances surrounding the closure of his restaurant, La Cibo, on Ogunlana Drive in Surulere, Lagos, dismissing claims that the business was shut down over unpaid rent.

Adegoke made the clarification on Monday, following a critical comment by an X user, @viccetti, who claimed that the restaurant had been silently closed over unpaid rent.

“I was driving pass Ogunlana Drive In Surulere and noticed that APC fan boy Pamilerin has silently closed down his restaurant La Cibo due to unpaid rent,” the user stated.

He went further to mock Adegoke over his political leaning, asking, “I thought APC supporters get special treatment in this country? What happened?”

The user also criticised the restaurant’s service, claiming he once waited for two hours to be served.

“Restaurants like that shouldn’t exist,” he asserted.

Responding, Adegoke denied that he was chased out, insisting the exit was a business decision taken after years of rising rent.

He said, “Happy they still haven’t gotten a new tenant two years after we left that building.

“Now they can see that we were doing them a favour, paying millions in rent year after year while they kept increasing it.”

Adegoke also berated the building owners for being insensitive, explaining that the business was not being used for money laundering, which could justify such increment.

“We eventually said enough was enough and walked away. Maybe they thought we were running a laundry business with the way they kept raising the rent,” he said.

La Cibo, also known as Lacibo Restaurant and Lounge, was co-founded by Adegoke, who has previously spoken about his love for food as the inspiration behind the venture.

The post Why I walked away from restaurant business location – Social influencer Pamilerin Adegoke appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Rivers 2027: Tam-George warns against election rigging
articles.summary:
Dr Austin Tam-George, Director of Strategy and Public Policy for the Dumo Lulu-Briggs’ Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Governorship Campaign Council in Rivers State, has warned against attempts to manipulate the 2027 elections, saying such actions would undermine the will of voters.

Tam-George gave the warning during an interview on ARISE News, where he called for a credible electoral process and urged Rivers residents to mobilise against what he described as excessive political control of the state by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike.

He described Rivers as being in an existential political crisis, alleging that Wike had maintained his influence through political allies and surrogates.

Tam-George also accused the minister of using political structures to influence the state’s leadership and determine its political direction. He claimed that Governor Siminalayi Fubara was no longer acting independently.

The NDC campaign council official, however, said the party was building a broad coalition of supporters across political divides to challenge the existing political arrangement.

He stressed that the 2027 election must reflect the genuine choices of the electorate, warning that any attempt to rig the process would amount to stealing the people’s mandate.

Tam-George described electoral manipulation as an attack on the sovereignty of voters and called on residents to defend their right to choose their leaders.

He also outlined some of the priorities of the NDC governorship candidate, Dumo Lulu-Briggs, if elected, including declaring a state of emergency in the education sector on his inauguration day.

According to him, the proposed administration would restore scholarships and bursaries, improve teachers’ welfare, digitise the civil service and address outstanding pensions and gratuities.

He added that the campaign was focused on industrialisation, improving public services and encouraging businesses to return to Rivers State.

Tam-George further alleged that political disputes had affected the functioning of some government ministries, claiming that key sectors, including health, justice and commerce, lacked substantive commissioners.

He maintained that Rivers residents needed to take an active role in determining the state’s political future, insisting that the 2027 election should be free, fair and credible.

The post Rivers 2027: Tam-George warns against election rigging appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Delta Govt condemns Uduere killings, dismisses link to Gov. Oborevwori, says no one will be shielded
articles.summary:
Delta State Government has dismissed allegations linking Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the killings in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, insisting that those responsible will not escape justice, no matter their political position or status.

The government also imposed an immediate curfew from 6pm to 6am everyday starting from today until further notice on the entire Ughelli North Local Government Area, to bring the situation under control.

According to a statement signed by the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Dr Kingsley Eze Emu, Governor Oborevwori was deeply disturbed by the killings and had directed security agencies to immediately investigate the incident, identify those responsible and ensure that they are brought to justice.

He described the loss of lives as tragic and unacceptable, stressing that no political ambition or disagreement should result in the taking of innocent lives.

The State Government commiserated with the families of the deceased, and all those affected by the incident, and also wished the injured victims a speedy recovery.

While acknowledging the seriousness of the allegations raised by Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Dr Emu said it was important to allow security agencies to conduct a thorough, impartial and professional investigation rather than rush to conclusions or assign blame without established facts.

He specifically dismissed the attempt to link Governor Oborevwori to the violence, describing such allegations as grave matters that must be substantiated and investigated rather than presented as established facts.

“The Governor has nothing to gain from violence or the loss of innocent lives. His administration remains committed to peace, security and the protection of every resident of Delta State, irrespective of political affiliation.”

“Governor Oborevwori has made it clear that anyone found to have participated in, sponsored or facilitated this criminal act must face the full weight of the law. Nobody will be protected on account of political position, status or affiliation,” he said.

The SSG emphasized that Delta State must not be allowed to degenerate into an atmosphere of political violence, adding that the right to campaign, canvass for votes and participate in the democratic process must be respected and protected.

He urged political leaders, party supporters and their followers to exercise restraint, avoid inflammatory statements and refrain from actions capable of escalating tensions in the state.

He further appealed to residents of Uduere and neighbouring communities to remain calm, cooperate with security agencies and provide useful information that could assist in the investigation.

He assured that the Oborevwori administration would continue to work with relevant security agencies to maintain peace and protect lives and property across the state.

Dr Emu reiterated that the government would not condone political violence under any guise, insisting that the perpetrators of the Uduere killings must be identified and brought to justice.

articles.title: 2027: Okpebholo promises third Benin flyover if Tinubu wins
articles.summary:
Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has promised to begin construction of a third flyover bridge in Benin City if President Bola Tinubu wins the 2027 presidential election.

The proposed bridge will link Agbor Road to Sakponba Road in Ikpoba-Okha Local Government Area of the state.

Okpebholo made the pledge during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Ikpoba-Okha, following the party’s campaign activities in Orhionmwon Local Government Area.

He said the project would improve movement and provide better access for residents and businesses in the area but explained that its execution would depend on financial support from the Federal Government.

“I promise to start a flyover bridge from the back of Guinness to Sakpoba Road in Ikpoba-Okha. I need money to do this, and I can only do it with the support of President Tinubu,” the governor said.

He urged residents to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 general election, arguing that their support would help sustain development in the state.

The governor also called on voters to support APC candidates, whom he described as competent and credible, saying they would work with his administration to advance development.

Deputy Governor Dennis Idahosa thanked residents of Orhionmwon and Ikpoba-Okha for their support and appealed to them to back Tinubu and other party candidates.

Former Edo State governor and senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, urged voters to consider competence and credibility rather than ethnic affiliations when choosing their leaders. He also claimed that the APC had performed well at the state and federal levels.

Former Deputy Governor Pius Odubu expressed confidence in continued development under Okpebholo, while APC leader in Edo South, Osagie Ize-Iyamu, praised the governor for starting electricity projects in Orhionmwon, which he said had experienced poor electricity supply for about 20 years.

The Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Matthew Urhoghide, commended Okpebholo over what he described as improved security in the state. He also urged residents to help secure 2.5 million votes for Tinubu.

APC State Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, said the party had attracted new members in Orhionmwon and remained united. He attributed the party’s cohesion to Okpebholo’s leadership and claimed that cultism, kidnapping and other criminal activities had reduced across the state.

The party’s Deputy State Chairman, Sylvester Aigboboh, said Orhionmwon and Ikpoba-Okha had benefited from more than 50 development projects. He urged residents to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates to sustain the projects.

articles.title: Police dismantle internet fraud camp in Abeokuta, arrest 11 suspects, recover vehicles, charms, others
articles.summary:
The Police Special Fraud Unit (SFU), Ikoyi, Lagos, has dismantled an internet fraud camp in Abeokuta, Ogun State, and secured the remand of eleven suspects arrested at the location.

Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SFU, DSP Ovie Kenneth Ewhubare disclosed this in a Monday statement issued on behalf of the Commissioner of Police of the unit.

According to the statement, the operation followed credible intelligence and coordinated investigative efforts which led detectives to House 10, Second Hill Estate, Oloke-Meji, Onikolobo, Abeokuta, where the suspects had been using the apartment as their operational base.

During the operation, detectives recovered eleven iPhones, three Samsung mobile phones, eight laptops, a Lexus RX 350 of 2014 model, charms, multiple blood-stained fetish items and suspected human remains.

Ewhubare said investigations revealed that one Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju, also known as Update, who is currently at large, rented the apartment in 2021 and subsequently recruited young men into an organised internet fraud operation commonly known as a Hustle Kingdom, where they used the facility as a base for cyber-related fraud and other criminal activities.

The police image-maker disclosed that the suspects admitted that they exploit the identities and personal details of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online.

The statement quoted the CP, SFU, CP Eloho Edwin Okpoziakpo, as saying that the discovery underscored the importance of credible information, intelligence-led policing and professional investigative skills in combating organised financial and cyber-enabled crimes.

He added that investigations were ongoing into the circumstances surrounding the occupation of the premises and the extent to which the property owner complied with the responsibility to properly verify and monitor occupants, particularly in view of the prolonged use of the apartment for criminal activities.

Ewhubare said efforts were also being made to trace and recover all the proceeds of crime in a bid to pursue justice in its restorative form.

articles.title: 2027: 4 dead, 4 wounded as Omo-Agege camp alleges assassination attempt in Uduere
articles.summary:
At least four people have reported and four others were wounded after gunmen allegedly opened fire on the campaign team of Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Delta Central Senatorial Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area.

The incident occurred on Monday, 23rd November 2026, during a campaign tour to Uduere.

In a press statement signed by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation said armed men opened fire at close range on Senator Omo-Agege and his entourage while he was addressing the crowd.

The campaign claimed the attack was a targeted attempt to assassinate the Senator.

According to the campaign, two of its aides namely, Moses Anaughe and a popular human rights activist,

Akima Efemena Umukoro were among those killed.

Two others were also killed, bringing the death toll to four.

Four others were wounded including Chief Evans Iwuvrie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba who was shot in the neck and Ayodo Wanogho.

The wounded are currently receiving medical attention.

The campaign alleged that witnesses heard the attackers shouting, _”It’s Omo-Agege we want to kill! It’s Omo-Agege we want to kill!”

It further alleged that the attack was led by the Chairman of Ughelli North LGA, Barr. Jaro Egbo, acting on orders from Governor Sheriff Oborevwori.

The Delta State Police Command and the Delta State Government have not yet issued a response as at the time of filing this report to the allegations.

The campaign also alleged that police officers present at the scene with six trucks did nothing to prevent the attack.

The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation demanded that Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, as Chief Security Officer of the state, should publicly condemn the attack in Uduere, order the immediate arrest and investigation of all persons alleged to have participated in, financed, or directed the attack, including Barr. Jaro Egbo, guarantee the safety of Senator Omo-Agege, NDC leadership and all opposition candidates in Delta State

It also called on the Inspector-General of Police to personally take over the investigation, saying it no longer has confidence in the Delta State Police Command.

It further called on the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to take note.

The campaign urged its supporters not to retaliate, saying its ward-to-ward tour of Delta Central will continue.

“Delta State is not a war zone. Campaigning is not a crime. Seeking the votes of the people should not be a death sentence,” the statement said.

articles.title: London promoter fulfils late brother’s dream with K1
articles.summary:
Bolanle Olatise turns grief into a mission as Alexis Promotions brings Fuji legend to UK stage

 

A United Kingdom-based music promoter, Bolanle Olatise, has revealed that her journey into entertainment was inspired by a promise she made to her late elder brother — to promote Fuji music icon, King Wasiu Ayinde Marshal, popularly known as K1 De Ultimate.

Olatise, who promotes under the aegis of Alexis Promotions Limited, disclosed this in an exclusive interview, where she spoke about passion, resilience and determination.

According to her, she is the last-born of three children, and her elder brother was a devoted lover of Fuji music, particularly the music of K1.

“My elder brother was deeply passionate about Fuji music, particularly K1. He loved the music and was a strong admirer of him,” she said.

She explained that her brother’s greatest dream was to one day promote K1, but he passed away before he could achieve it.

“Unfortunately, my brother passed away, but one of his greatest dreams was to promote K1. I promised him that I would make that dream a reality. That promise was the major reason I ventured into entertainment and music promotion,” Olatise said.

The London-based promoter admitted that at the time she made the promise, she did not have the financial capacity to undertake a project of such magnitude.

“At the time, I couldn’t afford to undertake such a huge project. However, I am someone who loves challenges,” she said.

“Whenever I set my mind on something, I work hard and do everything possible to achieve it. So, I started saving towards fulfilling my brother’s dream.”

Olatise said her entry into music promotion was therefore not driven by fame or profit, but by commitment to family, legacy and a love for Fuji music.

Through Alexis Promotions Limited, she has continued to work towards bringing K1’s music to a wider audience in the United Kingdom, turning what began as a personal promise into a growing professional brand.

Olatise maintained that she remains committed to sustaining her brother’s legacy through quality entertainment and promotion of African music in the diaspora.

The post London promoter fulfils late brother’s dream with K1 appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Gov. Lawal flags-off Zamfara APC campaign in Mafara, vows inclusive governance
articles.summary:
From John Bassey, Gusau

The Executive Governor of Zamfara state, Dr. Dauda lawal has flagged off the All Progressive Congress, APC Campaign, consultation and mobilization exercise, the target is to gather more than three million votes for President Bola Ahmad Tinubu and ensure the success of all candidates under the party.

The exercise which commenced at the prayer grounds of Talata Mafara aimed at honouring the son of Zamfara state, Dr. Abdullaziz Yari the Director General of APC Presidential Campaign Council as his home town sets the pace for the remaining 13 Local Government Areas, Governor Lawal vowed inclusive governance and assured the citizens of Zamfara state of a conducive state of peace where everyone experience prosperity, joy and togetherness during his second tenure.

Governor Lawal pledged to intensify war against insurgency, build more infrastructure, concentrate on Rural Access Roads construction, focus on human capital development and fullfil his proposed plans under rescue Agenda if elected come 2027.

He encouraged the people of Zamfara state, members, supporters and stakeholders of APC to have more confidence on the administration of President Bola Tinubu and his administration as the only leadership that have the capacity to satisfy their imaginations and enhance their comfort in the next four years.

He called on the people to vote for APC both in the state, local government and wards level in order to secure their freedom.

The Director General, APC Presidential Campaign Council, Sen. Abdullaziz Yari Abubakar expressed gratitude to the people of Zamfara state, supporters, members and stakeholders of APC for coming out in mass for the flag-off exercise in Talata Mafara amidst the long distance and poor condition of the roads.

Presence at the flag-off exercise were the former governors of Zamfara state, House of Assembly members, serving Senators, House of Representative members and other dignitaries to celebrate the commencement of the exercise.

articles.title: 2027: Tinubu woos Ndigbo in Lagos, seeks support for second term, APC candidates
articles.summary:
President Bola Tinubu has appealed to members of the Igbo community in Lagos State, market leaders and traders to support his re-election bid in 2027, urging them to vote for the All Progressives Congress (APC) and its candidates across the country.

Tinubu made the appeal on Monday while addressing the Ndigbo Lagos State Town Hall, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative (NNDDI) at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos.

The President, who adopted a conciliatory tone in his engagement with the Igbo community, acknowledged that a significant number of Ndigbo in Lagos did not support his presidential ambition in the 2023 election.

He, however, urged them to reconsider their political position, obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and support his administration for another four years, citing ongoing infrastructure development and economic opportunities across the country, particularly in the Southeast.

Addressing a large gathering of traders and socio-cultural leaders drawn from major commercial centres, including Alaba International Market, Radio Market and ASPAMDA, Tinubu said another term would enable him to consolidate his administration’s achievements and continue serving Nigerians.

“The critical aspect in our national anthem is what I came here for. I appeal for the job and I am ready to serve; to serve you as I did in my first term. The Constitution allows me to serve for another term, so I want a second term,” he declared.

The President urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and religious differences, insisting that the country should be regarded as a common home where everyone could pursue legitimate aspirations and prosper.

“Let’s see ourselves as one people living in the same house geographically called Nigeria. So, if you are in Nnewi, Onitsha or anywhere, grow up there and you come to Lagos, you are just answering the call of business and opportunity that God-given country, Nigeria, has given to you,” he said.

Tinubu cautioned against individuals and groups seeking to exploit ethnic differences for political advantage, stressing that national development depended on unity, mutual understanding and collective responsibility.

“Don’t let anyone come to divide us. In brotherhood we stand,” he added.

The President also made references to his family’s multi-ethnic connections, including his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, who is of Itsekiri heritage, as an illustration of the cultural diversity and interconnectedness that define Nigeria.

He maintained that Nigerians, irrespective of their ethnic backgrounds or places of origin, should be able to live, work and conduct business anywhere in the country without discrimination.

Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, who attended the town hall alongside his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, described Tinubu’s presence as a significant recognition of the Igbo community and its contributions to Lagos State.

Sanwo-Olu expressed appreciation to the President for honouring the gathering, noting that the engagement provided an opportunity to strengthen relationships between the government and the Ndigbo community.

He also acknowledged political leaders, business associates and other stakeholders at the event, recognising their contributions to the political and economic development of Lagos and Nigeria.

The governor made references to Nigeria’s political journey, particularly the elections of 1999, 2003 and 2007, while acknowledging the roles played by various political leaders in shaping the country’s democratic development.

The town hall brought together Igbo community leaders, traders, business owners, political stakeholders and government representatives to discuss issues affecting Ndigbo in Lagos and explore ways of strengthening their relationship with the state and Federal Government.

It also provided a platform to promote dialogue, inclusion and peaceful coexistence, with participants underscoring the importance of mutual respect and cooperation in sustaining the unity and development of Lagos State and Nigeria.

articles.title: Benue PDP inaugurates campaign council, says over 15 pol parties have endorsed Aondoakaa
articles.summary:
Ahead of the general elections in 2027, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Benue State has inaugurated the Aondoakaa/Ogbenjuwa 2027 Campaign Council in Makurdi, the state capital.

The PDP, during the inauguration on Monday said more than 15 political parties have endorsed its governorship candidate, Chief Mike Aondoakaa, and are working hard to ensure his victory come at the polls.

The chairman of the party, Ezekiel Adaji, who disclosed this while addressing party members at the event said the endorsements were evidence of growing support for Aondoakaa and the party’s determination to reclaim power in the state.

Adaji urged party members to intensify mobilisation across the 23 local government areas, expressing confidence that the Aondoakaa-led administration would restore peace and address insecurity, particularly the difficulties confronting farmers.

The PDP candidate Mike Aondoakaa, SAN, in his address, pledged to promote fairness, protect businesses and ensure that farmers, investors and other residents could pursue legitimate economic activities without intimidation or discrimination.

Aondoakaa also called for independent public institutions, effective leadership and improved access to basic amenities, including clean water.

Aondoakaa pledged to develop rural communities and step up the fight against insecurity to enable people return to their ancestral homes to continue their farming activities.

He said Benue, an agrarian state, has majority of its people living in rural areas, arguing that concentrating development in Makurdi and a few other towns is completely unacceptable and selective.

The PDP governorship candidate promised to prioritize local government autonomy to allow council chairmen have a free hand to operate, so that people living in rural communities can have sustained security, access to clean water and good rural roads.

He announced that his blueprint has mapped out programmes including enhanced security, pointing out that an attack during his administration on one local government would be considered an attack on all 23 local government areas to ensure that the people are defended.

Aondoakaa condemned what he described as gagging of the opposition by the present administration, arguing that whenever PDP is in power, the rule of law is practised and true democracy is observed.

He recalled that during the immediate past administration, the then Governor Samuel Ortom always allowed opposition to use public facilities such as the IBB Square and the Aper Aku Stadium, stating that what is happening currently is not democratic.

Also, the Senate Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro, congratulated members inaugurated into the Aondoakaa/Ogbenjuwa Campaign Council, led by Chief Laha Dzever, and pledged to mobilise support for the candidates across Benue South Senatorial District (Zone C).

He urged the campaign council to work assiduously for the victory of the party and expressed optimism that Aondoakaa would be a listening governor and not an emperor.

Responding on behalf of the campaign team, the Director-General of the council, Dr. Laha Dzever, promised that he and his team would do everything possible to lead the party to victory.

He urged the Benue people to support their candidates pledging that a PDP government would promote unity, fairness and inclusive development.

Tajikistan withdrew from International Criminal Court on day Putin visited
articles.summary:
Tajikistan has announced that it withdrew from the International Criminal Court (ICC) on the same day that Russian leader Vladimir Putin visited the country.

Source: Le Monde, as reported by European Pravda

Details: Tajikistan has published an official notice announcing its withdrawal from the Rome Statute, stating that the decision took effect on 20 November 2026 – the day of Putin's visit. ICC member states are required to arrest Putin if he enters their territory.

Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova, Russia's commissioner for children's rights, have been wanted by the ICC since 2023 for the unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children. The Kremlin leader visited Tajikistan on his way back from a summit with US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

In a statement, the ICC said it regrets Tajikistan's decision: "Decisions by States Parties to disengage from the Rome Statute risk undermining the collective pursuit of justice and weakening global efforts to end impunity. The ICC stands at the heart of the international system of accountability, and its effectiveness depends on sustained and unequivocal support from the international community."

Background:

In September 2023, the European Parliament called on the ICC to issue an arrest warrant against self-proclaimed Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko in connection with the deportation of Ukrainian children.

At the meeting in Shenzhen on 19 November, Trump urged Putin and Xi to join efforts to fight the ICC.

articles.title: German chancellor says 2008 decision not to admit Ukraine to NATO was a mistake

Quote: "Today, looking back, we can all see what a mistake it was not to support the American proposal at the 2008 NATO summit in Bucharest to admit Ukraine to NATO. If it had become a member of NATO, this war could probably have been prevented."

Details: Merz's statement comes as French President Emmanuel Macron proposes to reopen discussions on Ukraine joining NATO.

"In the current situation, given Russia's hardline stance, I think we need to reopen the question of Ukraine's accession to NATO," Macron said after the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin.

Merz called France's position "logical", saying it is consistent with the security guarantees Ukraine needs and is expected to receive after the war ends. These include the idea of providing Ukraine with guarantees similar to those in Article 5 of the NATO Treaty. The German chancellor said such security guarantees are "very close" to NATO membership.

"Frankly, I cannot imagine Ukraine's future without the security guarantees it urgently needs. And these are security guarantees not only for Ukraine, but for all of us," Merz said.

Former German chancellor Angela Merkel has repeatedly defended her decision to refuse Ukraine a Membership Action Plan in 2008. She has argued that if Ukraine had started moving towards NATO membership, the war would have begun much earlier.

Background:

On 21 November, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that the issue of NATO membership for Ukraine continues to be raised at meetings with allies, but the outcome will depend on the terms on which the war ends.

Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had privately told his Western counterparts that he doubts the war in Ukraine can be ended through negotiations and doubts Kyiv will be able to join NATO in the near future.

articles.title: Russians repeatedly changed date and cause of Ukrainian journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna's death in state registers
articles.summary:
Data on the death of Ukrainian journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna, who died in Russian captivity, was amended several times in the register of Russia's Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat), with a different date or cause of death given each time.

Source: an investigation by Russian media outlet Vazhnye Istorii (Important Stories), based on leaked Rosstat data provided to the journalists by the hacker groups Silent Crow and Cyber Partisans

Details: The journalists found one record in the Rosstat database concerning the death of a woman whose dates of birth and death exactly match those of Viktoriia Roshchyna. The cause of death was determined by a forensic medical examiner, while the death was registered by a specialised department of the Civil Registry Office of the Perm city administration.

The outlet noted that a week before her death, Viktoriia was transferred from pre-trial detention centre No. 2 in Taganrog to pre-trial detention centre No. 3 in the city of Kizel in Perm Krai.

The register entry relating to the journalist's death was amended several times. The data was first entered in the Rosstat database in late December 2024, giving 16 December 2024 as the date of death and listing the cause as unknown. However, the death certificate issued was final rather than an interim one.

A few days later, the Civil Registry Office sent Rosstat a correction changing the date of death to 19 September 2024. If this date is accurate, Viktoriia died six days before the prisoner exchange in which she had been promised a place.

Amendments continued to be made in 2025. In February, a Rosstat employee entered details from a new death certificate and changed the cause of death from "unknown" to "illness". According to the latest approved information in the database, the journalist died of myocardial dystrophy – changes in the heart muscle that led to a heart rhythm disorder and pulmonary oedema.

The record was last amended on 11 February 2025, three days before Viktoriia's body was brought back to Ukraine.

The investigative journalists noted that when the cause of death is unknown, an interim death certificate is usually issued first. In Viktoriia's case, however, the first certificate was final. It was later replaced with a new one "in place of the final certificate", specifying a particular cause of death. Fewer than 0.3% of all records in the Rosstat system are amended in this way.

It is even rarer for the date of death to be changed to an earlier one, with both the day and month altered: this occurs in approximately 0.1% of records.

Meanwhile, other identifying details – citizenship, address, place of birth, marital status, education and occupation – are not listed in the record. Nor are they recorded in entries for other Ukrainians who have died in Russian custody, including Oleksandr Markov, a 74-year-old pensioner from Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Viktor Demchenko, a 71-year-old resident of Donetsk Oblast, and prisoner of war Oleksandr Ishchenko.

The journalists said the Russian authorities registered the death of Polish citizen Krzysztof Galos in the same way. Galos was detained in Russian-occupied territory of Ukraine in 2023 and held at pre-trial detention centre No. 2 in Taganrog. In all the identified cases except Ishchenko's, where the cause of death could not be established due to decomposition of the tissue, the forensic medical examiners listed heart and vascular diseases as the cause of death.

The place of death for Roshchyna, Markov, Ishchenko and Galos is listed in the database as "other location", which is the usual designation for deaths that occur in pre-trial detention centres or during transfers. The Ukrainian forensic medical examiners who examined Viktoriia's body found signs of torture, evidence of extreme emaciation, and some internal organs missing.

Read more: The Viktoriia Project: the story of the captivity and torture endured by journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna and thousands of Ukrainians imprisoned by Russia

Background:

In March 2022, Russian occupying forces abducted journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna for the first time in the occupied city of Berdiansk, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, and held her captive for 10 days. She was released on 21 March after being forced to record a video saying she had no complaints against the Russian secret services.

In August 2023, Viktoriia travelled to temporarily occupied territory again to prepare a report. She went missing on 3 August.

In May 2024, Serhii Tomilenko, head of the National Union of Journalists of Ukraine, reported that Russia had for the first time acknowledged Viktoriia's unlawful detention. The journalist's father had received a letter dated 17 April from the Russian Defence Ministry stating that Viktoriia was being held in Russia.

On 10 October 2024, Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War reported Roshchyna's death in Russian captivity.

Investigative journalists from Slidstvo.Info found that Viktoriia had been brutally tortured with electric shocks and a knife at Russian pre-trial detention centre No. 2 in Taganrog. Due to extreme emaciation, she weighed around 30 kg (66 lb). Shortly before her death she was transferred to pre-trial detention centre No. 3 in Kizel. Ukrainska Pravda reported that when the occupying forces returned Viktoriia's body, it was labelled as that of an "unidentified male" and some internal organs were missing, including the brain, eyeballs and part of the trachea.

On 14 May 2025, the Verkhovna Rada (Ukrainian parliament) backed a request from 26 MPs to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that Viktoriia Roshchyna be posthumously awarded the title of Hero of Ukraine.

On 14 July 2026, Ukrainska Pravda published an open appeal by media professionals, human rights activists and public figures calling for Viktoriia to be awarded the title of Hero of Ukraine. At the end of the month, nearly 800 signatures were submitted to the President's Office.

On 15 October, the Verkhovna Rada voted by 255 votes to resubmit the request to the president to posthumously award Viktoriia the title of Hero of Ukraine.

On 28 October, Viktoriia was posthumously honoured with an OXI Courage Award in Washington.

Details: The Russian Foreign Ministry claimed that Estonia is "deliberately and purposefully providing its airspace" to Ukrainian forces so that they could fly their drones through Estonian territory.

"Estonia continues to actively support the Kyiv regime by covertly providing its airspace for Ukrainian drones to fly through in order to carry out attacks on north-western Russia," the ministry said.
